run's write call: the owner or a tool admin; a destructive one: a tool admin other than the owner; a workflow
approval: the approval's role). `403` when the caller may not decide it (`held[].canDecide` is false).

#### `/workflow` (B-4009)

`POST /api/conversations/:id/workflows` (`chat:write`, `agents:run`), body `{ "workflow": "<name or id>", "input": { … } }`
→ `202 Invocation` with `run.kind: "workflow-run"`. Its approvals show in `held` and are decided with the `held`
route above. The chain tree is `GET /api/chains/<run.chain>` (the Runs screen's chain view: `#/runs?chain=<id>`; check
`web/js/screens/runs.js` for the parameter it reads).

#### `+skill` (B-4005)

`PUT /api/conversations/:id/skills/:name` (`chat:write`), body `{ "mode": "sticky|once" }` → `{ "skills": [ … ] }` (the
list as in `invocations`). `DELETE /api/conversations/:id/skills/:name` → `{ "skills": [ … ] }`. A sticky skill's
instructions join the system prompt of every later turn until it is removed; a `once` skill applies to the next turn
and is then removed by the server. `404` when the skill is not offered in this conversation.

### Socket events (to the conversation owner's sockets)

- `chat.invocation` `{ conversationId, invocationId, kind, state, messageId }`: an invocation was created or changed.
  Reload `GET …/invocations` (and the conversation when a message changed state).
- `chat.skills` `{ conversationId }`: the active skills changed (a `once` skill was used).
- `run.step` `{ runId, n, lane, title, state, meta }` and `run.state` `{ runId, state, error }`: already sent for agent
  runs; match `runId` to `invocation.run.id` to stream steps into the run card.
- `workflow.run` `{ runId, workflowId, state, … }`, `workflow.step`, `workflow.approval`: already sent for workflow runs.

### Flags (B-4002)

A held tool call is a flag of kind `hold` with `checkpoint: "tool-call"`; `POST /api/flags/:ref/decide` with
`approved` or `rejected` runs or rejects it (the existing Flags screen's buttons). Its detail has
`held: { messageId: <invocation id>, state, content: <tool and arguments as JSON> }`.

## Sprint 36b (1.6.0): model thinking templates (B-11707)

A model in `GET /api/admin/models` has `thinking: { mode, recorded, template }`: `mode` is `native`, `template` or
`none`; `recorded` is false when nobody recorded it and the manifest's capabilities decide; `template` is
`{ id, name, system, open, close, startsOpen }` for a template model, else null (`problem` is added when a recorded
template is not one the server knows). `capabilities` contains `thinking` exactly when the mode in force says the
model thinks. A profile's `model` in `GET /api/admin/profiles` carries `thinking: { mode, recorded, template: { id, name } }`.

- `GET /api/admin/models/thinking-templates` (`models:read`) → the built-in templates,
  `[{ id, name, system, open, close, startsOpen }]`: `magistral` (`<think>` … `</think>`), `magistral-think-tokens`
  (`[THINK]` … `[/THINK]`), `think-tags` (no instruction: a model that reasons in `<think>` tags unprompted).
- `PATCH /api/admin/models/:id` (`models:manage`) also takes
  `thinking: { "mode": "native|template|none"|null, "template": "<built-in id>" | { "system": "…", "open": "<t>", "close": "</t>", "startsOpen": false } }`.
  `mode: null` forgets the record. `400` for `template` without a template, an unknown built-in, a template with
  another mode, tags that are equal, shorter than two characters or hold white space; `409` for an embedding model or
  a retired one. Audited as `model.updated`.
- `POST /api/admin/profiles` without `thinkDefault` and `thinkCeiling`, on a model whose entry records `native` or
  `template`: the profile starts at `medium` up to `high`. Given values are kept.
- `POST /api/admin/models/:id/evaluate`: the tool-calling test sends a system prompt; a template model's evaluation has
  a third test, `Thinking template`.

For a template model the gateway never sends the `think` option. When a request asks for thinking it puts the
template's instruction ahead of the system prompt (or adds a system message), and it always moves what the model
writes between the tags to `thinking` in the stream (`chat.chunk` `thinking`; `/v1` returns the answer only, as it
does for native thinking), dropping the tags and the white space after the closing tag.

## Sprint 41 (1.7.0): guardrail rules drafted from a description (B-9601, B-9602)

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/admin/guardrails/sets/:id/describe` | Drafts one rule from a description through a published profile (`guardrails:manage` and `inference:invoke`). Body `{description (3 to 2000 characters), profile, label? (default internal, within the caller's clearance)}` |
| `POST /api/admin/guardrails/sets/:id/describe/:draftId/save` | Adds the drafted rule to the set's draft, in shadow (`guardrails:manage`). No body is read |

What changed on existing routes:

| Method and path | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/guardrails/sets/:id` | Adds `described`: for each rule of the working version that a model drafted, `{byName, at, profile, enforceApproved}` |
| `POST /api/admin/guardrails/sets/:id/draft/publish` | `403` with `step: dual-control` and `rules` when the draft holds a described rule that enforces and no second guardrail admin approved such a version yet |
| `POST /api/admin/guardrails/sets/:id/draft/approve` | Also records the approval for the described rules that enforce in the approved version (`describedRulesEnforcing` in the audit entry) |

The draft: the description passes the `user-input` checkpoint (a redacting rule's redacted text is what the model
reads), the model is called through the profile as the caller, with the usage metered as `workflow`, and its answer
passes the `model-output` checkpoint. From the answer only `name`, `checkpoint`, `mechanism`, `action`, `severity` and
`description` are read. The server sets the id (the name as a slug, numbered when a rule of the set or of the platform
baseline has it), `stage: shadow`, `onError: closed`, `enabled: true` and the type. The mechanism must be `pattern`,
`pii`, `secrets`, `budget` or `allow-list`. The result is validated like any saved rule; `problems` lists what failed.
One open draft is kept per person and rule set, for seven days.

Audit: `guardrails.rule.drafted` (profile, whether valid, the rule id; not the description), `guardrails.rule.added`
with `described: true`, `guardrails.publish.refused`.

## Sprint 41 (1.7.0): Redis for multi-process installs (B-9001, B-9002)

No new routes.

| Method and path | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /readyz` | With `REDIS_URL` configured, adds `checks.redis`: `ok`, or `unavailable` while the bus's Redis does not answer (its subscriber connection down, or no PING answer within two seconds). Such an instance answers 503 until Redis answers again; the cause is logged, not returned. Without `REDIS_URL` there is no `redis` check |
| `GET /api/admin/overview` | An instance cut off from Redis shows `state: not ready` with `checks.redis: unavailable` from its next heartbeat |
| `com.atproto.label.subscribeLabels`, `com.atproto.sync.subscribeRepos` | Unchanged on the wire. Behind the bus the instance reads the newest seq from the database every `ATPROTO_STREAM_POLL_SECONDS`, so an event whose bus message was lost reaches its subscribers within one interval, in seq order and once |

A server process that is one of several on its database (`WORKERS_ENABLED=false`, `SERVER_REPLICAS` above 1, or
another instance's live heartbeat) refuses to start without `REDIS_URL` and exits with status 1 and the reason on
standard error: `exprsn-ai failed to start: REDIS_URL is required because …`. See `docs/deploy.md`, "Redis and more
than one process".

## Sprint 41 (1.7.0): workflows calling listed public hosts (B-9101, B-9102)

No new routes. An HTTP step's configuration (`kind: http` in a workflow graph) changed:

| Field | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `method` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, and now `PATCH` and `DELETE`. Every method but `GET` is a write: a step with a retry policy gets the warning "writes to another system; a retry may send it again", and a workflow published as a tool is `destructive` when it has a `DELETE` step |
| `url` | May name a public host when the tenant's list of allowed hosts (`PUT /api/admin/integrations/hosts`) names it or a network holding every address it resolves to. A parameter in the URL's own query string whose name says it carries a credential is refused |
| `query` | New, optional: `{name: value}`, at most 50, added to the URL percent-encoded. A value is a template or a vault reference `vault:path#key` |
| `headers` | As before (`Content-Type`, `Accept`, `Authorization`, `X-…`). A header whose name says it carries a credential (`X-Api-Key`, `X-Auth-Token`, …) takes `vault:path#key`, optionally after `Bearer `, `Basic ` or `Token `, as `Authorization` does |
| `body` | A field whose name says it carries a credential takes `{vault:path#key}` as its whole value (optionally after `Bearer `, `Basic ` or `Token `), in a JSON body or a form body. With `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` the secret is percent-encoded, otherwise it is escaped for a JSON string |

**Hosts.** A step's host is resolved once and the connection goes to the address that was checked. A host whose
addresses are all private is allowed as before: `WORKFLOW_HTTP_HOSTS` narrows it and the tenant's list narrows it
further when it has entries. A host whose addresses are all public needs the tenant's list. Cloud metadata,
link-local, unspecified and multicast addresses, loopback unless `WORKFLOW_HTTP_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`, and a name that
answers with both internal and public addresses are refused. Redirects are not followed: a `3xx` comes back as the
step's status. The list is read for every call. A refused step fails with the host named, for example
`api.partner.example is a public host that is not on this tenant's list of allowed hosts. A tenant admin adds it
under Registry, Allowed hosts.`

**Credentials.** `POST /api/workflows` (with a graph), `PUT /api/workflows/:id/draft`, `POST /api/workflows/:id/publish`
and `POST /api/workflows/import` answer `400` when an HTTP step holds a literal where a reference belongs, naming the
step and the header, parameter or field; `POST /api/workflows/:id/validate` and the workflow's `validation` list it
as an error of code `config`. A value shaped like a private key, a cloud access key, a provider token or a JWT is
refused whatever its name. Every reference is checked for the saver (`403`, step `vault-policy` or `role`) and read
at each run as the run's principal; the value is in the request only, never in the graph, the run, a step's output
or its detail (a step's detail lists the names of its `query` parameters, not their values). A bundle's
`references.vault` names the references of headers, query parameters and bodies, and `bindings.vault` rebinds them.
A version published before 1.7.0 with a literal in an `X-` header still runs; saving or publishing it again is
refused.

## Sprint 41 (1.7.0): held messages, group posts, comments and edits (B-9401 to B-9404)

A write the `user-input` guardrail holds (`require-approval` in enforce) is no longer refused with `422`. It is stored
sealed and waits, read by its sender only. A `block` verdict still refuses. Migration `057_held_writes`.

| Write | Held answer | Where it waits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/messaging/conversations/:id/messages` | `202`, the message with `state: held` and `held` | Its own row, state `held` |
| `PATCH /api/messaging/messages/:id` | `202`, the message as everyone reads it, with `pendingEdit: {id, state, reason, body}` | `held_writes` |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/posts` | `202`, the post with `state: held` and `held` | Its own row |
| `POST /api/feed/posts/:id/comments` | `202`, the comment with `state: held` and `held` | Its own row |
| `PATCH /api/feed/posts/:id` (body) | `202`, the post as everyone reads it, with `held: {kind: feed-post-edit, body}` | `held_writes` |
| `POST /api/feed/posts` | `202` as since 1.4.0; `held.reason` is `unavailable` when no rule could decide | Its own row |

`held` is `{id, kind, state, reason, note, since}`. `reason` is `review` (a rule asked for a reviewer; a hold flag is
in the review queue, source kind `held-write`) or `unavailable` (every rule that held it is a model-backed rule that
could not run; no flag is filed). The sender's lists return their own held and rejected items; nobody else's lists,
counts, searches, notifications, socket events or exports carry them. One author has at most `HELD_MAX_PER_AUTHOR`
waiting and a tenant at most `HELD_OUTAGE_MAX_PER_TENANT` waiting on an unavailable check; past either the answer is
`422` with `step: held-queue-full`. A second edit of a message or post whose edit waits is `409`.

**The sender.** `GET /api/me/held` lists what of theirs waits or was rejected (`authenticated`).
`POST /api/me/held/:id/withdraw` takes back what still waits: it is removed and its flag closed (`rejected`, with a
`withdrawn` event). `DELETE` on a held or rejected message, group post or comment does the same for that object.

**The reviewer** (`flags:review` or `moderation:review`; never the sender; within their workspaces, and for a direct
conversation anyone holding the permission).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/moderation/held?state=&reason=` | `{items, summary}`: held items, oldest first (`state` defaults to `held`; `all` for every state) |
| `GET /api/moderation/held/summary` | `{review, unavailable, oldestUnavailableAt, limits}` |
| `GET /api/moderation/held/:id` | The item with its `text` and `context: {place, items}` (what was written before it); text above the reviewer's clearance is withheld |
| `POST /api/moderation/held/:id/decide` `{decision: accept or reject, reason?}` | Through the hold flag. Accept delivers it once, with its original time, and notifies as a new write would; reject tells the sender. `409` when it was decided already, or when it waits on an unavailable check |
| `POST /api/moderation/held/rescreen` | Screens again, now, what waits on an unavailable check: `{delivered, rejected, review, waiting, expired}` |

`POST /api/flags/:ref/decide` with `approved` or `rejected` decides a `held-write` flag the same way, and
`GET /api/flags/:ref` shows the held text as `held.content`.

**The re-screen job** `moderation.held.rescreen` runs every `HELD_RESCREEN_SECONDS` for tenants with something
waiting on an unavailable check. It screens each item again as its sender. A pass delivers it (redacted text is
stored redacted), a block refuses it and tells the sender, a rule that now asks for a reviewer files the flag, and a
check that still cannot run leaves it and the rest of the tenant's items for the next round. After
`HELD_OUTAGE_EXPIRE_HOURS` without a verdict an item is refused. `moderation.held.purge` deletes decided items
`HELD_KEEP_DAYS` after their decision.

**Socket events.** A delivered message raises `conversation.message.created` with `released: true` to every member,
the sender included. `conversation.message.held` `{messageId, heldId, kind, state}` goes to the sender's sockets only,
when their message or edit is rejected or withdrawn. A delivered comment or group post raises `feed.comment.created`
or `group.post.created` with `released: true`.

**Audit.** `moderation.held.created`, `.delivered`, `.rejected`, `.withdrawn`, `.review` and `.rescreened`, and
`messaging.message.held`, `messaging.message.edit.held`, `group.post.held`, `feed.comment.held` and
`feed.post.edit.held`, all without the text.

## Sprint 41 (1.7.0): evidence retention and legal hold (B-9501 to B-9504)

**Takedown (B-9501).** A file a moderation decision took down is its own state: `GET /api/files/:id` and every other
file route answer `404`, `GET /api/files/trash` does not list it, `POST /api/files/trash/restore` answers `409`
(`step: takedown`, audited `file.restore.refused`) and `POST /api/files/trash/empty` leaves it (audited
`file.purge.refused`). Reversing the action, or an upheld appeal, lifts it.

**Evidence retention (B-9502).** An object a moderation action hid is kept while its case is open: its flag is
undecided, an appeal of the action waits, or the last decision in the case is younger than
`MODERATION_EVIDENCE_DAYS`. Purges leave it and write `retention.skipped` once per object, purge path and case.
`DELETE /api/conversations/:id`, `DELETE /api/messaging/messages/:id`, `DELETE /api/knowledge/documents/:id`
and the record delete routes answer `409` with `step: retention` for a kept object (audited
`retention.delete.refused`).

**File retention and version cap (B-9503).**

| Route | Permission | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PUT /api/admin/tenants/:tid/workspaces/:wid/file-retention` | `tenant:manage` | `{ retentionDays, versionCap }`, each a whole number of 1 or more, or null. Audited `file.retention.updated` |
| `GET /api/files/usage` | `files:read` | now also `retention: { retentionDays, versionCap, lastRunAt }` |

The `files.purge` job applies them on its schedule: a file unchanged for `retentionDays` goes to the trash
(`file.retention.trashed`), and of each file the newest `versionCap` versions stay, always the current one
(`file.versions.pruned`). Files under a hold are left alone.

**Legal hold on a case or an object (B-9504).** `POST /api/compliance/holds` takes, beside `user` and `workspace`:

- `{ scope: "case", scopeId, reason, approverId }`: `scopeId` is the flag's id or its reference (`F-12`).
- `{ scope: "object", objectType, objectId, reason, approverId }`: a moderated object by its registry type and id.

`GET /api/compliance/holds` also returns `objectTypes`, `evidenceDays` and `evidenceExports`.

| Route | Permission | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/compliance/holds/:id/exports` | `compliance:manage` | `{ reason, approverId }`: asks to export what an active hold of scope `case` or `object` keeps; the approver is another holder |
| `POST /api/compliance/evidence-exports/:id/decide` | `compliance:manage` | `{ decision: approved or rejected, note }`; not by the requester (`403`, `step: dual-control`) |
| `POST /api/compliance/evidence-exports/:id/withdraw` | `compliance:manage` | the requester, while pending |
| `GET /api/compliance/evidence-exports/:id/download` | `compliance:manage` | the requester only: JSON Lines with the hold, the flag, the actions, the appeals and each object |

`POST /api/admin/tenants/:tid/offboard` answers `409` (`step: legal-hold`) while the tenant has an active legal hold.

**Audit.** `file.restore.refused`, `file.purge.refused`, `file.retention.updated`, `file.retention.trashed`,
`file.versions.pruned`, `retention.skipped`, `retention.delete.refused`, `evidence.export.requested`, `.approved`,
`.rejected`, `.withdrawn`, `.downloaded` and `evidence.exported`.

## Sprint 41 (1.7.0): the vault's platform scope and named keys (B-9201 to B-9205)

The digests and signatures the server keys itself (session ids, CSRF tokens, API-key and SCIM token digests, recovery
and emailed codes, DAV and PDS app passwords, PDS session tokens, file, share and form links, media URLs, calendar
feed signatures, OIDC values, channel session tokens) use named HMAC keys in the vault's platform scope instead of
`SESSION_SECRET`. Version 1 of each key is the `SESSION_SECRET` in use when the scope was first opened.

### Platform scope (`platform:manage`)

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/platform/vault/keys` | `{ scope, status, keys }`: each key's `name`, `path` (`sys/transit/<name>`), `service`, `uses`, `latestVersion`, `minVersion`, `loaded`, `refused` and `versions` (`version`, `createdAt`, `accepted`). Never any key material |
| `POST /api/admin/platform/vault/keys/:name/rotate` | A new version, with a recent sign-in. New digests and signatures use it; earlier versions stay accepted. Audited `vault.transit.key.rotated` (`scope: sys`) |
| `POST /api/admin/platform/vault/keys/:name/retire` | `{ minVersion }`: what versions below it issued is refused from now on. `400` when above the latest version. Audited `vault.transit.key.configured` |
| `GET /api/admin/platform/vault/policies` | The scope's grants |
| `POST /api/admin/platform/vault/policies` | `{ service, path, capabilities, effect }`: `path` is `*`, `sys` or a path under it. A `deny` of `sign` or `verify` closes a key to its service (its features answer `503`) |
| `DELETE /api/admin/platform/vault/policies/:id` | |
| `GET /api/admin/platform/vault/explain?service=&path=&capability=` | The decision and the grants that bear on it |

The keys and their services: `session` (`identity.sessions`), `api-key` (`identity.api-keys`), `mfa`
(`identity.mfa`), `app-password` (`identity.app-passwords`), `pds` (`atproto.pds`), `link` (`links`), `feed`
(`groups.calendar`), `federation` (`federation.oidc`), `channel` (`channels`), `identifier` (`identifiers`).

A tenant's vault routes never reach this scope: `GET /api/vault/transit/keys` lists the tenant's keys only, a
grant with a `sys/` path or the subject kind `service` answers `400`.

### Transit: `hmac-sha256`

`POST /api/vault/transit/keys` takes `type: "hmac-sha256"`. `sign` answers `exai:v<n>:<base64>` (HMAC-SHA-256 of the
input under version n); `verify` recomputes under the version the signature names, so signatures of the previous
version verify until `minDecryptVersion` passes it (`400` then). Such a key does not encrypt.

### Start-up and the hot path

A server opens the scope before it serves a request. The steps, in order: `configuration`, `database`, `kms`,
`data-keys`, `vault-system-scope`, `sessions-and-api-keys`, `authentication`. A failing step ends the process with
`exprsn-ai failed to start: at step <name> (n of 7): <reason>`. A process that continues with the scope closed
answers every request under `/api` with `503` (`title: Vault unavailable`, `step: vault-system-scope`).

Settings: `VAULT_SYS_REFRESH_SECONDS` (60) and `VAULT_LEASE_CACHE_MS` (1000).

**Audit.** `vault.transit.key.created`, `.rotated` and `.configured` with `scope: sys`; `vault.sys.used` (one entry
per service and minute: `uses`, `from`, `to`); `vault.denied` for a service a policy refuses; `vault.lease.issued`,
`.renewed`, `.revoked`, `.expired` and `.revoke-failed` for the generic leases (issued by the API-key leases below).

## Sprint 41 (1.7.0): dynamic API-key leases (B-9301, B-9302)

A role names a scope set and a lifetime. Reading its credential path issues a fresh API key under a lease; the key
is in that answer only, and it stops when the lease ends. The built-in provider `exprsn` issues this server's own
keys. An outside provider is registered per tenant; `github` (GitHub App installation tokens) is the one kind this
server has. A tenant with no registered provider has no outside provider, and nothing is called.

All routes are under `/api`. Providers and roles need `secrets:admin`; roles, creds and leases need `secrets:read`
and, for a lease, the vault policy's `read` on `apikey/<provider>/<role>`.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /vault/apikey/providers` | `{providers, kinds}`: `exprsn` first, then the tenant's providers (`name, kind, endpoint, label, config, credentialRef, configured, state, roles, liveLeases`); `kinds` lists what this server can talk to and what each needs |
| `POST /vault/apikey/providers` `{name, kind, endpoint?, label?, config, credentialRef}` | Registers an outside provider (`201`). `credentialRef` is a `vault:path#key` reference the caller may read; it is read later as them. For `github`: `config: {appId, installationId}`, the credential is the App private key (PEM), `endpoint` defaults to `https://api.github.com` |
| `PATCH /vault/apikey/providers/{provider}` `{endpoint?, label?, config?, credentialRef?, state?}` | Changes it; `state: disabled` stops it issuing |
| `DELETE /vault/apikey/providers/{provider}` | Removes it and its roles (`204`); `409` while it has live leases |
| `PUT /vault/apikey/providers/{provider}/roles/{role}` `{scopes, config?, ttlSeconds?, maxTtlSeconds?}` | Saves a role. For `exprsn`, `scopes` are permissions; for `github`, `<permission>:<read\|write\|admin>` and `config: {repositories?}` |
| `DELETE /vault/apikey/providers/{provider}/roles/{role}` | Removes a role (`204`); leases already issued run to their end |
| `GET /vault/apikey/roles` | The roles the caller's policy lets them list or read, with `canIssue`, `path` and `reference` |
| `POST /vault/apikey/creds/{provider}/{role}` `{ttlSeconds?}` | Issues a lease (`201`): the lease view plus `key`, `leaseDurationSeconds` and `renewable` |
| `GET /vault/apikey/leases` `?all=1&provider=&state=&limit=` | The caller's leases; `all=1` needs `secrets:admin` |
| `GET /vault/apikey/leases/{id}` | One lease (the key is never in it) |
| `POST /vault/apikey/leases/{id}/renew` | Moves the expiry by the lease's period, never past its maximum; `410` once it has ended or lapsed, `409` at the maximum |
| `POST /vault/apikey/leases/{id}/revoke` | Ends it now; `502` with the lease in `revoking` when its provider refuses the revoke (retried by the sweeper) |

- **An `exprsn` key** belongs to the reader and carries the role's scopes that the reader holds and that the
  request's own credential carries; `409` (`step: apikey-lease-scopes`) when that is none. It is accepted only
  while its lease is live, and like every API key it is intersected with its owner's roles on each request.
- **Refusals.** `403` `step: vault-policy` without the grant; `403` `step: apikey-lease-chain` when the request was
  made with a leased key; `429` `step: apikey-lease-limit` past `VAULT_APIKEY_LEASES_MAX` (20) live leases of one role
  for one person; `409` `step: apikey-provider-unconfigured` for a provider without its credential; `409`
  `step: egress` when the provider's address is not allowed (a public host must be on the tenant's list of allowed
  hosts); `502` `step: apikey-provider` when the provider refuses or does not answer.
- **Lifetimes.** `ttlSeconds` is the renew period (the lease lapses when it is not renewed within it),
  `maxTtlSeconds` the absolute life; they default to `VAULT_LEASE_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS` and
  `VAULT_LEASE_MAX_TTL_SECONDS`. A GitHub token lives an hour, and its lease never longer.
- **References.** `vault:apikey:<provider>/<role>#key` is accepted where an HTTP tool or a workflow HTTP step takes
  a vault reference. It is checked at save against the saver's policy and resolved at use as them; every read issues
  a fresh key and a new lease.
- **Audit.** `vault.apikey.provider.registered`, `.updated` and `.removed`, `vault.apikey.role.saved` and `.removed`,
  `vault.apikey.lease.issued` (never the key), and the `vault.lease.*` entries of the lease itself.


## Sprint 42 (1.7.0): groups: profile fields, search and paging, notifications (B-9703, B-9704, B-9708)

Migration `062_group_profiles_notices`. Everything stays inside the caller's workspaces and clearance, as in Sprint 27c.

### Profile fields and the member limit (B-9703)

A group or channel view carries `tags` (an array), `website`, `memberLimit`, `full` (where the view has a member
count), and `avatar` and `banner` (`null`, or `{state: scanning | ready | rejected | gone | not an image, url}` with
`url` only once the image is released and the viewer clears the file's label). They are shown to whoever may know the
group exists, like its name.

| Route | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/groups` and `PATCH /api/groups/:id` | Also take `tags?` (up to 10, each up to 30 characters; stored trimmed, lower case, without duplicates), `website?` (an `http(s)` address without credentials, up to 300 characters, or `null`) and `memberLimit?` (1 to 100,000, or `null` for none). Tags and the website pass the `user-input` guardrail (`422`, `step: guardrails` on a block; a redaction is stored redacted). A website that is not one is `422`, `step: website`. Lowering the limit below the present count removes nobody |
| `PUT /api/groups/:id/avatar` | Owner, and `files:write`. The raw image is the body (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, at most 2 MiB; `415`, `413`). It is uploaded into the file store of the group's workspace at the group's label and through its quarantine: `202` with the group, `avatar.state: scanning` |
| `DELETE /api/groups/:id/avatar` | Owner. The group no longer shows it; the file stays in the file store |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/avatar` | Whoever may know the group, once the pinned version passed its scan and the viewer clears the file's label; otherwise `404`. Served with the sandbox headers, `no-store` |
| `PUT /api/groups/:id/banner` | Owner, and `files:write`. As the avatar, at most 5 MiB |
| `DELETE /api/groups/:id/banner` | Owner |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/banner` | As the avatar |

At its member limit a group answers `409` (`title: Group full`, `step: member-limit`, `limit`) to
`POST /api/groups/:id/join` (in an open group and, in a request group, before any request is made),
`POST /api/groups/:id/invites` and `POST /api/group-requests/:id/accept` (the request or invitation stays pending).
The last place is taken under a lock on the group's row.

### Search and paging (B-9704)

`GET /api/groups`, `GET /api/groups/:id/members` and `GET /api/calendar/events/:id/attendees` take `q` (a search,
up to 100 characters), and `limit` (1 to 200) with `cursor`. Without `limit` and `cursor` each answers the array it
always did. With either, the answer is `{items, next, total}`: `next` is the cursor of the next page or `null`, and
`total` counts every match. Pages are cut by keyset, so a row that joins or leaves between two requests neither
repeats nor skips the others. A cursor this server did not make is `400`.

| Route | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups?q=&limit=&cursor=` | `q` matches the name or a tag. Pages are in code-point order of the name, then the id (with `near`, by distance, then the id) |
| `GET /api/groups/discover?q=` | `q` narrows the candidates by name or tag before they are ranked |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/members?q=&role=&limit=&cursor=` | `q` matches the user name or the display name; `role` keeps one role. Oldest membership first, then the user id |
| `GET /api/calendar/events/:id/attendees?q=&response=&limit=&cursor=` | `q` as for members; `response` keeps one answer. Pages are in the order of the first answer, then the user id; the unpaged list stays by display name |

### Notifications (B-9708)

| Notification `kind` | Sent to | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event.created` | The group's members who are still let in (active, in the workspace by membership, cleared), except the creator | A new event |
| `event.rescheduled` | The attendees (going or maybe) who can read the event now, except whoever moved it; also by email | The start, end, time zone or all-day flag changed. Once per change: `group_event_notices` holds one row per event and sequence |
| `event.notice` | The same attendees, except the sender; also by email | "Notify attendees" |
| `group.role` | The member | Their role was changed by someone else |
| `group.member` | The removed member; the group's owners and moderators | A removal; someone joined (an open join or an accepted invitation) or left |

No notification carries an event's sealed title or an organiser's message.

| Route | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `PATCH /api/calendar/events/:id` | Also answers `notified` (how many attendees were told) when the time changed |
| `POST /api/calendar/events/:id/notify` `{message}` | Moderators (the events right). Up to 1,000 characters, screened at `user-input` (`422`, `step: guardrails`; a redaction is stored redacted), kept sealed with the event. `201 {id, eventId, kind: message, message, notified, createdBy, createdAt}`. At most 5 in 24 hours for one event (`429` with `Retry-After`) |
| `GET /api/calendar/events/:id/notices` | Readers of the event. The last 100, newest first: `[{id, eventId, kind: rescheduled \| message, message, notified, createdBy, createdAt}]` |

Audit: `group.avatar.set`, `group.avatar.removed`, `group.banner.set`, `group.banner.removed`,
`group.event.notice.sent`; `group.event.updated` carries `attendeesNotified` when the time changed, and
`group.updated` the member limit before and after.

## Sprint 42 (1.7.0): group roles and permission flags; event extras (B-9705, B-9707)

Migration `065_group_roles_event_extras`. `groups:read` to read and `groups:write` to change; what a caller may do is
decided by the rights of their role in the group.

### Roles (B-9705)

The rights: `read`, `post`, `rsvp`, `invite`, `decide`, `remove-members`, `moderate`, `events`, `check-in`, `cases`,
`channels`, `settings`, `roles`, `delete`. The tiers: `owner` (all), `admin` (all but `delete`), `moderator` (up to
`channels`), `member` (`read`, `post`, `rsvp`), `guest` (`read`, `rsvp`).

| Route | Needs | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/roles` | read the group | `{tiers: [{role, rights}], rights: [{right, label, custom}], custom: [{id, name, rights, members}], mine, canManage}` |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/roles` | `roles` | `{name, rights}`: a custom role. 403 `step: group-role` for a right the caller lacks, 400 for `delete`, 409 for a taken name or the twenty-first role |
| `PATCH /api/groups/:id/roles/:roleId` | `roles` | `{name?, rights?}`. 403 `step: self-grant` when the caller holds the role, `group-role` when it carries a right they lack |
| `DELETE /api/groups/:id/roles/:roleId` | `roles` | Removes it; its holders stay as members. `{removed, members}` |
| `PATCH /api/groups/:id/members/:userId` | `roles` | `{role}` (a tier) or `{customRoleId}`. 403 `step: group-role` when the member holds, or the new role carries, a right the caller lacks; `self-grant` when it would raise the caller; 409 for the last owner |

`GET /api/groups/:id` carries `rights` (the caller's) and `customRole`; a member in `GET /api/groups/:id/members`
carries `customRole` (`{id, name}` or null) beside `role`, which is `member` for a holder of a custom role.

### Event extras (B-9707)

`POST /api/groups/:id/events` and `PATCH /api/calendar/events/:id` also take `kind` (`in-person`, `virtual`,
`hybrid`), `virtualUrl` (an http or https address; 422 `step: virtual-url`, or `guardrails`), `visibility` (`group`,
`members`, `organisers`), `rsvpDeadline` (ISO 8601, not after the end; null clears it), `rsvpApproval` and `waitlist`.
`draft: true` on create keeps the event a draft (`state: draft`): only holders of `events` read it, and nothing is
announced or scheduled. An event's record carries the same fields, `attendance.waitlisted` and `attendance.pending`,
and `myRsvp.response` may be `waitlisted` (with `position`) or `pending`.

| Route | Needs | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/calendar/events/:id/publish` | `events` | Publishes a draft: reminders are scheduled and the members who may read it are told. 409 when it is not a draft |
| `POST /api/calendar/events/:id/rsvp` | as before | `going` may answer `response: pending` (approval required) or `waitlisted` with `position` (full, with a waitlist). 409 `step: rsvp-deadline` after the deadline, except for `declined`. `promoted` counts who took a place this answer freed |
| `POST /api/calendar/events/:id/rsvps/:userId/decide` | `events` | `{decision: approve or decline}` for an answer that is `pending`: `going`, `waitlisted` when full with a waitlist, 409 when full without one, or `declined`. 422 `step: attendee` when the person may no longer attend; 403 for one's own answer |
| `GET /api/calendar/events/:id/attendees` | read the event | `response` may also be `waitlisted` or `pending`; those rows are shown to holders of `events` only, with `queuedAt` |
| `POST /api/calendar/events/:id/cancel` | `events` | A draft is discarded without a notice |

## Sprint 42 (1.7.0): group moderators act on cases; a group's linked conversation (B-9706, B-9709)

Migration `064_group_cases_conversations`. `groups:read` to read and `groups:write` to change; what a caller may do is
decided by their role in the group. `:ref` is a flag's id or its reference (`F-12`), or an appeal's (`A-3`).

### Cases (B-9706)

A case is a flag on the group, one of its posts or one of its events. The caller needs the `cases` right (owners and
moderators) in the group the content is in; the list of a group includes the channels in which they have it. Anything
else answers 404, as does a case above the caller's clearance.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/cases` | `?state=`. `[{id, ref, kind, state, severity, objectType, objectId, label, ruleName, dueAt, createdAt, groupId, groupName, assignee, assigneeName, hideable}]` |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/cases/:ref` | The flag as a reviewer sees it, with `excerpt`, plus `groupId`, `groupName`, `assigneeName`, `object: {type, id, state, ownerId, ownerName, hideable}`, `own` (the caller's own content) and `actions: [{id, action, by, byName, userId, userName, moderationActionId, banId, note, at}]` |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/cases/:ref/moderators` | `[{userId, name}]`: who the case may be assigned to |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/cases/:ref/act` | `{action: confirm \| dismiss \| hide \| warn \| suspend \| ban, note?, days?}`. Answers the case as above. `warn` needs `note`; `suspend` needs `days`. 403 `step: independence` for one's own content; 409 `step: assignee` when it is assigned to another moderator and the caller is not an owner; 409 for a hold flag; the bans' own answers for `suspend` and `ban` |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/cases/:ref/assign` | `{userId: id \| null}`. An open case goes to an owner or moderator cleared for it (422 `step: assignee` otherwise), never to its author (403) |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/appeals` | `?state=`. Appeals of actions on the group's content, each with `groupId`, `groupName` and `decidable` |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/appeals/:ref` | One appeal with its `statement` |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/appeals/:ref/review` | Takes it for review. 403 `step: independence` for the appellant and for whoever took the decision |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/appeals/:ref/decide` | `{decision: upheld \| denied, note?}`. `{appeal, effects, groupId, groupName}`; upheld restores the object and reopens the flag |

### Linked conversation (B-9709)

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/conversation` | `{linked: false, canLink}` or `{linked: true, conversationId, label, title, member, linkedBy, linkedAt, canLink}`. Only members (and managers) are told of a link |
| `PUT /api/groups/:id/conversation` | Owners. `{}` or `{label?}` makes a conversation named after the group; `{conversationId, removeOthers?}` links one the caller owns, in the group's workspace. 201 with the view. 409 when the group has one already or the conversation is another group's; 409 `step: members` with `outside` when people in it are not in the group and `removeOthers` is not true; 422 `step: label-floor` when its label is below the group's; 422 `step: members` above `MESSAGING_MAX_MEMBERS` |
| `DELETE /api/groups/:id/conversation` | Owners. `{linked: false, conversationId}`: the conversation stays, with the group's roles written into it |

Changed: a conversation's view carries `groupId` (null unless linked). For a linked conversation `POST`, `PATCH` and
`DELETE /api/messaging/conversations/:id/members[/:userId]` answer 409 `step: group-link` with `group`; the caller's
`role` is the one their group role gives (owner, admin for a moderator, member); `PATCH /api/groups/:id` answers 422
`step: label-floor` when it would raise the group's label above its conversation's.

## Sprint 43 (1.7.0): groups as access subjects, the response cache, did:exprsn, plugin UI surfaces (B-98, B-99, B-113, B-112)

Migrations `069_group_access_subjects`, `070_response_cache`, `071_user_dids`, `072_plugin_surfaces`.

### Groups as access subjects (B-98)

A social group counts for a person while they have a member row, their account is active, the group (and, for a
channel, its parent) is not deleted, no ban or suspension of theirs stands in it, they are cleared for its label and
they belong to its workspace (`groups/subjects.ts`). It is read at every decision: leaving, a ban or a suspension ends
what the group was granted at once. A grant never lifts anyone above their clearance or the object's label.

| Route | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/members?departed=1` | B-9801. Members whose account is no longer active are left out of the list; with `departed=1` a holder of `groups:manage` sees them too, each with `departed: true` |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/claim-ownership` | B-9801. A holder of `groups:manage` becomes owner of a group with no active owner (joining it when not a member): `{id, owner, joined}`. 409 while it has an active owner; 403 step `permission` otherwise. Audited `group.ownership.claimed`. The sweep `groups.ownerless` (every `GROUPS_OWNERLESS_MINUTES`, 15) tells the managers of a newly ownerless group once (`group.ownerless`) |
| `GET /api/files/:id/group-grants`, `GET /api/files/folders/:id/group-grants` | B-9802. The social groups a file or a folder is granted to: `[{id, fileId, folderId, groupId, groupName, createdBy, createdAt}]` |
| `POST /api/files/:id/group-grants`, `POST /api/files/folders/:id/group-grants` | `{groupId}`. 201 the grant. Takes the right to change the file (or membership of the folder's workspace); the group's workspace ceiling must admit the file's label (403 step `zone`); 409 when already granted. Audited `file.group-grant.created` |
| `DELETE /api/files/group-grants/:grantId` | 204. Audited `file.group-grant.revoked` |

A grant gives read only. A folder's grant covers every file below it, in its subfolders too. `GET /api/files/shared`
lists files read through a group with `sharedVia: 'social_group'`, `groupId` and, through a folder, `viaFolder`.

- **Vault (B-9803).** `subjectKind: 'social_group'` with the group's id in `POST /api/vault/policies` (400 when no live
  group has it). Deny wins as for every subject. `POST /api/vault/policies/explain` lists the caller's
  `subjects.socialGroups` and names them in `socialGroupNames: {id: name}`.
- **Knowledge (B-9804).** `POST /api/knowledge/bases/:id/access` takes `kind: 'social_group'` (`read` or `manage`); the
  access list names the group.
- **Apps (B-9805).** `POST /api/apps` and `PATCH /api/apps/:app` take `groupId` (null to clear); `PUT
  /api/apps/:app/entities/:entity/group` `{groupId}` scopes one entity's records. Only someone holding the group's
  `roles` right (or `groups:manage`) scopes data to it (403 step `group-role`). A group-scoped app is visible, and a
  group-scoped entity's records are listed, read and written, only for the group's members (and holders of
  `tenant:manage`), designers included. Row and field policies take the subject `{kind: 'group_role', value}`: the
  reader's tier (`owner`, `moderator`, `member`, ...) or custom role name in the scoping group. App and entity views
  carry `groupId`. Audited `app.entity.scoped`.

### Response cache (B-99)

A profile opts in with `cacheTtlSeconds` (null or 0: off; at most 30 days) and `cacheLenient` on `POST` and `PATCH
/api/admin/profiles`. A chat or `/v1` turn whose answer is in the cache is answered without the model: it passed the
user-input checkpoint at send and passes the output check again, is metered with no model tokens (`cache_hit` on its
usage row) and audited (`chat.cache.hit`, `api.chat.cache.hit`); `chat.status` says `cached: true`. Not cached
unless the profile is lenient: tools, attachments, a temperature above zero (or none set). `/v1` never caches a
request with tools or `X-Exprsn-Knowledge`/`X-Exprsn-Memory` context.

| Route | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cache/responses?days=7` | `tenant:manage` or `platform:manage`. `{profiles: [{profileId, profile, ttlSeconds, entries, storedHits, turns, hits, hitRate, days}]}` for the caller's tenant |
| `POST /api/admin/cache/responses/purge` | `{profileId?, entryId?}` (neither: the whole tenant). `{removed, profiles}`. Audited `chat.cache.purged` |

### `did:exprsn` (B-113)

| Route | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/me/atproto/exprsn-did` | `atproto:link`, a browser session. `[{did, method: 'exprsn', curve, publicKeyMultibase, alsoKnownAs, createdAt, document}]`: the caller's own `did:exprsn`, minted (a key made in the signer or OpenBao) the first time; `alsoKnownAs` names their hosted PDS DID. Audited `atproto.user-did.minted` |
| `GET /xrpc/com.exprsn.identity.resolveDid?did=` | Public. `{did, didDoc}` for a `did:exprsn` or `did:key` (offline), `did:plc` or `did:web`; 400 `DidNotFound` |

### Plugin UI surfaces (B-112)

A manifest's `ui` lists declarative surfaces (`docs/decisions/plugin-ui-surfaces.md`): `{id, slot: settings | record |
conversation | file | dashboard, title, description?, app?, entity?, capabilities, data: {id: {api, with}}, actions:
{id: {api, with}}, blocks: [{type: text|kv|table|action, ...}]}`.

| Route | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/plugins/:id/surfaces` | `plugins:manage`. `[{id, slot, title, description, capabilities, missingGrants, approved, approvedBy, approvedAt, enabled}]` |
| `PUT /api/admin/plugins/:id/surfaces/:surface` | `{approve?, enabled?}`. Approving takes every capability the surface declares granted (409 naming the missing ones) and enables it. Audited `plugin.surface.approved`, `.unapproved`, `.enabled`, `.disabled` |
| `GET /api/plugin-surfaces?slot=&app=&entity=` | Signed in. The approved, enabled surfaces of enabled plugins for the slot: `[{plugin: {id, key, name}, id, slot, title, description, blocks, data: [ids], actions: {id: {api}}}]` |
| `POST /api/plugin-surfaces/:plugin/:surface/data/:call`, `.../actions/:call` | `{context: {record?, app?, entity?, conversation?, file?}}`. Runs the declared call as the viewer: the plugin must hold its capability (403 step `capability`), the viewer the route's permission; their clearance is capped at the plugin's max label. 404 for a surface that is not approved and enabled, or a call it does not declare. An action is audited `plugin.surface.action` |

### Cross-posting (B-114)

Migration `073_feed_crosspost`. The B-11401 runbook (public host, wildcard DNS, PLC, relay, AppView) is in
`docs/deploy.md`, "The PDS on the public network".

| Route | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/me/crosspost` | `feed:read`. `{enabled, account: {did, handle, state} \| null, ready}`: the author's choice, and whether they have an active account on this server's PDS |
| `PUT /api/me/crosspost` | `feed:write`. `{enabled}`. 409 when turning it on without an active PDS account. Audited `feed.crosspost.enabled`, `.disabled` |
| `GET /api/feed/posts/:id/crosspost` | `feed:read`, the post's author. `{state: none \| skipped \| written \| deleted \| failed, uri, reason, error, updatedAt}` |

A post goes to the author's repo when it is published, its visibility is `public`, its label is `public`, it has text
of its own, the author has opted in and their PDS account is active. Audited `feed.crosspost.written`, `.updated`,
`.deleted`; a takedown emits `!takedown` on the record's at-uri and a restore negates it.

## Sprint 42 (1.7.0): sessions and keys as leases; signing keys and third-party credentials in the vault (B-9206 to B-9208)

### Sessions and API keys as leases (B-9206)

No route changes. With `CREDENTIAL_STORE=leases` the session cookie's value starts `l1.` and a new API key is
`exai_k2_<prefix>_<secret>`; the lists of sessions and keys show both kinds, and a key's `prefix` shows its form.

### Signing keys (B-9207)

`secrets:read` to list, `secrets:admin` and a recent sign-in to change; the vault's path policy then decides: `list`
on a key's path to see it, `manage` on `transit/signing/<domain>` to rotate.

| Route | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/vault/signing-keys` | `{custody: signer \| openbao \| null, keys: [{id, domain, name, path, keyType, backend: signer \| openbao \| sealed, isolated, state, createdAt, rotatable, registeredBy, registeredAt}], unregistered: {<domain>: n}}`. `custody` is where a held key would be made here |
| `POST /api/vault/signing-keys/register` | `{domains?}`. `{registered, keys}`. Registers what the domains hold and the vault does not know; creates, moves and rotates nothing. Idempotent |
| `POST /api/vault/signing-keys/:id/rotate` | `{immediate?}` (OIDC). `201 {rotated, next, keys}`. `409` for a key that is not the one signing now, or a domain that is not rotated here (`oidc` and `webhook` are). `403` without `manage` |
| `DELETE /api/vault/signing-keys/:id` | `204`. The registration goes; the key stays and goes on signing |
| `GET /api/admin/platform/vault/signing-keys`, `POST .../register`, `DELETE .../:id` | The same for the platform's own keys (issuers of no tenant, the ACME account key), with `platform:manage` |
| `POST /api/vault/transit/keys` | Also takes `custody: sealed \| held`. `held` (types `ed25519`, `ecdsa-p256`) makes the key in the signer process or OpenBao transit; `409 step: key-custody` when neither is configured. A key's view carries `custody: sealed \| signer \| openbao` |

### Credential moves (B-9208)

`secrets:admin`; the two that change something need a recent sign-in.

| Route | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/vault/credential-moves` | `{kinds: [{kind, title, path, service, sealed, moved, references, external}], remaining}`. Counts only |
| `POST /api/vault/credential-moves` | `{kinds?, limit?}`. `{moved: [{kind, id, field, path}], failed: [{kind, id, field, error}], remaining}`. Run again while `remaining` is not 0 |
| `POST /api/vault/credential-moves/restore` | `{kinds?}`. `{restored: [{kind, id, field}]}`. The integrations read their sealed values again |

Kinds: `webhook`, `mcp-server`, `mcp-oauth-client`, `connection`, `moderation-provider`, `channel`, `knowledge-source`.

## Sprint 42 (1.7.0): vault reference owners; group bans, invite links and messages (B-9209, B-9701, B-9702)

Migration `063_reference_owners_group_bans`.

### Reference owners (B-9209)

A saved `vault:<path>#<key>` reference resolves as the person who saved it. One such reference of one person can be
handed to a workspace or to a service; it then resolves under that owner's path policy and no longer depends on the
person. All three routes need `secrets:admin`.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/vault/reference-owners` | `{owners: [{id, savedBy, savedByName, savedByActive, ref, owner: {kind: workspace \| service, id, name}, clearance, createdBy, createdAt}]}` |
| `PUT /api/vault/reference-owners` | `{savedBy, ref, owner: {kind, id}}`. A workspace by id; a service named `integration.<name>`. `400` for a reference that takes an API-key lease or an unknown person or workspace; `403` when the caller cannot read the reference; `404` when the secret does not exist; `409` (`step: vault-policy`, `path`) when the owner holds no `read` on the path. Saving it again replaces the owner |
| `DELETE /api/vault/reference-owners/:id` | `204`. The reference resolves as the person again |

`POST /api/vault/policies` accepts `subjectKind: service` in a tenant for a subject named `integration.<name>`.
Audit: `vault.reference.owner.set`, `vault.reference.owner.removed`.

### Bans and suspensions (B-9701)

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/bans` | Moderators. The standing ones, or with `state=all` every one: `[{id, groupId, userId, userName, kind: ban \| suspend, state: active \| lifted \| ended, reason, createdBy, createdByName, createdAt, expiresAt, liftedBy, liftedAt}]` |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/bans` | Moderators (an owner for a moderator). `{userId, kind, days?, reason?}`. A suspension needs `days` (at most 365) and a member; a ban without `days` stands until lifted and may name someone who is not a member. `409` for an owner, and when one stands already; `422` when the guardrail refuses the reason |
| `DELETE /api/groups/:id/bans/:banId` | Moderators. Lifts it |

While one stands, in the group or for a channel in its group, `POST /api/groups/:id/join`, accepting an invitation
and redeeming an invite link answer `403` (`step: ban`, `kind`, `until`), and inviting the person or accepting their
request answers `409` (`step: ban`, `ban`). `GET /api/groups/:id` carries `standing: {kind, until} | null` for the
caller. Audit: `group.ban.created`, `group.ban.lifted`.

### Invite links and messages (B-9702)

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/invite-links` | Moderators. `[{id, groupId, hint, maxUses, uses, remaining, expiresAt, state: active \| used \| expired \| revoked, createdBy, createdAt, revokedAt}]`; never a code |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/invite-links` | Moderators. `{maxUses?: 1..10000 \| null, expiresInDays?: 1..365}` (default: `GROUP_INVITE_DAYS`). `201` with the view plus `code` and `url`, shown this once. At most 50 links in use per group |
| `DELETE /api/groups/:id/invite-links/:linkId` | Moderators. Withdraws it |
| `POST /api/group-invites/lookup` | `{code}`. `{group: {id, name, label, parentId?, parentName?}, state, expiresAt, remaining, member}`. `404` for a wrong code and for anyone outside the group's workspace or below its label |
| `POST /api/group-invites/redeem` | `{code}`. `{joined: true, role: member, groupId, groupName}`. `410` (`step: invite-link`, `state`) when the link expired, was withdrawn or is used up; `403` (`step: ban` or `parent`); `409` when already a member or the group is full (`step: member-limit`), which takes no place on the link |

A code is read in any case, with or without separators. Lookups and redemptions are limited to 20 a minute per person
(`429`). `POST /api/groups/:id/join` takes `{message?}` and `POST /api/groups/:id/invites` takes `message` beside
`userId` and `role`: up to 500 characters, `422` (`step: guardrails`, `field: message`) when the guardrail blocks or
holds it. Request views carry `message` for the group's moderators and the person concerned. Audit:
`group.invite-link.created`, `group.invite-link.revoked`; `group.member.joined` carries `via: invite-link` and the
link.

## Sprint 54 (1.9.0, Unreleased): the store wizard, archive and restore, store backups (B-181, B-185, B-186)

Every route needs `identity:manage`; a kind the registry marks `platform` (Exprsn platform accounts) also needs
`platform:manage` (`403`, `step: role`). Routes marked *recent* need a browser session with a recent sign-in (`401`
with `step_up: true` otherwise). Store views (`GET /api/admin/identity-providers` and the others) now carry `state`
(`active` or `archived`), `stateBefore` and `archivedAt`. Migrations `140_identity_store_state` and
`141_identity_store_backups`; without them versions report `available: false`, archive answers `503`
(`reason: migration_pending`) and saving a backup answers `503`, while creating stores and downloading a backup work.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/identity-store-kinds` | `{kinds: [{kind, title, description?, signIn: password \| redirect \| push, platform, sections: [{id, title, step: connection \| attributes, description?, fields: [{key, label, type: text \| url \| number \| boolean \| select \| multiselect \| list \| secret, required, help?, placeholder?, advanced?, default?, options?, min?, max?, pattern?, accepts?}]}], presets: [{id, title, description?, config, mappings?}]}], archive, backups}`: the forms generated from each kind's zod schema |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-store-kinds/{kind}/check` `{config, step?}` | `{ok, errors: [{path, message}], config}`: the configuration with its defaults when valid; with `step`, only that step's fields count |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-store-kinds/{kind}/test` `{config, credentials?: {username, password?}}` | `{ok, result: connected \| unreachable \| ok \| found \| not_found \| invalid \| disabled \| error, steps, user?, detail?}`. Nothing is saved; the password is used once and never stored or audited; failures count toward the account's lockout (`429` when locked). Audited `identity.store.wizard_tested` (the username only) |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers` (changed) | Also takes `reason` (kept with version 1) and `test: {username, password?}`: "test before save", `409` (`reason: test_failed`, `result`, `steps`) when the store cannot connect or find the account |
| `PATCH /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}` (changed) | Also takes `reason`; each change is a version. `409` for an archived store's name, configuration or enabling |
| `PUT /api/admin/identity-providers/order` `{ids, reason?}` | Every store of the tenant once, first asked first; positions become 10, 20, … Audited `identity.provider.reordered` |
| `GET /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/versions` | `{available, versions: [{version, name, kind, position, enabled, config, reason, createdBy, createdAt, changes: [{path, before, after}]}]}`, newest first |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/archive` `{revokeSessions?, revokeApiKeys?, reason?}` *recent* | `{store, users, sessionsRevoked, apiKeysRevoked}`. `409` for the local store, a store managed by the configuration file, the only enabled store, or one already archived. Audited `identity.store.archived` |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/restore` `{to?: previous \| disabled, reason?}` *recent* | `{store, users, mappings}`; `409` when not archived. Audited `identity.store.restored` |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/backups` `{save?}` | Without `save`: the archive as the response (`Content-Disposition: attachment`), audited `identity.store.backup.downloaded`. With `save: true`: `201 {id, createdAt, bytes, sha256, counts}`, kept in the blob store, audited `identity.store.backup.created` |
| `GET /api/admin/identity-store-backups` | `{available, backups: [{id, providerId, providerName, kind, bytes, sha256, counts, createdBy, createdAt}]}` |
| `GET /api/admin/identity-store-backups/{id}/download` | The saved archive (checked against its digest). Audited `identity.store.backup.downloaded` |
| `DELETE /api/admin/identity-store-backups/{id}` | `204`. Audited `identity.store.backup.deleted` |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-store-backups/restore` `{archive \| backupId, mode?: same \| new, name?, dryRun?}` *recent* | The signature is verified first (`422`, `reason: signature \| seal \| digest \| format`, audited `identity.store.backup.refused`). `{dryRun, backup: {id, createdAt, source}, target: {id, name, kind, created}, changes: [{what, action: create \| update \| unchanged \| skip, detail}], summary, warnings}`. `dryRun` defaults to true. Audited `identity.store.backup.restore_previewed` or `.restored` |

The archive (`exprsn-store-backup/1`): `{format, id, createdAt, source: {tenant: {id, slug}, store: {id, name, kind}},
counts, key, sealed: {cipher: aes-256-gcm, wrappedKey, data, sha256}, signature}`; the payload inside `sealed` is
described in `docs/identity.md`.

## Sprint QA-1 (1.9.9-qa, Unreleased): store governance (Sprint 54 leftovers, B-181, B-185, B-186)

Dual control on store changes and restores, purge after a retention period, scheduled backups, the CSV export of a
store's users and the raw upload of a large backup (`identity/store-governance.ts`,
`routes/admin/identity-store-governance.ts`; `docs/identity.md` "Store governance"). Every route needs
`identity:manage` (a platform store also `platform:manage`); *recent* as above. Migration
`142_identity_store_governance`; without it these routes answer `503` (`reason: migration_pending`), except the upload
(which needs `141` only), and `PATCH`, restore and `DELETE` of stores behave as in 1.9.0. A proposal is
`{id, tenantId, kind: store.config | store.restore | store.purge | settings, providerId, name, payload, summary, state:
pending | approved | rejected | withdrawn | superseded, proposedBy, proposedAt, decidedBy, decidedAt, note, mine, changes}`
(`changes`: the configuration diff of a `store.config` proposal; payloads hold secret references and backup ids only).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/identity-store-governance` | `{available, settings: {dualControl: auto \| on \| off, purgeAfterDays, updatedBy, updatedAt}, dualControl: {available, mode, on, identityAdmins, warning}, backups, uploadMaxBytes, exportInlineMax}` |
| `PUT /api/admin/identity-store-governance` `{dualControl?, purgeAfterDays?, reason?}` *recent* | `{settings, dualControl, proposal}`; `202` with a `settings` proposal when it would turn dual control off while it is in force. Audited `identity.store.settings.updated` |
| `PATCH /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}` (changed) | Under dual control a `config` that differs from the saved one is not applied: `202` with the store (name, order and enabled applied) and `proposal` (`store.config`). `409` (`reason: proposal_pending`) while one waits |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-store-backups/restore` (changed) | With `dryRun: false` under dual control: `202` with the dry run and `proposal` (`store.restore`); an inline archive is kept as an uploaded backup first |
| `DELETE /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}` (changed) | With migration 142: as the purge route (`204` when purged at once) |
| `GET /api/admin/identity-store-proposals` `?state=&providerId=` | Proposals, newest first |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-store-proposals/{id}/approve` `{note?}` *recent* | `{proposal, result}`: applies it. `403` (`step: dual-control`) for the proposer; `409` when decided, `reason: stale` when the store's configuration changed since (the proposal is superseded). Audited `identity.store.proposal.approved` and the applied change |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-store-proposals/{id}/reject` `{note?}` | Another admin; the proposer withdraws instead (`409`). Audited `identity.store.proposal.rejected` |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-store-proposals/{id}/withdraw` | The proposer only (`403`). Audited `identity.store.proposal.withdrawn` |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/purge` `{reason?}` *recent* | An archived store past `purgeAfterDays`: `{purged, links, mappings, versions}`, or `202 {proposal}` under dual control. `409` with `reason: not_archived \| retention`, `purgeableAt`, `purgeAfterDays`. Audited `identity.store.purged` |
| `GET /api/admin/identity-store-backup-schedules` | `{available, schedules: [{providerId, frequency, keepCount, keepDays, enabled, nextRunAt, lastRunAt, lastStatus, lastError, lastBackupId, failures, updatedAt}]}` |
| `GET /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/backup-schedule` | `{available, schedule}` (null when none) |
| `PUT /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/backup-schedule` `{frequency: daily \| weekly, keepCount?, keepDays?, enabled?}` | The schedule; `keepCount` defaults to 7 when neither is given. Audited `identity.store.backup.schedule.updated` |
| `DELETE /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/backup-schedule` | `204`; saved backups are kept. Audited `identity.store.backup.schedule.removed` |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/backup-schedule/run` | `202 {jobId}`: one scheduled run now (job `identity.store.backup.run`) |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/users-export` `{job?}` (also `users:manage`) | `text/csv` (`username, display_name, email, state, groups, last_sign_in`; `X-Rows`, `X-Omitted`: accounts above your clearance left out), or `202 {jobId, accounts}` above 1,000 accounts or with `job: true`. Audited `identity.store.users.exported` or `.export_requested` |
| `GET /api/admin/identity-store-exports/{jobId}` (also `users:manage`) | The finished job's CSV, for its requester only (`404` otherwise, `409` while it runs). Audited `identity.store.users.exported` |
| `PUT /api/admin/identity-store-backups/upload` | The raw backup file (any content type, at most 50 MB: `413`), streamed to the blob store and checked (`422` as for restore, nothing kept). `201 {id, archiveId, createdAt, bytes, sha256, counts, source}`; restore it by `backupId`. Audited `identity.store.backup.uploaded` |

Saved backups (`GET /api/admin/identity-store-backups`) now carry `origin`: `manual`, `schedule` or `upload`. Jobs:
`identity.store.backups.due` (queued every 15 minutes per tenant with a due schedule), `identity.store.backup.run`,
`identity.store.users.export`.

## Sprint 54 (1.9.0, Unreleased): Active Directory, cloud directory presets, Exprsn platform accounts (B-182 to B-184)

No new admin routes and no migration: the kinds `ad` and `exprsn-platform` and the presets are entries in the kind
registry (`GET /api/admin/identity-store-kinds` lists them; `identity/providers/store-kinds.ts`), saved and tested with
the store routes above. See `docs/identity.md`.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers`, `PATCH /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}` (changed) | `kind` may be `ad` or `exprsn-platform` (the latter also needs `platform:manage`). An `ad` configuration with a plain `ldap://` URL without StartTLS is refused (`400`, `config.urls.<n>`). An `oidc` store's `directory` (`msgraph` or `google`) and an `exprsn-platform` store's `platformUrl` pass the service URL checks: `400` with `reason: service_url` for a metadata address, or a public one under `SERVICE_INTERNAL_ONLY`. Directory and platform credentials take `vault:` references only |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/test` (changed) | An `ad` store: domain controllers (DNS SRV or URLs), TLS, the service bind and the base. An `oidc` store with a directory: discovery, the directory grant and a first page of users and groups. An `exprsn-platform` store: the address checks, the authorization server answers, the client secret resolves |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}/sync` (changed) | Also for an `oidc` store with a directory (users looked up by their directory id) and for `ad` (by objectGUID) |
| `POST /api/auth/login` (changed) | An Active Directory account whose password has expired or must change, or whose account has expired, gets `403` with `reason: password_expired \| must_change \| account_expired` and the reason in words, after the right password only; locked and disabled accounts get the usual `401` (the audit's `auth.login.failed` carries `refusal`) |
| `GET /api/auth/sign-in-options` (changed) | Lists `exprsn-platform` stores with `protocol: exprsn-platform` and their start address |
| `GET /federation/exprsn-platform/start?provider=<id>&return=?` (public; `/t/<tenant>/…` for other tenants) | `302` to the platform's authorize endpoint with `state` and PKCE S256, setting the `exai_fed` browser binding; `502` page when the store is unknown, disabled or archived |
| Any `/api` or `/v1` route (changed: authentication) | 1.9.0 (B-184): `Authorization: Bearer <platform CA token>` (the platform CA's full signed token object as base64url JSON, `eyJ…` without dots) is accepted when an active `exprsn-platform` store with `acceptApiTokens` matches its CA domain and trust anchor. `X-Exprsn-Tenant: <slug>` names the tenant when several match. The person is the account linked through that store; permissions are its roles narrowed by the store's `scopeMap`; no CSRF token; step-up and browser-only routes answer `403` (`step: credential`). Refusals: `401` problem+json with `error: invalid_token` or `tenant_ambiguous` and `reason`, `503` `platform_unavailable`; `429` after 20 failed credentials a minute. See `docs/identity.md` |
| `POST /api/admin/identity-providers`, `PATCH /api/admin/identity-providers/{id}` (changed, B-184) | An `exprsn-platform` configuration takes `acceptApiTokens` (default false), `tokenIssuer`, `tokenTrustAnchor` (PEM bundle with a CA certificate), `tokenJwksUrl`, `tokenValidateUrl`, `tokenServiceId`, `tokenServiceToken` (`vault:` only), `apiAudience`, `scopeMap` (`<bit>=<permission> …`, permissions checked), `tokenCacheSeconds` (0 to 300); `400` when opted in without them. `tokenValidateUrl` and `tokenJwksUrl` pass the service URL checks |

## Sprint 55 (1.9.0, Unreleased): CA settings, CA tokens and member certificates (B-187 to B-189, B-195)

`pki/settings.ts` (`s.pkiSettings`), `pki/tokens.ts` (`s.caTokens`), `pki/members.ts` (`s.memberCerts`), routes
`routes/pki-settings.ts`, `routes/ca-tokens.ts`, `routes/member-certs.ts` (mounted before `routes/pki.ts`), the public
key list in `routes/pki-public.ts`. Migrations `127_pki_settings` and `128_ca_tokens`; until they run, settings are
the environment's (saving answers `409`, `step: settings-table`) and tokens report `configured: false` (`409`,
`step: tokens-table`). Errors are problem details; refusals by range or floor are `422` with `step: settings` and
`key`. See `docs/pki.md`.

### Settings (`pki:manage`; the platform scope also `platform:manage` and a recent sign-in)

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/pki/settings` | `{configured, canPlatform, platform: [view], tenant: [view], proposals, issuers: {root, intermediate}, keys}`; a view is `{key, group, label, range, value, source: tenant \| platform \| environment \| default, env, envValue, floor: {value, source} \| null, saved, scopes, dual, applies}`. `proposals` (pending) only for platform admins; `issuers` are the keys, validity and path lengths in force |
| `PUT /api/pki/settings` `{scope: platform \| tenant, values?, reset?: [key], reason?}` | Values are checked against their ranges, floors and the rules between settings (`422`). Root and intermediate keys (subject, key algorithm, validity, path length) become one proposal; the rest apply at once. `{applied: [key], proposal, settings}`. Audited `pki.settings.updated`, `pki.settings.proposed`. Two saves at once: `409` (`step: settings-version`) |
| `GET /api/pki/settings/proposals?state=pending\|applied\|rejected\|withdrawn\|all` | `platform:manage`. `{proposals: [{id, scope, changes, state, reason, proposedBy, proposedAt, decidedBy, decidedAt, note}]}` |
| `POST /api/pki/settings/proposals/{id}/approve` `{note?}` | `platform:manage`, a recent sign-in, never the proposer (`403`, `step: dual-control`). The values are checked again and saved; they apply at the next rotation (subject, algorithm) or re-issue (validity, path length). Audited `pki.settings.approved` |
| `POST /api/pki/settings/proposals/{id}/reject` `{note?}` | `platform:manage`. Rejected, or withdrawn by its proposer. Audited `pki.settings.rejected`, `pki.settings.withdrawn` |

Keys: `root.subject`, `root.days`, `root.keyType`, `root.pathLen`, `intermediate.subject`, `intermediate.days`,
`intermediate.keyType`, `intermediate.pathLen`, `leaf.subject`, `profiles.subject`, `crl.intervalMinutes`,
`crl.validityHours`, `crl.nextUpdateDays`, `ocsp.validityMinutes`, `ocsp.cacheSeconds`, `ocsp.delegated`,
`ocsp.responderDays`, `ocsp.responderKeyType`, `ocsp.batch`, `ocsp.maxBatch`, `acme.termsUrl`, `acme.certDays`,
`acme.privateIdentifiers`, `acme.issuerId`, `publicUrl`, `ratePerMinute`, `tokens.maxBytes`, `tokens.signature`,
`tokens.defaultExpiry`, `tokens.defaultTtlMinutes`, `tokens.defaultUses`, `tokens.rotationDays`, `members.enabled`,
`members.profileId`, `members.withToken`, `members.renewDays`, `members.signIn`, `members.mtls`, `members.san`. The key
algorithms are `ecdsa-p256`, `ecdsa-p384`, `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072` and `rsa-4096`; `POST /api/pki/issuers` takes the
same, and without `keyType` or `days` (and on rotate and re-issue without `days`) the settings apply.

### CA tokens and tickets

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/pki/tokens?state=&kind=&subject=&limit=` | `pki:manage`. `{configured, tokens: [token], signers, permissions, resourceTypes, ticketMaxMinutes, defaults}`; a token is `{id, kind, resource: {type, id}, permissions, action, subject, label, expiry, expiresAt, maxUses, usesLeft, size, state, revokedAt, revokedReason, replacedBy, refreshedFrom, signerId, createdBy, createdAt, lastUsedAt}`, never the token text |
| `POST /api/pki/tokens` `{resource: {type: url \| did \| cid, id}, permissions: [read \| write \| append \| delete \| admin], expiry?: {kind: time \| uses \| persistent, ttlMinutes?, uses?}, subject?, label?}` | `pki:manage`. `201` with the token once (`token`, a compact JWS). Defaults from the settings; larger than `tokens.maxBytes` is `422` (`step: size`). Audited `pki.token.issued` |
| `POST /api/pki/tickets` `{resource, permissions, action, ttlMinutes? (1 to 1440, default 15), subject?, label?}` | `pki:manage`. A one-time ticket for one action. Audited `pki.token.ticket.issued` |
| `GET /api/pki/tokens/{id}` | `pki:manage`. One token |
| `POST /api/pki/tokens/{id}/revoke` `{reason?}` | `pki:manage`. Audited `pki.token.revoked` |
| `POST /api/pki/tokens/revoke` `{ids? \| subject? \| resource? \| signerId? \| all?, reason?}` | `pki:manage`. Bulk revoke (a URL resource covers the paths below it). `{revoked}`. Audited `pki.token.revoked.bulk` |
| `POST /api/pki/tokens/signers/rotate` | `pki:manage`. A new token signer now; the old one is retired and keeps verifying. Audited `pki.token.signer.rotated` |
| `POST /api/pki/tokens/validate` `{token, resource?, permission?, action?, spend?}` | `pki:tokens`. `{active, reason?, token?, usesLeft?}`; reasons `malformed`, `unknown`, `expired`, `spent`, `revoked` (or the revocation reason), `replaced`, `signer-revoked`, `signer-expired`, `bad-signature`, `resource`, `permission`, `action`. A use-limited token spends one use (unless `spend: false`), a ticket always; audited `pki.token.used`, `pki.token.ticket.redeemed` |
| `POST /api/pki/tokens/introspect` `{token}` | `pki:tokens`. RFC 7662-style `{active, jti, token_type, iss, sub, iat, exp, resource, permissions, action, uses_left, max_uses, expiry, signer}`; spends nothing |
| `POST /api/pki/tokens/refresh` `{token}` | `pki:tokens`. `201` with a new token (same binding, a fresh lifetime, the uses left); the old one is `replaced`. Not for tickets (`409`). Audited `pki.token.refreshed` |
| `GET /pki/tokens/{tenant}/keys` | Public (the CA's per-address limit). `{keys: [{kid, alg, state, notAfter, x5c, x5t#S256}]}`: each live signer's certificate chain, base64 DER |

### Member certificates

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/me/certificates` | Signed in. `{configured, enabled, signIn, mtls, certificates: [{id, certificateId, state, keyWaiting, tokenWaiting, hasToken, pickedUpAt, renewedFrom, createdAt, revokedAt, certificate}]}` |
| `POST /api/me/certificates/{id}/pickup` `{password}` | A browser session with a recent sign-in. `{pkcs12 (base64), token, serial, notAfter}` once: the key made at join in a PKCS#12 file under this password, and the CA token if one came with it; `409` after that. Audited `pki.member.picked_up` |
| `GET /api/pki/members` | `pki:manage`. The tenant's member certificates |
| `POST /api/pki/members/sweep` | `pki:manage`. Issue what joins missed, renew what is due, revoke for people who left, now. Audited `pki.member.sweep` |
| `POST /api/auth/certificate` `{}` | Public, behind the sign-in limit. Signs in with the member certificate a trusted proxy forwarded (`PKI_CLIENT_CERT_HEADER`, `PKI_CLIENT_CERT_VERIFY_HEADER: SUCCESS`, from a `PKI_CLIENT_CERT_PROXIES` peer); the tenant must allow it (`members.signIn`). The answer is the session body of `POST /api/auth/login`; the tenant's second-factor rules apply. Audited `auth.login` with `target.method: certificate` |

mTLS for the API (`members.mtls`): a request with no session or bearer that carries `X-Client-Cert-Auth: 1` and a
forwarded member certificate is authenticated as its member (`401`, `step: client-certificate`, when the certificate
is refused). CLI: `exprsn-ai pki:settings show | set <key>=<value>… | reset <key>… | proposals [--tenant <slug> |
--platform]`.

## Sprint 55 (1.9.0, Unreleased): leaked-password lists, checks against them and tenant deny words (B-192 to B-195)

Migration `131_leaked_password_lists` (not registered yet: until it is, every list route answers `installed: false`
or `503` with `reason: migration_pending`, and checks behave exactly as `BREACHED_*` says). Code: `identity/leaked/`
(`hashes.ts` formats and digests, `store.ts` staging, building and reading, `bloom.ts`, `mirror.ts`, `service.ts`
`s.leakedPasswords`), `identity/deny-words.ts` (`s.passwordDenyWords`), `routes/admin/leaked-passwords.ts`,
`cli/passwords.ts`; console `web/js/screens/platform-leaked.js` (Platform › Leaked passwords).

Platform lists need `platform:manage`; the tenant's own lists, its settings and the report need `identity:manage`
(the Identity admin and Tenant admin roles). The tenant is always the caller's. A list's `scope` is `platform` or
`tenant`; its `hashKind` (`sha1` or `ntlm`) is fixed when it is made.

| Route | Permission | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/leaked-passwords/lists?scope=platform\|tenant` | `platform:manage` or `identity:manage` (the scope's) | `{installed, scope, lists: [{id, scope, name, description, hashKind, source, enabled, activeVersion, latestVersion, activeEntries, versions, createdAt, updatedAt}], platformLists?}`; `platformLists` (tenant scope) is how many platform lists apply, without naming them |
| `POST /api/admin/leaked-passwords/lists` `{scope, name, description?, hashKind?}` | as above | `201` with the list. A name is unique in its scope (`409`). Audited `passwords.list.created` |
| `GET /api/admin/leaked-passwords/lists/{id}` | as above | The list with `versions: [{version, state: staging \| queued \| building \| mirroring \| ready \| failed, format, source, note, activate, linesRead, invalid, duplicates, entries, bytes, bloom: {bits, hashes, falsePositiveRate}, prefixLength, mirror: {cursor, total} \| null, jobId, error, createdAt, builtAt}]` |
| `PATCH /api/admin/leaked-passwords/lists/{id}` `{enabled?, description?}` | as above | A list turned off is not checked. Audited `passwords.list.updated` |
| `DELETE /api/admin/leaked-passwords/lists/{id}` | as above | The list, its versions and their blobs (`409` while a version is building). Audited `passwords.list.deleted` |
| `PUT /api/admin/leaked-passwords/lists/{id}/upload?format=hibp\|hashes\|plain&note=&activate=true\|false` (raw `text/plain` or `application/octet-stream` body) | as above | Streams the body (never read whole; at most `LEAKED_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES`, `413`), parses it to binary digests (a plain-text line is hashed and dropped at once) into a new version, and queues the job `passwords.list.build`. `202` `{version, jobId, lines, invalid, invalidLines (line numbers only), digests}`. Audited `passwords.list.uploaded`; the job audits `passwords.list.built` (and `passwords.list.activated` when `activate`) or `passwords.list.failed` |
| `POST /api/admin/leaked-passwords/lists/{id}/mirror` `{note?, activate?}` | `platform:manage` | A platform list only (`400` otherwise): fetches the whole Pwned Passwords corpus from `BREACHED_HIBP_URL` through its range API (16^5 prefixes at `LEAKED_MIRROR_RPS`) into a new version, as the job `passwords.list.mirror`. Called again while a mirror is stopped or failed, it resumes that version from its cursor. `202` `{version, jobId}`. Audited `passwords.list.mirror.started` / `passwords.list.mirror.resumed` |
| `POST /api/admin/leaked-passwords/lists/{id}/versions/{version}/activate` | `platform:manage` or `identity:manage` | Makes a built version the active one: replacing, or rolling back (`409` unless `ready`). Audited `passwords.list.activated` with `previous` and `rollback` |
| `DELETE /api/admin/leaked-passwords/lists/{id}/versions/{version}` | as above | An inactive version and its blobs (`409` for the active one or one being built). Audited `passwords.list.version.deleted` |
| `GET /api/admin/leaked-passwords/settings` | `identity:manage` | `{installed, signinAction: warn \| require_change \| block, failMode: open \| closed, denyWords, denyTermList, updatedAt}`. Defaults: `require_change`, `open`, none |
