| `PUT /api/admin/leaked-passwords/settings` `{signinAction?, failMode?, denyWords? (at most 200, 1 to 64 characters each), denyTermList? (a guardrail term list id, or null)}` | `identity:manage` | Saves them (words differing only in case are kept once). Audited `passwords.settings.updated` with what changed |
| `GET /api/admin/leaked-passwords/report` | `identity:manage` | `{checked, flagged, changed, accounts: [{userId, username, displayName, flaggedAt, action, changedAt}]}`: accounts whose password was found on a list at sign-in, and whether it was changed since |

What the checks answer (`s.leakedPasswords.check(tenantId, password)`, called by the one password pipeline,
`SigninPolicies.checkNewPassword`, after the policy and the deny words): `{found: true, action: block, message}`,
`{found: false, action: accept}`, or `{unavailable: true, action: accept | block, reason}`, by the tenant's fail
mode. Never which list, how often, or a count. `s.leakedPasswords.atSignIn(tenantId, userId, password)` answers the
tenant's `signinAction` for a password found on a list version added since the account was last checked; the pipeline
refuses (`block`, `403` `reason: leaked`) or asks for a change (`require_change`, the `password` stage). Audited
`password.leaked.signin`; the person gets a security notice. `s.passwordDenyWords.check(tenantId, password)`
answers `{found, term?}`; the pipeline refuses with `400` `reason: deny_word` naming the word.

## Sprint 55 (1.9.0, Unreleased): the tenant sign-in policy and OAuth client settings (B-190, B-191)

Migrations `129_signin_policy` (`signin_policies`, `password_history`) and `130_oidc_client_settings`
(`oidc_client_settings`, `oidc_refresh_families`). Until they run, every route below answers with today's values
(`available: false`) and saving answers 503. Audited `identity.policy.*` and `oidc.client.settings.*`.

### Sign-in policy (`identity:manage`)

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /admin/signin-policy` | `{available, policy, updatedBy, updatedAt, effective, bounds, warnings, oauth: {available, stored, effective, bounds}}`. `policy` is what the tenant set (null: none); `effective` is what is in force, with `sources` per value (`platform floor`, `platform`, `tenant`, `default`) |
| `PUT /admin/signin-policy` | Saves the policy (below); values outside `bounds` answer 400. Returns the view with `warnings` (forced expiry, character rules). Audited `identity.policy.updated` with before and after |
| `DELETE /admin/signin-policy` | Removes it (and the password history it kept): the platform's values apply. Audited `identity.policy.reset` |
| `PUT /admin/signin-policy/oauth` | The tenant's OAuth defaults (below). Audited `oidc.client.settings.defaults_updated` |

The policy, every field optional (left out: the platform's value or the default):

```json
{
  "password": { "minLength": 14, "maxLength": 128, "requireLower": false, "requireUpper": false, "requireDigit": false,
                "requireSymbol": false, "notSimilarToPrevious": true, "history": 5, "expiryDays": 0 },
  "lockout": { "maxAttempts": 5, "windowMinutes": 15, "durationMinutes": 15 },
  "sessions": { "idleMinutes": 20, "absoluteHours": 8, "stepUpSeconds": 120 },
  "mfaMethods": ["totp", "passkey", "email"]
}
```

`minLength` is never below 12. `lockout.maxAttempts`, `sessions.idleMinutes`, `sessions.absoluteHours` and
`sessions.stepUpSeconds` are at most the platform's `LOCKOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, `SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES`,
`SESSION_ABSOLUTE_HOURS` and `STEPUP_WINDOW_SECONDS`. `history` is 0 to 24, `expiryDays` 0 to 730.

The OAuth defaults: `{codeTtl (10 to 600 s, default 60), accessTtl (60 to 1800 s, for new clients, default 600),
refreshTtl (300 s to 90 days, for new clients, default 8 h), pkce: all | public (default), ratePerMinute (1 to
100,000 or null, default null), rotation: rotate (default) | reuse}`.

### What applies to a person (`users:manage`)

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /admin/users/:id/signin-policy` | `{user, configured, password: {managedHere, stores, mustChange, setAt, expiresAt, rules}, lockout, sessions, mfa: {required, why, enrolBy, allowed, enrolled, notAllowed}, sources}` |

### OIDC client settings (`identity:manage`)

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /admin/federation/oidc/clients/:id/settings` | `{clientId, name, type, confidential, dynamic, refreshGrant, stored, effective, bounds, reusedFamilies}`. `effective`: `codeTtl`, `accessTtl`, `refreshTtl`, `pkceRequired`, `consent` (`tenant`, `on`, `off`), `ratePerMinute`, `rotation`, with `sources` (`client`, `tenant`, `default`). `reusedFamilies`: grants revoked because a rotated refresh token came back |
| `PUT /admin/federation/oidc/clients/:id/settings` | `{codeTtl?, accessTtl?, refreshTtl?, pkceRequired?, consent?, ratePerMinute?, rotation?}`, `consent` one of `inherit`, `on`, `off` and `rotation` one of `inherit`, `rotate`, `reuse`; `null` for `codeTtl` or `ratePerMinute` inherits the tenant's. A public client cannot turn PKCE off or keep refresh tokens (409); a self-registered client always asks for consent (409). Audited `oidc.client.settings.updated` |

The protocol endpoints apply them: the code lifetime at `/oauth/authorize`, PKCE at the authorization and PAR
endpoints, the consent screen at `/oauth/authorize` (`prompt=consent` still asks), the rate limit at `/oauth/token`,
`/oauth/par` and `/oauth/device_authorization` (429 `slow_down` with `Retry-After`), and rotation at the refresh
grant (`reuse`: the answer has no `refresh_token`; the old one keeps working until it expires).

### Changed

- `POST /auth/login`: the tenant's lockout settings; a local password that no longer meets the tenant's policy, or has
  passed a forced expiry, signs in to the `password` stage with `passwordChange: {reason: policy | expired | leaked}`.
  The second-factor step offers only the methods the tenant allows (an account with none of them keeps its own);
  `POST /auth/mfa/{totp,email,email/send,webauthn}` answer 403 `mfa_method_not_allowed` for another kind when the
  account has an allowed one.
- `POST /auth/password/check`: the tenant's rules, including any character classes it turned on.
- `POST /me/password`, `POST /auth/password/reset`, `POST /admin/users` (with a password), `POST
  /admin/users/:id/password`, sign-up and the CSV import's new `password` column go through one pipeline: the policy
  (400 `reason: policy` with `rule`, or `history`), the tenant's deny words (400 `deny_word`), the leaked-password
  lists (400 `leaked`, or 503 when the tenant fails closed). They may return `warnings`.
- `GET /me/mfa` returns `allowedMethods`; `POST /me/mfa/{totp,email,webauthn/options}` answer 403 for a kind the tenant
  does not allow. Step-up (`window_seconds`, `GET /me` `stepUp.windowSeconds`) is the tenant's window.
- `DELETE /me/grants/:clientId` also audits `oidc.consent.withdrawn` when a consent was removed.
- `POST /admin/federation/oidc/clients`: without `accessTtl`, a new client gets the tenant's default lifetimes.

## Sprint 53 (1.9.0, Unreleased): albums on Files, album links, albums in the feed and groups (B-177 to B-179)

`files/albums.ts` (`s.files.albums`), `files/album-links.ts` (`s.files.albums.links`), routes `routes/albums.ts` and
`routes/albums-public.ts`; migrations `135_albums` and `136_album_links`. Reading needs `files:read`, changing
`files:write`; what a person may do in an album is their standing in it, and what they see of its items is the album's
access rule (`docs/security.md`, "Albums"). Without migration 135, `GET /api/albums` answers `available: false` and the
other routes `503` (`migration: 135_albums`); without 136, the link routes `503` and the public ones `404`.

An album is `workspace` (the workspace sees it), `group` (the group's members see it) or `personal` (its owner and the
people it names). Standing: `owner`, `editor` (orders, removes any item, edits the details and cover, manages viewers
and contributors), `contributor` (adds files, removes their own), `viewer`; in a group album the group's moderators
act as editors. In a workspace or group album a role is held by members of that workspace or group only (`422`,
`step: audience`). `label` is the effective label as the caller may see it (the album's high-water mark when they are
cleared for it), `floorLabel` the label of the title and description. Items are images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF), and
videos once the file store accepts them.

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/albums` | `?kind=workspace\|group\|personal`, `?workspace=`, `?group=`. `{available, albums: [album]}`: the caller's own, those naming them, their workspaces' and groups', newest first. An album is `{id, kind, title, description, floorLabel, label, workspaceId, groupId, ownerId, ownerName, role, cover: {itemId, fileId, chosen} \| null, itemCount, can: {add, edit, manage, editors, delete, links}, createdAt, updatedAt}`; `itemCount` counts only what the caller may see |
| `POST /api/albums` | `{kind, title, description?, label?, workspaceId?, groupId?}` (`groupId` for a group album, which takes the group's `post` right). `201` the album. The label must clear the caller and fit the workspace's ceiling or the group's label (`403`, `step: clearance` or `zone`). Audited `album.created` |
| `GET /api/albums/:id` | The album with `items: [{id, fileId, name, type, kind, size, label, position, version, altText, description, addedBy, addedByName, addedAt, mine}]` in order (only what the caller may see) and, for editors and the owner, `contributors: [{userId, name, role, addedBy, addedAt}]`. `404` outside the audience, `403` below the floor |
| `PATCH /api/albums/:id` | Editors. `{title?, description?, label?, coverItemId?}`. Audited `album.updated` |
| `DELETE /api/albums/:id` | The owner. `204`; the files stay. Its links stop working. Audited `album.deleted` |
| `GET /api/albums/:id/card` | B-179: what a feed card shows: `{id, kind, title, description, label, itemCount, cover, ownerName, preview: [{itemId, name, type, altText}]}`, as the caller may see it |
| `POST /api/albums/:id/items` | Contributors. `{fileIds}` (at most 100): files the caller may change (a member of the file's workspace, cleared for its label), ready, of an image or video type (`415` otherwise), within the audience's ceiling (`403`, `step: zone`). `201 {added, alreadyIn, album}`. Audited `album.item.added`; the people in the album are told (batched) |
| `DELETE /api/albums/:id/items/:itemId` | Contributors their own, editors any they can see. The album; the file stays. Audited `album.item.removed` |
| `PUT /api/albums/:id/order` | Editors. `{itemIds}`: the items named take the places they held, in this order; the others keep theirs. Audited `album.reordered` |
| `GET /api/albums/:id/items/:itemId/preview` | The item's preview, through the album's access rule; where none was drawn, the cleaned image (audited `file.downloaded`, `detail.via: album:<id>`) |
| `GET /api/albums/:id/items/:itemId/content` | The item as served to readers (images without their metadata), under the media sandbox. Audited `file.downloaded` with `detail.via: album:<id>` |
| `GET /api/albums/:id/download` | What the caller sees of the album as a zip (`application/zip`), streamed through `platform/zip-writer.ts` (stored members, data descriptors, no length known up front), cleaned copies, names made unique. `409` when there is nothing to download, `413` past about 3.7 GiB. Audited `album.downloaded` (`detail.files`, `detail.count`, `detail.bytes`) |
| `PUT /api/albums/:id/contributors/:userId` | Editors (only the owner gives or takes `editor`). `{role: viewer\|contributor\|editor}`. The contributors. Audited `album.contributor.set` |
| `DELETE /api/albums/:id/contributors/:userId` | Editors, or the person leaving. Audited `album.contributor.removed` |
| `POST /api/albums/:id/post` | B-179, also `feed:write`. Contributors. `{body?, visibility?: workspace\|unlisted\|public}`. A feed post in the album's workspace (or group) with `source: {kind: album, id}`, labelled the album's label; `public` needs a public album; a personal album is refused (`409`). `201` the post (`202` when held). Audited `album.posted` |
| `GET /api/groups/:gid/albums` | B-179, also `groups:read`. The group's Albums tab: `{available, albums, canCreate}` for a reader of the group |
| `GET /api/albums/:id/share-links` | Editors. `[{id, albumId, mode, password, expiresAt, views, downloads, lastUsedAt, createdBy, createdAt, revokedAt, state}]` |
| `POST /api/albums/:id/share-links` | Editors. `{mode: view\|download, expiresInHours (1 to 720, default 72), password?}` (at least 8 characters, hashed with argon2id). Needs the tenant's anonymous-link setting and a public album floor (`403`, `step: policy` or `label`), and an expiry within the tenant's maximum (`400`). `201` with the `token` (`exa_…`, shown once). Audited `album.share.created` |
| `DELETE /api/albums/:id/share-links/:linkId` | Editors. `204`. Audited `album.share.revoked` |
| `GET /api/albums/:id/upload-links` | Editors. `[{id, albumId, workspaceId, folderId, expiresAt, maxFiles, maxBytes, received, remaining, createdBy, createdAt, revokedAt, state}]` |
| `POST /api/albums/:id/upload-links` | Editors who are members of the album's workspace. `{expiresInHours (1 to 720, default 168), maxFiles (1 to 500, default 50), maxBytes? (per file, at most FILES_MAX_BYTES), folderId?}`. The album's label must fit the workspace's ceiling and the caller's clearance (`403`). `201` with the `token` (`exu_…`, shown once). Audited `album.upload.link_created` |
| `DELETE /api/albums/:id/upload-links/:linkId` | Editors. `204`. Audited `album.upload.link_revoked` |
| `GET /api/albums/:id/uploads` | Editors. What came in through the links: `[{id, linkId, fileId, name, size, uploaderName, state: scanning\|added\|rejected, reason, createdAt, settledAt}]` |

Public routes (no session, no cookie; rate-limited per address with SHARE_ANONYMOUS_PER_MINUTE, media at ten times
that; every refusal of a link is the same `404`):

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/public/album-links/open` | `{token, password?}`. The album as anonymous readers see it (public items only): `{title, description, label, mode, expiresAt, mediaExpiresAt, coverItemId, items: [{id, name, type, kind, size, altText, description, preview, full, download?}]}`; `preview`, `full` and `download` are signed media addresses good for 15 minutes. `401` with `passwordRequired: true` without or with a wrong password (audited `album.share.password_failed`), `429` past the attempts (10 per link and address range in 15 minutes). Audited `album.share.viewed` |
| `GET /api/public/album-links/media/:cap` | One item through a media address: `preview` (the preview, else the cleaned image), `full` (the cleaned copy inline), `download` (download links only, an attachment, audited `album.share.downloaded`) |
| `POST /api/public/album-links/download` | `{token, password?}`. The public items as a zip, for a download link (`403` for a view link). Audited `album.share.downloaded` |
| `POST /api/public/album-uploads/open` | `{token}`. `{albumTitle, maxFiles, maxBytes, remaining, expiresAt}` |
| `PUT /api/public/album-uploads` | The raw file, the token in `X-Upload-Token`, `?name=<file name>&uploader=<the uploader's name>` (1 to 80 characters, stored as given, sealed). A place is taken atomically (`409` when the link is full), `413` past the link's size or FILES_MAX_BYTES, the storage quotas apply; the file is the link creator's, in the album's workspace, labelled with the album's label, and goes through quarantine and the scan. `202 {id, name, size, state}`; it joins the album when the scan passes (`album.upload.added`), or is `rejected` with the scanner's reason (`album.upload.rejected`). Recorded with the spam signals (surface `post`, the link as the account, the address range). Audited `album.upload.received` |

Notifications (B-179): a new kind `album` (People and groups). Items added to an album are gathered for ten minutes
(the job `album.notify`, one per album and window); then the owner and the people the album names each get one
notice, "N items added to <title>", counting only what they may see and nothing they added themselves, labelled with
the highest of those items, routed to `#/albums?album=<id>`. Sprint 49 preferences decide the channels and timing.

## Sprint 53 (1.9.0, Unreleased): group proposals, voting and carrying out decisions (B-174 to B-176)

Migrations `133_group_proposals` and `134_group_votes` (not registered yet: until they are applied, the reads answer
`available: false` and every change is 503 with `reason: migration_pending`). `groups:read` reads, `groups:write`
changes; inside the group the caller's rights and the group's governance settings decide (`groups/governance.ts`).
Proposals belong to groups, not channels (422 `step: parent`). Proposal text, options and actions are sealed as
`group-proposal:<id>` and labelled as the group is; they pass the `user-input` guardrail (422 `step: guardrails`).

### Governance settings (B-174)

| Route | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/governance` | readers of the group | `{available, propose: members \| role \| owners, proposeRole, method, threshold: {num, den}, quorum: {kind: none \| share \| count, value}, minHours, maxHours, defaultHours, secret, confirmKinds, rules, canPropose, canManage, canConfirm}` |
| `PUT /api/groups/:id/governance` | `settings` | Any of those fields and `rules` (text or null). 422 `step: hours` (min ≤ default ≤ max), `threshold` (a fraction above one half), `quorum`, `propose` (role mode needs `proposeRole`, a tier or a custom role id). Audited `group.governance.updated` (the rules' text is not) |

### Proposals (B-174)

| Route | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/proposals` | readers | `?state=`. `{available, proposals: [{id, kind, state, title, method, secret, outcome, opensAt, closesAt, electorate, turnout, needsConfirmation, createdBy, createdByName, label, mine: {eligible, voted}}]}`; drafts only to their author and the owners. Due votes are closed first |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/proposals` | whom the settings allow (owners always) | `{kind: free \| setting \| member \| role \| rules \| spend, title, body?, options?, action?, method?, threshold?, quorum?, secret?, hours?}`. Actions: `setting {patch: {name?, description?, visibility?, joinMode?, tags?, website?, memberLimit?}}`, `member {op: add \| remove, userId}`, `role {userId, role? \| customRoleId?}`, `rules {rules}`, `spend {amountMinor, memo?}`. A kind that changes something is decided by majority or supermajority (422 `step: method`); approval and ranked choice need 2 to 20 options. 403 `step: governance`; 422 `step: action` or `budget`. 201 with the proposal |
| `GET /api/group-proposals/:id` | readers | The proposal: `{…, options: [{id, label}], action, result (the tally and its working), commitments (secret, after close), commitmentsDigest, ballots (public, to members), mine: {eligible, voted, choice}, can: {edit, open, delete, vote, confirm}, discussion: {conversationId, messageId}, carriedResult, failure}` |
| `PATCH /api/group-proposals/:id` | its author, while a draft | The same fields as creating. 409 once voting has started |
| `DELETE /api/group-proposals/:id` | its author or an owner, while a draft | `{id, deleted}` |
| `POST /api/group-proposals/:id/open` | its author or an owner | `{hours?}` within the group's range (422 `step: hours`). Fixes the electorate (members in effect with more than a guest's rights; 422 `step: electorate` when none), posts it in the group's linked conversation as the author, tells the electorate (`group.governance`). Audited `group.proposal.opened` |

States: `draft → open → closed` (with `outcome`: `passed`, `rejected` or `no_quorum`) `→ carried_out | failed` for a
passed proposal of an actionable kind.

### Voting (B-175)

| Route | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/group-proposals/:id/ballots` | the electorate, while open | `{choice}`: `yes \| no \| abstain`, or option ids (approved, or ranked best first). Again to change it. A secret ballot answers `{receipt: {proposalId, ballotId, choice, nonce, commitment, token}}`, once; changing it takes `{choice, ballotId, token}` from the receipt (409 `step: receipt` without, 403 with a wrong one). 403 `step: electorate` for someone not in the group when voting opened; 409 after close |
| `POST /api/group-proposals/:id/verify-receipt` | readers | `{commitment, choice}`. `{published, counted, detail}`: whether that pair is in the list published at close |

Closing happens on the first read after `closesAt` and every minute in the `groups.governance.tick` job, which also
sends one reminder before the close to the electorate who have not voted. `group.proposal.closed` records the tally,
the quorum, the rounds of a ranked-choice count and, for a secret vote, the number and digest of the commitments.

### Decisions (B-176)

| Route | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/group-proposals/:id/confirm` | an owner | A passed decision of a kind in `confirmKinds`: confirmed and carried out now. 409 when it does not wait |
| `POST /api/group-proposals/:id/decline` | an owner | `{reason?}`. Not carried out: `failed` with the reason |

A passed decision is applied through the group's services as the group (an owner's rights in that group only):
`setting` through `PATCH /api/groups/:id`'s service, `member add` accepts a pending request to join or sends an
invitation, `member remove`, `role` through the member role change, `rules`, and `spend` as a budget entry. Audited
`group.decision.applied`, `failed`, `awaiting`, `confirmed` and `declined`; the result is posted in the conversation.

### Budget (B-174, B-176)

| Route | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/groups/:id/budget` | readers | `{available, canManage, currency, balanceMinor, entries: [{id, amountMinor, currency, balanceAfter, memo, proposalId, createdBy, createdByName, createdAt}]}` |
| `PUT /api/groups/:id/budget` | `settings` | `{currency}` (ISO 4217); 409 while the balance is not zero |
| `POST /api/groups/:id/budget/entries` | `settings` | `{amountMinor, memo?}`: money in (positive) or out (negative). 409 `step: balance` below zero, `step: budget` with no budget. 201 |

## Sprint 52 (1.9.0, Unreleased): the search index, search across chats and posts, one search box (B-170 to B-173)

`search/` (`s.search`: `normalise.ts` the folding, query reading and snippets, `keys.ts` the tenant search keys,
`indexer.ts` the blind index written at write and by the backfill, `query.ts` the reader, `chats.ts`, `posts.ts`,
`everything.ts`), routes `routes/search.ts`; migrations `138_search_index` and `139_search_state`. Without them, the
search routes answer as before the index (`engine: fallback`), writes index nothing, `GET /api/admin/search` says
`installed: false` and the admin actions answer `503`. Queries are never audited or stored; the console keeps recent
searches in the browser. What the index reveals is in `docs/security.md`, "Search index".

A query is words (all must match, folded: case, accents, a final plural "s"; common English stop words left out),
`"quoted phrases"` (the words side by side) and `word*` (a beginning; type-ahead reads the last word so). Every
answer says `engine: index` (the tenant's blind index, once its backfill finished) or `fallback` (before it: chats by
the per-conversation keyed terms of B-2605 with phrases and prefixes checked on the opened text, posts by opening the
newest 1,000 posts and comments in scope, `partial: true` when that cut anything). Every result is checked again as
the caller before its text is opened; a result is a snippet around the match with `highlights: [[start, end]]`.

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/search` | Any one of `messages:read`, `feed:read`, `files:read`, `knowledge:read`, `groups:read`, `social:read`, `records:read`, `chat:read`. `?q=` (1 to 500), `?sources=chats,posts,files,knowledge,groups,people,apps,assistant` (default: every source the caller holds the permission of), `?limit=` (1 to 20, default 5). `{q, engine, groups: [{source, title, items: [{id, title, sub, snippet, highlights, label, at, route}], total, error, route}]}` in that order of sources; a source the caller may not search is left out; one that fails has `items: []` and `error` ("This source could not be searched just now.") while the others answer. Each source is its own search as the caller: B-171 and B-172 below, `files.search`, knowledge document names then passages (`KnowledgeService.search`, lenient, no rerank), `groups.list`, the people directory, app records through each entity's `q` (ten apps, twenty entities), the caller's own assistant chats by title. `route` is a console route (`messages?convo=`, `messages?post=`, `files?file=`, `knowledge?kb=`, `groups?group=`, `person?user=`, `apps?app=`, `chat?id=`) |
| `GET /api/search/suggest` | The same permissions. `?q=` (up to 200; empty answers `{groups: [], completions: []}`), `?sources=`. Type-ahead: three results a source with the last word as a prefix (knowledge by document name only), and `completions`: words of those results that complete it |
| `GET /api/search/messages` | `messages:read`. B-171: every conversation the caller is in now. `?q=`, `?from=<user>`, `?conversation=`, `?group=` (the group's linked conversation), `?workspace=`, `?after=` and `?before=` (epoch ms, ISO date or date-time; a date as `before` is the end of that day), `?has=file,link`, `?label=`, `?mode=keyword\|semantic\|hybrid` (default `hybrid` when `MESSAGING_EMBED_MODEL` is set, else `keyword`; `409` for meaning without it), `?limit=` (1 to 100), `?offset=`. `{items: [{kind: message, id, conversationId, conversation: {kind, title, groupId}, authorId, authorName, threadId, createdAt, label, hasFile, snippet, highlights, route, score: {fused, keyword, semantic}}], total, mode, engine}`. Scope first: active conversations the caller is a member of at a label they clear, from the time they joined, without people in a block with them; filters before counting |
| `GET /api/search/posts` | `feed:read`. B-172: posts and comments of the feed, groups and lists. `?q=`, `?author=`, `?tag=`, `?group=` (`403`/`404` as the group's own read), `?workspace=`, `?list=` (one of the caller's lists, `404` otherwise), `?after=`, `?before=`, `?kind=post\|comment\|all`, `?limit=`, `?offset=`. `{items: [{kind, id, postId, authorId, authorName, workspaceId, groupId, createdAt, label, tags, snippet, highlights, route, score}], total, engine, partial}`. The feed's scope (`FeedService.scope`); unlisted posts and their comments for their author only; blocks either way and mutes take the other person out; labels within the caller's clearance; all before counting |
| `GET /api/admin/search` | `tenant:manage`. `{installed, enabled, state: off\|building\|ready, activeVersion, buildingVersion, progress: {processed, total, percent, at} \| null, jobId, error, startedAt, finishedAt, documents, keys: [{version, state, createdAt}], writeIndexing}` |
| `POST /api/admin/search/enable` | `tenant:manage`. `{}`. Turns the index on: key version 1, writes indexed from now, the job `search.backfill` over existing messages, posts and comments. `202` the status; `409` when on. Audited `search.index.enabled`; `search.index.ready` (system) when the backfill finishes |
| `POST /api/admin/search/rebuild` | `tenant:manage`. `{restart?}`. While a backfill is building and `restart` is not true: resumes it from its saved cursor (audited `search.index.resumed`). Otherwise builds everything again under a new key version; queries keep the current one until it is complete, then the old version's postings, prefixes and key are deleted (audited `search.index.rebuilt`). `202` the status |
| `POST /api/admin/search/rotate` | `tenant:manage`. `{}`. A new search key: as a rebuild, audited `search.key.rotated` |
| `POST /api/admin/search/disable` | `tenant:manage`. `{}`. Deletes the tenant's postings, prefixes, documents, keys and state; search answers as before. Audited `search.index.disabled` |

Jobs: `search.backfill` (`{tenantId, version}`, 200 documents a batch, cursor and counts saved after each, five attempts,
progress reported) and `search.index.doc` (a write whose indexing failed, retried). Indexing at write follows the
`message.*` and `post.*` integration events and the audit entries `feed.comment.created`, `feed.comment.deleted`,
`feed.post.visibility`, `messaging.conversation.deleted` and `moderation.action.applied`/`reversed`; it runs after the
write commits and never fails it. Tenant offboarding deletes the index with the tenant's other derived tables.

### 1.9.9-qa: saved searches, links to one message, search within (B-173)

`search/saved.ts` (`s.search.saved`), `search/filters.ts` (the chat and post filter schemas the search routes and saved
searches share); migration `145_saved_searches`. Until it is applied, `GET /api/search/saved` answers
`{available: false, items: []}` and the other saved-search routes `503`. A saved search's name, query and filters are
sealed (`docs/security.md`, "Search index"); saved searches are the caller's own, and another person's is `404`.
Since 1.9.9-qa a message result's `route` is `messages?convo=<conversation>&message=<message>` and a comment's
`messages?post=<post>&comment=<comment>`; the console opens the exact message or comment.

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/search/messages/:id/locate` | `messages:read`. Where a message is, for a link to it: `{id, state: sent\|deleted\|hidden\|held\|unavailable, conversationId, createdAt, threadId}`, never its text. `unavailable` (with nulls) for a message the caller cannot see now (not a member, before they joined, a block, above their clearance) and for an id that does not exist, alike |
| `GET /api/search/saved` | Any one of the search permissions. `{available, max: 100, items: [{id, name, q, source, filters, createdAt, updatedAt, lastRunAt}]}`, the most recently changed or run first |
| `POST /api/search/saved` `{name, q, source?: all\|chats\|posts\|files\|knowledge\|groups\|people\|apps\|assistant, filters?}` | The same, and the source's own permission (`403` otherwise). `name` 1 to 120, `q` 1 to 500. `filters` (chats and posts only, `400` for other sources) are the query parameters of `GET /api/search/messages` or `/posts` as strings or lists (`{conversation, has: ["file"]}`), checked by the same schemas; empty values are dropped. At most 100 a person (`422`). `201` the saved search. Audited `search.saved.created` with the source and the filter names, never the name, query or values |
| `GET /api/search/saved/:id` | The caller's own saved search (`404` otherwise) |
| `PATCH /api/search/saved/:id` `{name?, q?, source?, filters?}` | Renames it or changes it; `filters` replace the old ones, and a new `source` without `filters` drops those it does not take. Audited `search.saved.updated` (`renamed`, `query` as booleans) |
| `DELETE /api/search/saved/:id` | `{id, deleted: true}`. Audited `search.saved.deleted` |
| `POST /api/search/saved/:id/run` `{limit?, offset?}` | Runs it as the caller now, with the source's permission asked again: `{saved, results}`, where `results` is the answer of `GET /api/search/messages` (chats), `/posts` (posts) or `GET /api/search` (all, or one other source). Sets `lastRunAt`; not audited |

The console: Search › "Save this search" (a dialog), the saved searches on the empty Search page (run, rename, delete),
and the palette command "Saved searches"; "Search in this conversation" (Messages, the conversation's Search drawer and
the palette), "Search in this group" (Groups, a group's header and the palette) and "Search in this feed" (the feed's
toolbar and the palette) open `#/search` with `?conversation=`, `?group=`, `?workspace=`, `?list=` or `?tag=` as the
filter, shown as "Searching only in …" with "Search everywhere".

## Sprint 52 (1.9.0, Unreleased): feature flags, targeting and rollout (B-167 to B-169)

A flag has a key (`^[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{1,55}$`), a type (`boolean` for on/off, `variant` with two to twenty named
variants, `number` with optional `min` and `max`), a default, a description, an owner and a life cycle: `planned`
(not live: it answers its default everywhere), `active`, `deprecated` (both live), `removed` (its default, no new
values). Values are set at four levels and the most specific wins: **workspace over tenant over plan over platform**,
then the default. A plan's value is set on the flag, or comes from the plan's entitlement `flag.<key>` (B-162). A
value at any level may carry a `rollout` of 0 to 100%: it reaches that share of people (or workspaces or tenants, the
flag's `rolloutBy`), sticky by a SHA-256 bucket of the flag key and the unit's id; those outside it fall to the next
level. A locked flag (`overridable: false`) ignores tenant and workspace values. Stale warnings: deprecated for over
30 days, active and unchanged for over 90, planned for over 90, past its review date, or rolled out to everyone at the
platform level for over 30 days. Every change is audited `flag.*` (label `internal`). Until migration
`137_feature_flags` is applied, every flag answers its built-in default, the list answers `available: false` and the
writes answer `503`.

| Route | Permission | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/feature-flags` | `platform:manage` or `tenant:manage`, clearance internal | Lists the flags. `{available, canManage, flags: [{key, type, defaultValue, options, description, owner, state, stateChangedAt, reviewAt, client, overridable, rolloutBy, stale: [{code, message}], mine: {tenant, workspaces}, platform?, counts?, pending?}], pending, workspaces}`; `platform`, `counts` and `pending` for platform admins only; removed flags only for them |
| `POST /api/admin/feature-flags` `{key, type, defaultValue, options?, description?, owner?, state?: planned \| active, reviewAt?: YYYY-MM-DD, client?, overridable?, rolloutBy?: user \| workspace \| tenant}` | `platform:manage`, a recent sign-in | Defines a flag (planned unless asked). Audited `flag.feature.created` |
| `GET /api/admin/feature-flags/proposals?state=&key=` | `platform:manage` | Platform changes waiting for (or decided by) a second platform admin |
| `POST /api/admin/feature-flags/proposals/{id}/approve` `{note?}` | `platform:manage`, a recent sign-in | Applies a pending change; never by its proposer (`403`, step `dual-control`). Audited `flag.change.approved` |
| `POST /api/admin/feature-flags/proposals/{id}/reject` `{note?}` | `platform:manage` | Rejects a pending change, or withdraws it when the proposer does. Audited `flag.change.rejected` / `flag.change.withdrawn` |
| `GET /api/admin/feature-flags/{key}` | `platform:manage` or `tenant:manage` | One flag with its stale warnings, its values (every level for platform admins, the caller's tenant's otherwise), its recent proposals (platform admins) and `you`, the caller's own evaluation |
| `PATCH /api/admin/feature-flags/{key}` `{description?, owner?, reviewAt?, client?, overridable?, rolloutBy?, options?}` | `platform:manage` | Describes the flag; the type never changes. Audited `flag.feature.updated` |
| `POST /api/admin/feature-flags/{key}/state` `{state, note?}` | `platform:manage`, a recent sign-in | Moves it along the life cycle: planned → active or removed; active → deprecated or removed; deprecated → active or removed; removed → deprecated. Audited `flag.feature.state_changed` |
| `PUT /api/admin/feature-flags/{key}/platform` `{defaultValue?, platform?: {value, rollout} \| null, reason?}` | `platform:manage`, a recent sign-in | The default and the platform value with its rollout (`null` clears it). A planned flag's change applies at once (`200`, audited `flag.platform.changed`); a live one waits for a second platform admin (`202` with the proposal, audited `flag.change.proposed`; one at a time, else `409`) |
| `PUT /api/admin/feature-flags/{key}/plans/{plan}` `{value, rollout?, note?}`, `DELETE` | `platform:manage` | A plan's value (by plan key). Audited `flag.value.set` / `flag.value.cleared` |
| `PUT /api/admin/feature-flags/{key}/tenant` `{value, rollout?, note?}`, `DELETE` | `tenant:manage` | The caller's own tenant's value; `403` on a locked flag. Audited `flag.value.set` / `flag.value.cleared` |
| `PUT /api/admin/feature-flags/{key}/workspaces/{workspace}` `{value, rollout?, note?}`, `DELETE` | `tenant:manage` | A workspace of the caller's tenant (`404` otherwise). Audited as above |
| `GET /api/admin/feature-flags/{key}/explain?workspace=&user=&tenant=` | `platform:manage` or `tenant:manage` | "Why does this tenant see this": `{key, value, on, level: workspace \| tenant \| plan \| platform \| default \| builtin, reason, state, unit, steps: [{level, set, value?, rollout?, fromEntitlement?, bucket?, reached?, skipped?}]}` for the caller's tenant (`tenant` for platform admins only) |
| `GET /api/me/flags` | signed in | `{flags: {key: value}}`: every flag with `client: true` that is not removed, evaluated for the caller in the current workspace |

The same `flags` object is in `GET /api/me` and in `GET /api/auth/session` (and the sign-in answer) once the session
is active. Server code asks `s.flags.on(ctx, key)` or `s.flags.value(ctx, key)` with `ctx = {tenantId, workspaceId?,
userId?}`; answers are cached for 30 seconds and dropped on every instance over the bus topic `feature.flags` (a
subscription change or an approved plan version drops the tenant's plan). A workflow branch step tests a flag with
`{flag: <key>, op, right?}` in place of `left` (the run's tenant, workspace and owner); an app flow condition leaf
`{field: "flag", flag: <key>, op, value?}` compiles to that step. Plugins holding `read:flags` call `flags.read`
`{key?, workspace?}` as their installer or viewer.

1.9.9-qa (live changes): every change that publishes `feature.flags` also reaches the consoles at once. Each instance
emits the socket event `flags.changed` `{at}` (no key, no value) to the console sockets it holds: the affected
tenant's room for a tenant, workspace or subscription change, every socket for a platform-wide change (a definition,
a platform or plan value, an approved proposal). Bursts are coalesced per room for 250 ms (`realtime/flags.ts`). The
console (`web/js/flags.js`) then fetches `GET /api/me/flags` after a random wait of 50 to 450 ms and re-applies every
`data-feature-flag` gate; a reconnecting socket fetches too, and the one-minute refetch on route changes stays as the
fallback. `App.flags.live()` says whether the console hears the event.

## Sprint 51 (1.9.0, Unreleased): billing cycles, tiered prices and discounts (B-163 to B-165)

Migrations `125_billing_cycles_tiers` (statement cycle columns; tiers need no structural change, price book items are
JSON) and `126_billing_discounts`. Until they are applied, statements are computed and stored exactly as before.

**Cycles (B-163).** A statement covers a window: a tenant without a subscription keeps its calendar months; with
one, the statement of a month is the subscription cycle that ends in it (`:month` is that month: a quarter from
January is the `2026-03` statement). A month inside a longer cycle resolves to that cycle's statement, and the days
before a subscription starts (or after it ends) are a statement of their own. Statements stored before 1.9.0 read as
one-month cycles; nothing stored is rewritten.

**Lines.** Every statement view has `period {from, to}`, `cycle {kind, months, anchorDay, subscriptionId?, planId?,
planName?}`, `pricing` (`monthly`: priced as before, money in `lines`; `cycle`: money in `charges`, `lines` keep the
metered detail at zero), `discountMicros` and `charges`: `[{kind: plan | seats | proration | usage | discount | credit
| tax, description, quantity, unit, unitAmount, amount, meter?, tier?, ruleId?, timing?: advance | arrears, from?,
to?, planId?, model?}]` (micros; in a cycle statement each line is a whole minor unit, rounded half away from zero;
`subtotal = Σ` non-tax lines, `total = subtotal + tax`, tax on the subtotal after discounts). The model is
`server/src/billing/types.ts` `ChargeLine`. A cycle statement's CSV export lists its charges.

**Tiered prices (B-164).** A price book item may add `pricing: flat | graduated | volume | package`, `tiers: [{upTo |
null, unitPriceMicros, flatMicros?}]` (graduated and volume; ascending, bounds inclusive, the last unbounded),
`minimumMicros` and `capMicros` (per cycle). A package charges `unitPriceMicros` per block of `perUnits`, a part block
rounded up. Tiers carry over price book versions inside a cycle. `400` for tiers on a flat or package item, missing
tiers, tiers out of order, or a cap below the minimum.

| Route | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /admin/billing/statements/:month/preview?tenant=` (`billing:read`) | The statement computed now, not stored, plus `discounts: [{ruleId, name, amount, capped, skipped}]` (why a rule did or did not apply) |
| `GET /admin/billing/statements` | `current` is the statement the present falls in (a cycle may end in a later month) |
| `GET /admin/billing/discounts?state=&source=&tenant=` (`billing:manage`) | `{rules, policy}` |
| `GET /admin/billing/discounts/:id` (`billing:manage`) | The rule, its codes (promotions) and approvals |
| `POST /admin/billing/discounts` (`billing:manage`) `{name, source?: rule \| promotion \| negotiated, scope: plan \| seats \| meter \| model \| family \| statement, scopeValue?, kind: percent \| amount \| allowance \| volume \| commitment, terms, currency?, validFrom?, validTo?, target?: {kind: all} \| {kind: tenants, ids} \| {kind: plans, ids}, stackOrder?, note?}` | `201 {rule, approval, needsApproval, reason}`. `terms`: `percentPpm` (percent, commitment; `minMonths`, default 12), `amountMinor` with `currency` (amount), `quantity` (allowance, of the meter: scope `meter`, or `model`/`family` with `terms.meter`), `tiers: [{from, percentPpm}]` with `measure: quantity \| amount` (volume). A negotiated rule targets one tenant. Above the approval threshold (and every allowance) the rule is `proposed`. Audited `billing.discount.created` or `billing.discount.proposed` |
| `PATCH /admin/billing/discounts/:id` (`billing:manage`) `{name?, stackOrder?, note?, state?: retired, scope?, scopeValue?, kind?, terms?, currency?, validFrom?, validTo?, target?}` | A change of terms above the threshold waits for approval (the rule keeps its terms meanwhile). Audited `billing.discount.updated`, `change-proposed` or `retired` |
| `GET /admin/billing/discount-approvals?state=` (`billing:manage`) | Proposals: `{id, ruleId, change: create \| update, proposal, reason, state, proposedBy, …}` |
| `POST /admin/billing/discount-approvals/:id/approve` and `/reject` (`billing:manage`) `{note?}` | Dual control: the proposer gets `403` (`step: dual-control`, audited `billing.discount.approval-refused`). Audited `billing.discount.approved` / `rejected` |
| `GET`, `PUT /admin/billing/discount-policy` (`billing:manage`) `{capPercentPpm?, capAmountMinor?, approvalPercentPpm?, approvalAmountMinor?}` | The cap on a statement's total discount (a share of the pre-discount total, an amount, or both: the smaller wins) and the approval thresholds (defaults 20% and 500.00). Audited `billing.discount.policy-updated` |
| `GET /admin/billing/promo-codes?rule=`, `POST /admin/billing/promo-codes` `{ruleId, code?, expiresAt?, maxRedemptions?}`, `PATCH /admin/billing/promo-codes/:id` `{expiresAt?, maxRedemptions?, state?}` (`billing:manage`) | Codes of promotion rules, upper case (generated when omitted). Audited `billing.promo.created`, `updated`, `retired` |
| `POST /admin/billing/promo-codes/redeem` (`tenant:manage`) `{code}` | For the session's tenant: `201 {redemptionId, rule}`. Every refusal (unknown, expired, retired, limit reached, already redeemed, not for this tenant or plan) is the same `409 This code cannot be redeemed.`; the audit `billing.promo.redeem-refused` says why. Audited `billing.promo.redeemed`. Redemptions are counted in one conditional update, so concurrent ones never pass the limit |
| `GET /admin/billing/redemptions` (`billing:read`) | The tenant's redemptions |

**Applying discounts.** Active rules valid at some moment of the window and targeting the tenant (all, listed, its
plan; a promotion once redeemed) apply in ascending `stackOrder`, each to its scope as the rules before it left it
(two 10% rules make 19%), never more than the scope, within the cap; each is its own `discount` line with `ruleId`.
A model or family scope takes the model's share of each usage line by quantity (`llama3.1` covers `llama3.1:8b`; a
trailing `*` is a prefix). A free allowance is valued at what those units would have cost.

## Sprint 51 (1.9.0, Unreleased): plans, subscriptions and the statement PDF (B-162, B-166)

Money in these routes is in integer minor units of the currency (cents; none for zero-decimal currencies). Proration
measures whole seconds and rounds each amount once, half away from zero (`mulDiv`): a change in the middle of a period
credits the old chargeable amount for the rest of the period and charges the new one for the same rest. The
denominator is always the whole cycle, so a short first period is prorated against it too.

| Route | Permission | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/billing/plans?retired=true` | `billing:read` | Tenant admins see the visible, active plans with an approved version; holders of `platform:manage` see every plan, private and (with `retired=true`) retired ones, with `pending` and `versions`. `{plans: [{id, key, name, description, visibility, state, trialDays, currentVersion, subscribable, current: {version, prices, allowances, entitlements, …}}], canManage}` |
| `GET /api/admin/billing/plans/{id}` | `billing:read` | One plan; a private plan is `404` to a tenant not on it |
| `POST /api/admin/billing/plans` `{key, name, description?, visibility?: visible \| private, trialDays?, prices, allowances?, entitlements?}` | `platform:manage`, a browser session, a recent sign-in | Creates the plan and its version 1 as `pending`: nothing can subscribe until a second platform admin approves it. `prices: [{currency, months: 1..36, priceMinor, seatPriceMinor, includedSeats}]`, one per currency and cycle length (a cycle without its own price uses the one-month price times its months); `allowances: {meter: units per month}` over the price book meters; `entitlements`: at most 50 flat keys (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$`) of a boolean, an integer or a string of up to 200 characters. Audited `billing.plan.created` |
| `PATCH /api/admin/billing/plans/{id}` `{name?, description?, visibility?, state?: active \| retired, trialDays?}` | as above | At once (no approval): nothing here changes a price. Audited `billing.plan.updated` / `billing.plan.retired` |
| `POST /api/admin/billing/plans/{id}/versions` `{prices, allowances?, entitlements?}` | as above | Proposes a version; one waits per plan at a time (`409`). Audited `billing.plan.proposed` |
| `POST /api/admin/billing/plans/{id}/versions/{version}/approve` `{note?}` | as above | A second platform admin puts it in force from now (`403` with `step: dual-control` for the proposer). Subscribers move to it at their next renewal. Audited `billing.plan.approved` |
| `POST /api/admin/billing/plans/{id}/versions/{version}/reject` `{note?}` | as above | Rejects it, or withdraws it when the proposer asks. Audited `billing.plan.rejected` / `billing.plan.withdrawn` |
| `GET /api/admin/billing/subscription?tenant=` | `billing:read` | `{tenantId, subscription: {id, plan: {id, key, name, version}, seats, includedSeats, currency, state: trialing \| active \| paused, trialEnd, startedAt, endsAt, cycle: {kind, months, anchorDay}, periodStart, periodEnd, cancelAtPeriodEnd, pausedAt, pendingChange, cycleAmountMinor, priceMinor, seatPriceMinor} \| null, history: [{seq, at, kind, state, planId, planVersion, seats, detail, actor}]}`. Time's transitions are written first. `?tenant=` is for system admins |
| `GET /api/admin/billing/subscription/periods?from=&to=` | `billing:read` | Each period overlapping the range with its in-advance `opening` charge, its `segments`, its `changes` (`{at, kind, creditMinor, chargeMinor, netMinor, remainingSeconds, periodSeconds}`) and its `allowances`; plus `stretches`, the statement engine's view. At most five years |
| `POST /api/admin/billing/subscription` `{planId, seats?, currency, cycle: {kind: monthly \| quarterly \| annual \| custom, months? (custom: 1..36), anchorDay?: 1..28}, trialDays?, endsAt?}` | `billing:manage` or `tenant:manage` | Subscribes the tenant (one live subscription: `409`). The anchor day defaults to today's (at most 28); the first period runs to the first anchor. The plan's trial applies to a tenant's first subscription only. A private plan, `trialDays` and `endsAt` in the past need a platform admin (`404`, `403`, `400`). Audited `billing.subscription.created` |
| `POST /api/admin/billing/subscription/preview` `{planId?, seats?, when: now \| renewal}` | as above | What the change would do: `{before, after, creditMinor, chargeMinor, netMinor, remainingSeconds, periodSeconds, nextCycleAmountMinor}`; nothing is stored |
| `PATCH /api/admin/billing/subscription` `{planId?, seats?, when}` | as above | `now`: applied and prorated (`proration` in the answer), audited `billing.subscription.plan-changed` / `seats-changed`. `renewal`: scheduled for the period's end, audited `billing.subscription.change-scheduled`. A paused subscription is not changed (`409`) |
| `DELETE /api/admin/billing/subscription/scheduled-change` | as above | Drops a scheduled change. Audited `billing.subscription.change-unscheduled` |
| `POST /api/admin/billing/subscription/cancel` `{when: period-end \| now}` | as above | At the period's end (audited `cancel-scheduled`; it ends then, audited `cancelled` by the system), or now with the rest of the period credited (audited `cancelled`) |
| `POST /api/admin/billing/subscription/keep` | as above | Undoes a cancellation at period end. Audited `cancel-unscheduled` |
| `POST /api/admin/billing/subscription/pause` / `resume` | as above | Pausing an active subscription credits the rest of the period; resuming charges what is left. While paused the plan charges nothing and has no allowances; periods keep their anchor. Audited `paused` / `resumed` |
| `GET /api/admin/billing/statements/{id}.pdf` | `billing:read` | A stored statement of the caller's tenant (system admins: `?tenant=`) as an A4 PDF: the plan and seats, subscription lines, usage by meter and tier, discounts, taxes, totals, credit notes, refunds and disputes. Another tenant's id is `404`. Audited `billing.statement.exported` with `format: pdf` |

The job `billing.subscriptions.tick` (every 15 minutes, only for tenants with a live subscription that time moved on)
writes trial ends, renewals (a scheduled change applied, the plan's newest approved version taken), cancellations at
period end and fixed ends into the history, dated when they happened, audited `billing.subscription.trial-ended`,
`renewed`, `cancelled` and `ended` with the actor `{service: billing}`.

For the statement engine, `s.subscriptions.at(tenantId, at)` returns what applied at that moment (`SubscriptionAt` in
`billing/types.ts`, plus `plan`, `state`, `trialEnd`, `cancelAtPeriodEnd`; prices are 0 while trialing or paused), or
null without a subscription; `s.subscriptions.periods(tenantId, from, to)` returns the stretches with the same plan,
seats and state, cut at every change and cycle boundary, with `fraction: {num, den}` in whole seconds.

The Stripe push (`POST /api/admin/billing/statements/{month}/push`) sends one invoice item per statement line:
subscription, proration and discount lines included (a credit or discount is a negative item), each with its own
idempotency key `exprsn-<statement>-<kind>-<digest>` and `metadata[line]`. Statements made before 1.9.0 send exactly
the items they always did (`item-<n>` keys).

## Sprint 50 (1.9.0, Unreleased): rate signals, spam patterns, graduated responses and moderation metrics (B-158 to B-161)

Migrations `122_spam_signals` and `123_spam_responses`. Code: `spam/signals.ts` (sliding windows on the rate
limiter's counter store, IP ranges, the time box), `spam/patterns.ts` (SimHash, links, domains, mentions, hashtags,
decay), `spam/policy.ts` (the policy and its defaults), `spam/service.ts` (`s.spam`: `record`, `observe`, `gate`,
responses, the `spam.sweep` job), `spam/metrics.ts` (`s.moderationMetrics`, the `moderation.metrics.rollup` job),
`routes/moderation-spam.ts`. Until a tenant saves a policy nothing is counted and every hook returns at once.

### Where it is counted

`s.spam.record(event)` is called, fire and forget, after posts and quotes (`feed/service.ts`), comments, group posts
(`groups/service.ts`), messages (`messaging/service.ts`), follows (`social/service.ts`), group invitations, reports
(`moderation/service.ts`), every sign-up attempt (`identity/signup.ts`), failed password sign-ins (`routes/auth.ts`)
and firehose records (`atproto/firehose.ts`, per DID, score only). It returns at once; the counting runs behind the
request, time-boxed (2 s), and is dropped when the store is slow. `s.spam.gate(principal, surface)` is called before
a post, comment, group post, message, follow or invitation: on a surface in `enforce` with a response active it
answers `429` (`step: spam-slow` or `spam-limit`, `Retry-After`, `response`, `appeal` the warning to appeal) or adds
a hold finding (`Spam and flood`) to the write's guardrail decision, so the write is held for review as for any rule
(`202` for a held feed post). It lets the write through after 150 ms whatever the store does.

### Routes

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/moderation/spam/policy` | `moderation:review`. `{enabled, surfaces: {<surface>: {mode: off \| shadow \| enforce, windowSeconds, account, ip, tenant}}, patterns, responses, allowList, saved, updatedAt, updatedBy, surfaceNames}` with defaults filled in. Surfaces: `post`, `comment`, `message`, `follow`, `invite`, `report`, `signup`, `signin_failed`, `firehose` |
| `PUT /api/moderation/spam/policy` | `moderation:manage`. Any part of `{enabled?, surfaces?, patterns?, responses?, allowList?}`; only what is sent changes. The first save turns the checks on unless `enabled: false`; every surface starts in `shadow`. `400` when the steps do not rise (`slowAt ≤ holdAt ≤ limitAt ≤ caseAt`), `422` (`step: allow-list`) for an account outside the tenant. Audit `spam.policy.updated` with the modes before and after |
| `GET /api/moderation/spam/accounts?min=&limit=` | `moderation:review`. Accounts with a score now (decayed), highest first: `{account, kind: user \| did \| ip, userId, username, displayName, score, level, reasons: [{signal, value, threshold, points}], events, lastSurface, firstSeen, updatedAt, exempt, responses}` |
| `GET /api/moderation/spam/responses?state=&userId=` | `moderation:review`. `[{id, userId, surface, kind: slow \| hold \| limit \| case, state: active \| lifted \| expired, score, reasons, sanctionId, flagId, startsAt, endsAt, liftedBy, liftedAt, liftReason}]` |
| `POST /api/moderation/spam/responses/:id/lift` | `moderation:sanction`. `{reason?}`. Lifts it and ends its warning (the person is told). `409` when it is not active. Audit `spam.response.lifted` |
| `GET /api/moderation/spam/signals` | `moderation:review`. The tenant-wide window per surface against its thresholds, the counter store's kind and whether it is degraded, events dropped |
| `GET /api/moderation/spam/mine` | `moderation:appeal`. The caller's own active responses (with the warning to appeal) |
| `GET /api/moderation/metrics?days=1..366` | `moderation:review`. `{days, series: [{day, decisions, block, redact, annotate, hold, appealsDecided, appealsUpheld, ttd: {flags, held, appeals: {n, meanMs}}, spam: {<kind>: n}}], totals: {decisions, rates, appealsDecided, appealsUpheld, falsePositiveRate, timeToDecision, spamResponses}, topRules, topSets}`. Default 30 days; today is computed afresh |
| `GET /api/moderation/metrics/export?days=` | `moderation:review`. The daily aggregates as CSV (`day,metric,dim,n,total`; a cell starting with `= + - @` is quoted as text). Audit `moderation.metrics.exported` |

### Scores and responses

Signals: `rate.<surface>.account`, `.ip` (/24 for IPv4, /56 for IPv6) and `.tenant` past the surface's thresholds in
its window; `near_duplicate` (the same text, SimHash within the Hamming threshold, to this many places);
`coordinated_cluster` (this many accounts sending it); `link_burst`; `new_domains` (domains first seen in the tenant
within `newDomainHours`); `mention_flood`, `hashtag_flood` (in one text); `new_account_velocity`. The score is the
higher of this event's points (capped at 100) and the last score decayed by `halfLifeMinutes`. Its step (`slowAt`,
`holdAt`, `limitAt`, `caseAt`) is applied on an enforcing surface: slow mode (one write every `slowSeconds`), hold
for review, a limit of `limitPerHour`, and a case (a `reviewer` flag with checkpoint `spam` carrying the reasons and
counts) with the limit; each for `durationMinutes`, cumulative and never a ban. The person gets a `spam.response`
notification and a system `warn` sanction to appeal through `POST /api/moderation/appeals`; an upheld appeal, a lift
or the sanction's expiry ends the response. Admins (`tenant:manage`, system admins) and the allow-list are exempt
(still scored). Audit: `spam.scored` (when the step rises; `mode`, `wouldApply` in shadow, `exempt`, `reasons`),
`spam.response.applied`, `spam.response.lifted`, `spam.policy.updated`.

The score is also a guardrail condition leaf: `spamScoreFor(tenantId, userId)` in `guardrails/detectors.ts` (50 ms
time box, null when unknown) for the context leaf `{ context: 'spamScore', op: 'gte' | 'lte', value }`.

The Overview's optional card `moderation-trends` (`moderation:review`) shows 14 days of the metrics.

## Sprint 49 (1.9.0, Unreleased): push providers, delivery and the delivery log (B-151, B-152, B-154)

Migrations `117_push_providers` and `118_push_deliveries`. Code: `push/` (`model.ts` the provider schemas, host rules
and message shape; `jwt.ts` APNs, FCM and VAPID tokens; `webpush.ts` RFC 8291 and RFC 8292; `senders.ts` one sender per
kind; `h2-pool.ts` the HTTP/2 sessions; `service.ts` `s.push`), `routes/push.ts`, `realtime/push.ts`, `cli/push.ts`.
With no enabled provider nothing is queued and nothing changes.

### Providers

Platform defaults need `platform:manage` (`/api/admin/platform/push/...`); a tenant's overrides need `tenant:manage`
(`/api/admin/push/...`). The same routes exist under both prefixes. Creating, changing and deleting a provider, storing
a credential and generating VAPID keys need a recent sign-in (`401 step_up`).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET …/providers` | `{scope, providers: [{id, scope, kind, name, appId, enabled, config, lastCheck: {at, ok, detail} \| null, createdAt, updatedAt}]}`. `config` holds settings and `vault:` references only |
| `POST …/providers` `{kind: apns\|fcm\|webpush\|http\|websocket, name, enabled?, config}` | `201`. `config` per kind (below); `400` for a literal credential, an unknown template placeholder, a credential in the URL, or (platform) a reference outside `vault:push/…`; `403` when the admin cannot read a tenant reference now (`secrets:read` and the path policy); `409` for a duplicate name. Audited `push.provider.created` |
| `GET …/providers/:id` | One provider |
| `PATCH …/providers/:id` `{name?, enabled?, config?}` | A new `config` is validated again and resets the last check; the saving admin becomes the references' owner. Audited `push.provider.updated` |
| `DELETE …/providers/:id` | `204`. Audited `push.provider.deleted` |
| `POST …/providers/:id/check` | Validates the credentials without sending a notification: APNs mints the ES256 token and verifies it (or reads the certificate and its key), FCM signs the assertion and fetches an OAuth token, Web Push parses the VAPID pair and signs a token, an HTTP vendor or outside WebSocket reads its references and resolves its host through the egress guard. `{ok, detail, at}` (a failure is `200` with `ok: false`). Audited `push.provider.checked` |
| `POST …/providers/:id/test` `{deviceId?}` | Sends a test to the caller's own active devices of the provider's kind (one when `deviceId`; `404` when it is not theirs). A Socket.IO provider goes to the caller's open consoles and waits for an acknowledgement. `{provider, results: [{deviceId, name, outcome: sent\|retry\|gone\|failed, status, reason, latencyMs}]}`; logged with `test`. Audited `push.test.sent` |
| `PUT …/secrets` `{path, data: {key: value}}` | Stores credentials in the vault (a tenant's as the caller under their path policy; the platform's in the vault's platform scope under `push/`) and answers `{path, version, refs: {key: "vault:<path>#<key>"}}`. Values are never returned |
| `POST …/vapid-keys` `{path}` | A new VAPID pair: the private key goes to the vault at `path` (`#private_key`); `201 {publicKey, privateKeyRef}` |
| `GET …/deliveries?provider&outcome&channel&user&since&before&limit` | The delivery log, newest first (`limit` ≤ 500): `{deliveries: [{id, tenantId, userId, user: {username, name}, notificationId, deviceId, providerId, providerKind, channel: push\|websocket, kind, outcome: sent\|failed\|dropped\|suppressed\|retrying\|waiting, status, reason, latencyMs, attempt, test, createdAt}], keepDays: 30}`. The platform's log lists attempts through platform providers; a tenant's, its own. Never a token, a credential or a notification's text |
| `GET /api/push/web-config` | Any signed-in member: `{publicKey, providerId}` of the tenant's Web Push provider, else the platform's; `404` without one |

Config by kind (every `…Ref` is a `vault:<path>#<key>` reference):

- `apns`: `{auth: token, keyRef, keyId, teamId, topic, environment: production|sandbox}` or `{auth: certificate,
  certificateRef, certificateKeyRef, topic, environment}`.
- `fcm`: `{serviceAccountRef, projectId?}` (the project from the key's `project_id` when unset).
- `webpush`: `{publicKey, privateKeyRef, subject: mailto:…|https://…}`.
- `http`: `{url, method: POST|PUT, auth: {type: none} | {type: bearer, tokenRef} | {type: header, header, valueRef} |
  {type: basic, username?|usernameRef?, passwordRef}, headers?, body, contentType?, response?: {success, retry, gone},
  timeoutMs?}`. `body` and the URL's path and query take `{title} {body} {data} {token} {collapseId} {ttl} {priority}
  {route} {kind} {link}` (a JSON value in the body, percent-encoded in the URL). Each response rule is `{status: [codes or
  "500-599"], pointer?, equals?}`; "token gone" is tried first, then retry, then success; defaults `gone` 404 and 410,
  `retry` 429 and 5xx, `success` 2xx.
- `websocket`: `{mode: socketio, ackTimeoutMs?}` (the console's socket; default 5000 ms) or `{mode: external, url:
  wss://…, auth?, headers?, body, response?, timeoutMs?}` (one message sent, the first reply mapped like an HTTP answer).
- Every kind takes `contentLabel: public|internal` (default `public`): a notification labelled above it is sent with a
  neutral title and no body.

### Delivery

`Notifications.notify` queues `push.deliver` per stored notification (its `push` input takes `collapseId`, `ttlSeconds`,
`priority`; `urgent` raises priority to high). With an enabled Socket.IO provider and the person online, the console's
sockets get `push.notification {deliveryId, notification}` with an acknowledgement (or `push.ack {deliveryId}`); with no
acknowledgement in `ackTimeoutMs`, `push.fallback` pushes. The push channel asks `notificationPrefs.decide` (a digest is
collected, a suppression logged) and queues one `push.send` per active device. 429 and 5xx retry at `Retry-After` or
an exponential backoff, at most 5 attempts and never past the time to live; APNs 410 or `BadDeviceToken`, FCM
`UNREGISTERED` or `INVALID_ARGUMENT` on the token and a mapped "token gone" call `pushDevices.markGone`. The log is
swept after 30 days (`push.deliveries.sweep`, hourly). Metrics: `exprsn_push_deliveries_total{kind, provider, outcome}`
and the histogram `exprsn_push_send_seconds{kind, provider}`.

CLI: `exprsn-ai push:test --user <username> [--kind <kind>] [--tenant <slug>]` (exit 2 when nothing was sent).

## Sprint 49 (1.9.0, Unreleased): push devices and notification preferences (B-150, B-153)

Migrations `115_push_devices` and `116_notification_preferences`. Push providers, delivery and the delivery log
(B-151, B-152) are documented with their own section.

### Devices (B-150, `platform/push-devices.ts`, `routes/push-devices.ts`)

A device is an endpoint a person registered: `platform` (`ios`, `android`, `web`, `desktop`), `provider` (`apns`,
`fcm`, `webpush`, `http`, `websocket`; APNs serves `ios` and `desktop`, Web Push `web` and `desktop`, FCM `android`,
`ios` and `web`), `appId` (app or bundle id), `name`, and the token or Web Push subscription, sealed with the tenant
key. No answer carries the token: a device is `{id, platform, provider, appId, name, fingerprint, state: active |
revoked | gone, reason, createdAt, lastSeenAt, endedAt, current}` (`fingerprint` is `xxxx:xxxx:xxxx`, 12 hex digits of
a digest of the token or the subscription's endpoint; `current`: registered from this session).

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /me/devices` | `{devices}`: the caller's devices, active first, then those ended in the last 30 days |
| `POST /me/devices` `{platform, provider, appId?, name?, token? \| subscription?}` | Registers a device: `201`. The same token again (same provider and app id) updates its row (`200`: session, name if given, the sealed value, `lastSeenAt`); an ended device becomes active again; another person's device moves to the caller. `token`: 8 to 4096 printable characters (all kinds but `webpush`); `subscription`: `{endpoint (https), keys: {p256dh (65-byte P-256 point), auth (16 bytes)}, expirationTime?}`, base64url (`webpush` only). `409` past 50 active devices |
| `PATCH /me/devices/:id` `{name}` | Renames one of the caller's devices |
| `DELETE /me/devices/:id` | Revokes it (`state: revoked`, the sealed token cleared) |
| `GET /admin/users/:id/devices` (`users:manage`) | A person's devices, for an identity or tenant admin; the person must be in the admin's tenant |
| `DELETE /admin/users/:id/devices/:deviceId` (`users:manage`) | Revokes one of them |

Devices end with the person's sessions: `SessionService.revokeAllForUser` (signing out everywhere else, password change
or reset, an admin disabling the account or changing its access, SCIM or directory deactivation, a sanction) revokes
them, except those registered from the session that is kept; revoking one session (including signing out) revokes the
devices registered from it; disabling or offboarding a tenant revokes all of its devices, and the offboarding purge
deletes the rows. A rotated session keeps its devices. The `push.devices.prune` job (daily, per tenant) deletes devices
not seen for `PUSH_DEVICE_IDLE_DAYS` (default 90; 0 turns it off) and ended rows 30 days after they ended.

For delivery (B-152), not HTTP: `s.pushDevices.forDelivery(tenantId, userId)` returns the active devices with the
opened token (`token`, or `subscription` for Web Push); `s.pushDevices.markGone(deviceId, reason)` ends one a provider
reported gone.

Audit: `push.device.registered` (a new device, a reactivated or moved one, or a changed platform or name; an unchanged
re-registration is not audited), `push.device.renamed`, `push.device.revoked` (`detail.reason`; one entry per tenant
with `count` and `devices` when sessions end), `push.device.gone`, `push.device.pruned`.

### Notification preferences (B-153, `platform/notification-kinds.ts`, `platform/notification-prefs.ts`, `routes/notification-prefs.ts`)

Preferences are kept per catalogue kind (`NOTIFICATION_KINDS`: id, title, description, group). A raw notification
kind maps to the entry with its id, else the longest entry id it starts with followed by a dot (`group.member` →
`group`), else `other`. Channels: `in_app`, `email`, `push`, `websocket`; timing: `instant`, `hourly`, `daily`,
`weekly`. `security` (security alerts, including sign-in from a new device and account changes an administrator made)
is mandatory everywhere.

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /me/notification-preferences` | `{saved, timeZone, quietHours: {mon…sun: {start, end} \| null}, urgentPassesQuiet, digestHour, digestWeekday, channels, timings, kinds: [{id, title, description, group, mandatory, lockedBy: platform \| tenant \| null, lockedReason, channels: {<channel>: {enabled, timing, source: mandatory \| you \| tenant \| default}}}]}` |
| `PUT /me/notification-preferences` `{timeZone?, quietHours?, urgentPassesQuiet?, digestHour?, digestWeekday?, kinds?: {<kind>: {<channel>: {enabled, timing} \| null} \| null}}` | Saves what is given; `null` for a channel or kind follows the tenant default again. `timeZone` is an IANA zone; quiet hours are `HH:MM`, a window ending before it starts runs past midnight. `409` (`kinds`) when a mandatory kind would be turned off or delayed; `400` for an unknown kind |
| `DELETE /me/notification-preferences` | Back to the tenant defaults |
| `GET /admin/notification-defaults` (`tenant:manage`) | `{channels, timings, kinds: [{id, title, description, group, locked, lockedReason, mandatory, channels: {<channel>: {enabled, timing, source: tenant \| default}}}]}` |
| `PUT /admin/notification-defaults` (`tenant:manage`) `{kinds: {<kind>: {mandatory?, channels?: {<channel>: {enabled, timing} \| null}} \| null}}` | Sets the tenant's defaults and mandatory kinds; `null` removes the kind's row. `409` when security alerts would be made optional |

The decision, `s.notificationPrefs.decide(tenantId, userId, kind, channel, {urgent, at})` →
`{deliver: now | digest | suppressed, reason: mandatory | instant | urgent | quiet_hours | digest | off | digest_summary, kind, digest?: {period: hourly | daily | weekly | quiet, dueAt}}`:
a mandatory kind goes now; then the person's choice, the tenant default or the built-in default (in-app and email on
and instant; push and WebSocket on for people's own matters); off is `suppressed`; in quiet hours (push, WebSocket and
email, never the in-app inbox) an urgent notification passes when `urgentPassesQuiet`, others wait for the end of the
window; a digest timing waits for its next period in the person's time zone, moved past quiet hours. `decideMany`
answers a fan-out; both read caches of 30 seconds dropped on every instance when preferences change. `Notifications.notify`
asks it for in-app and, when the sender asks for email, for email; `urgent` on `notify` marks an urgent notification.
With no preferences and no tenant defaults every answer is `now`, as before. Delivery (B-152) asks it for push and
WebSocket and calls `s.notificationPrefs.collect(item, decision)` for a `digest` answer.

Held notifications (`notification_digest_items`, the title sealed) are sent by the `notifications.digest` job every
`NOTIFICATION_DIGEST_MINUTES` (default 5; 0 turns it off): per person, one in-app summary (kind
`notification.digest`, labelled the highest label of its items) for in-app, push and WebSocket items, and one email
(template `notification-digest`, titles only, and not even those of items labelled above `internal`) for email items.

Audit: `notification.prefs.updated` (`detail.settings`, `detail.kinds`: what changed, not the values),
`notification.prefs.reset`, `notification.defaults.updated` (`detail.kinds`, `detail.mandatory`).

### Notification templates (1.9.0, Unreleased; `platform/notification-templates.ts`, migration `132_notification_templates`)

A template is a named, versioned preference set of the tenant: a choice per kind and channel, optional quiet hours
with "urgent passes", the digest hour and weekday, and a description. Tenant admins manage them under `tenant:manage`,
the permission of the tenant defaults. Applying one writes its choices as each person's own preferences (what
`PUT /me/notification-preferences` saves), so people customise afterwards in Settings. `replace` removes the person's
kind choices first and sets quiet hours, "urgent passes" and digest times to the template's (built-in values where it
sets none); the time zone is kept. `fill` sets only the kinds the person has not chosen, and the settings only when
they have none saved (quiet hours when they have none). Mandatory kinds (locked, or made mandatory by the tenant) are
never turned off or delayed: saving such a template is refused (`409`, `kinds`), and applying skips them
(`skippedKinds`). One template may be the default for new members: every account created in the tenant
(`UserRepo.create`, after its transaction commits) gets it in `fill` mode. Without the migration's tables the list
answers `available: false`, the other routes `503` (`reason: migration_pending`), and nothing else changes.

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /admin/notification-templates` (`tenant:manage`) | `{available, templates: [{id, name, description, version, defaultForNewMembers, kinds: {<kind>: {<channel>: {enabled, timing}}}, quietHours, urgentPassesQuiet, digestHour, digestWeekday, people, createdBy, updatedBy, createdAt, updatedAt}], targets: {roles: [role ids held in the tenant], groups: [{id, name}]}}` |
| `POST /admin/notification-templates` (`tenant:manage`) `{name, description?, kinds, quietHours?, urgentPassesQuiet?, digestHour?, digestWeekday?, defaultForNewMembers?}` | `201` with the template and `versions`. `409` for a name in use or a mandatory kind turned off or delayed (`kinds`); setting `defaultForNewMembers` clears it on the others |
| `GET /admin/notification-templates/{id}` (`tenant:manage`) | The template, `people` (how many are based on it) and `versions: [{version, name, createdBy, createdAt}]` |
| `PATCH /admin/notification-templates/{id}` (`tenant:manage`) | Any of the create fields; a change of name, description or body makes a new version (`defaultForNewMembers` alone does not). `409` as for create |
| `DELETE /admin/notification-templates/{id}` (`tenant:manage`) | Deletes it and its versions; people keep the preferences it wrote and are no longer "based on" it |
| `POST /admin/notification-templates/{id}/apply` (`tenant:manage`) `{mode: replace \| fill, target: {kind: users, userIds?, usernames?} \| {kind: role, role} \| {kind: group, groupId} \| {kind: everyone}, dryRun?}` | `{template: {id, name, version}, mode, dryRun, target, people, changedPeople, changedKinds, skippedKinds, unknown}`. A role, group or everyone reaches active accounts only; `400` when none of the named people is in the tenant, `404` for an unknown group. `dryRun` counts without writing |

`GET /me/notification-preferences` adds `template: {id, name, version, currentVersion, mode, appliedAt, changedKinds} | null`:
the template the person's preferences were last applied from, its version then and now (`null` once deleted), and how
many kinds the person changed since. `DELETE /me/notification-preferences` clears it.

Audit: `notification.template.created`, `.updated` (`detail.version`, `detail.previousVersion`, `detail.changed`),
`.deleted` (`detail.people`), `.applied` (`detail.mode`, `detail.target`, `detail.people`, `detail.changedPeople`,
`detail.changedKinds`, `detail.skippedKinds`; `target: new-member` with `kind: system` for a new member).

## Sprint 48 (1.8.0, Unreleased): security scans as a promotion gate, and the emergency vault seal (B-144, B-145)

Migrations `107_security_scans` and `108_vault_seal`.

### Security scan results and the gate (B-144, `security/scans.ts`, `security/scan-formats.ts`)

A result is attached to one artefact by its digest and applies to nothing else: an app package (`app-package`,
`sha256:<package hash>`), a plugin bundle (`plugin-bundle`, the bundle digest, or `sha256:<manifestHash>` for an
inline manifest) or a script runner image (`script-image`, the image's `sha256:` digest). Reading and uploading need
the kind's permission: `apps:design`, `plugins:manage` or `platform:manage`. The tenant is the caller's.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `PUT /admin/security/scans/upload?kind=&digest=&ref=&format=&scannedAt=` | The raw report as the body (up to 16 MB): Trivy JSON, SARIF 2.1.0 or a CycloneDX JSON SBOM, detected unless `format` is given. `digest` may be left out when the report names it (Trivy `RepoDigests`, a CycloneDX component hash). `scannedAt` (epoch ms) overrides the report's time. 201 with the result's summary; 422 for a report that is none of the three; 404 for an app package digest the tenant does not have. Audited `security.scan.uploaded`. A CI hook uses an API key with the kind's permission |
| `GET /admin/security/scans?kind=&digest=&limit=` | `{kinds, results}`: newest first, only the kinds the caller may read and within clearance |
| `GET /admin/security/scans/:id` | One result with its normalised `findings`: `{kind, severity, id, package, version, fixedVersion, licence, path, title}` |
| `DELETE /admin/security/scans/:id` | `platform:manage`, recent sign-in. Audited `security.scan.deleted` |
| `GET /admin/security/policy` | `{maxCritical, maxHigh, maxAgeDays, missing, licenceDeny, version, kinds, trivyMirrors}`. Default: `maxCritical: 0`, `maxHigh: null` (no limit), any age, `missing: 'warn'`, no denied licences |
| `PUT /admin/security/policy` | `platform:manage`, recent sign-in. The whole policy; `missing` is `warn` (allow with a warning) or `refuse`; `licenceDeny` SPDX ids. Audited `security.scan.policy.updated` with before and after |
| `POST /admin/security/gate` `{kind, digest, ref?}` | What the gate would decide now, writing nothing |
| `GET /admin/security/gate/pipelines/:id?to=test\|production&package=` | `apps:design`: the gate for the package a promotion would carry (the promotion dialog's preview); `newPackage: true` when a promotion to test would build a new, unscanned package |
| `GET /admin/security/exceptions?state=` | Exceptions with who requested and who accepted them |
| `POST /admin/security/exceptions` `{findingId, package?, kind?, digest?, reason, expiresAt}` | Requests one (pending). `findingId` is a CVE, rule or misconfiguration id, or `licence:<SPDX>`; at most 365 days; without `kind` it covers every kind and needs `platform:manage`. Audited `security.scan.exception.requested` |
| `POST /admin/security/exceptions/:id/approve` `{note?}` | `platform:manage`, recent sign-in, someone other than the requester (403 `dual-control`); the approver is who accepted it. Audited `.approved` |
| `POST /admin/security/exceptions/:id/reject`, `/withdraw` (the requester), `/revoke` (`platform:manage`, ends an active one) | Audited `.rejected`, `.withdrawn`, `.revoked` |

The gate counts the latest result of each format for the digest that is not older than `maxAgeDays` (none fresh:
refused); refuses more critical or high findings than allowed (licence findings do not count there), less those an
active, unexpired exception accepts; refuses a component under a denied licence (`A OR B` only when every alternative
is denied); and without any result allows with a warning or refuses, per `missing`. It runs at:

- `POST /apps/pipelines/:id/promote` (to test and to production) and again when the deployment job runs (an approval
  may take long). A refusal is `409 Security gate refused` with `step: 'security-gate'` and `gate` (the outcome:
  `outcome`, `reasons`, `warnings`, `results`, `counts`, `blocking`, `excepted`); the blocking findings are also listed
