  in `detail`. A successful promotion's answer carries `gate`. New: `packageId` in the body promotes that package of
  the development app to test (the exact one a result names) instead of building a new one. Rollbacks are not gated;
- `POST /admin/plugins/:id/enable`, and installing another version over a removed one (an upgrade);
- `POST /admin/platform/settings/SCRIPT_IMAGE_*/proposals` and their approval: a result matches only an image named
  as `<repository>@sha256:…`; a tag counts as no result.

Each run is audited `security.gate.passed`, `security.gate.warned` or `security.gate.blocked` with where it ran
(`pipeline.promote`, `pipeline.deploy`, `plugin.enable`, `plugin.upgrade`, `script-image`).

### The emergency vault seal (B-145, `vault/seal.ts`)

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /admin/platform/vault/seal` | `platform:manage`: `{sealed, kms, sealable, problem, escrow: {id, threshold, shares, keyCheck, matchesRunningKey}, last, proposals, signerSealed}` |
| `POST /admin/platform/vault/seal/proposals` `{reason}` | `platform:manage`, recent sign-in. Refused (409) without an escrow of the running key, with OpenBao, or while another proposal waits. Expires after an hour. Audited `vault.seal.proposed` |
| `POST /admin/platform/vault/seal/proposals/:id/approve` `{note?}` | `platform:manage`, recent sign-in, not the proposer (403 `dual-control`): the seal fires on every instance. Audited `vault.seal.approved`, `vault.sealed` |
| `POST /admin/platform/vault/seal/proposals/:id/reject`, `/withdraw` | Audited `vault.seal.rejected`, `vault.seal.withdrawn` |
| `GET /public/vault/seal` | Public: `{sealed, instance}`; while sealed also `since`, `mode`, `escrow: {id, threshold, shares}` and this instance's `progress: {submitted, needed}` |
| `POST /public/vault/unseal` `{share}` | Public (the share is the credential; 10 a minute per address; same origin). One escrow share; at the threshold the vault is unsealed (`{sealed: false}`). 422 for a share that is malformed, mistyped or of another escrow. Audited `vault.unseal.share`, `vault.unseal.share.refused`, `vault.unseal.failed`, `vault.unsealed` |
| `POST /public/vault/unseal/reset` | Forgets the shares given so far on this instance. Audited `vault.unseal.reset` |
| `POST /public/vault/break-glass` `{shares, reason}` | Public: the threshold of shares together seal at once. Audited `vault.seal.break-glass` (or `.refused`), `vault.sealed` |

While sealed every other route answers `503 Vault sealed` (`step: 'vault-sealed'`, `sealed: true`, `unseal:
'/unseal.html'`, `Retry-After: 30`), except `/healthz`, `/readyz` (with `checks.vault: 'sealed'`), `/metrics`, the
console's static files and `GET /auth/session`, which answers `{authenticated: false, stage: null, sealed: true}`.
CLI: `exprsn-ai vault:seal-status`, `vault:unseal [--share …] [--check <kcv>] [--signer-only]`, `vault:seal
--break-glass --reason <text> [--share …]`. The signer protocol gains `seal`, `unseal` and `seal-status`
(`signer/protocol.ts`). Procedure: [runbooks/emergency-seal.md](runbooks/emergency-seal.md).

## Sprint 48 (1.8.0, Unreleased): plugin creator, Overview cards, knowledge feedback and page tree (B-147 to B-149)

Migrations `109_plugin_drafts`, `110_overview_prefs` and `111_knowledge_feedback_tree`. Every route takes the tenant
from the session, validates its input with zod, fails with problem+json and audits every change.

### Plugin creator (B-147, `plugins/drafts.ts`)

All need `plugins:manage` (the permission that installs plugins). A draft is its author's: another admin gets 404.
A draft is data; the server builds a manifest from it and checks it with `validateManifest` (including
`surfaceProblems`), and never loads or runs anything from it.

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/admin/plugin-drafts/vocabulary` | The capability vocabulary with plain-language help, risk, events and calls; the required/optional and grants explanations; surface slots and block types; domain calls; declarative actions; event groups and types; handler kinds; the signing policy (`PLUGINS_REQUIRE_SIGNED`) |
| POST | `/api/admin/plugin-drafts/check` | `{wizard}` → `{manifest, valid, problems: [{step, message}]}`; saves nothing. A step is 1 basics, 2 capabilities, 3 surfaces, 4 events and handler |
| GET | `/api/admin/plugin-drafts` | The caller's drafts, each with its built manifest and problems |
| POST | `/api/admin/plugin-drafts` | `{wizard?}` → 201 a draft (at most 50 a person). Audited `plugin.draft.created` |
| GET | `/api/admin/plugin-drafts/:id` | One draft: `{id, name, key, step, wizard, pluginId, manifest, valid, problems}` |
| PUT | `/api/admin/plugin-drafts/:id` | `{wizard?, step? (1 to 5)}`. Audited `plugin.draft.saved` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/plugin-drafts/:id` | 204. A plugin installed from it stays. Audited `plugin.draft.deleted` |
| GET | `/api/admin/plugin-drafts/:id/download?format=bundle\|manifest` | An unsigned import bundle (`manifest.json` in `exprsn-bundle/1` listing `files/plugins/<key>.json`, mirror `plugins`; sign `manifest.json` offline and add `manifest.sig` as the second entry before importing) or the plugin file. 422 when the draft does not validate. Audited `plugin.draft.exported` with the file's sha256 |
| POST | `/api/admin/plugin-drafts/:id/install` | `{maxLabel?, reason?}` → 201 the plugin, in the state `installed` with **no** grants: grant and enable it through `/api/admin/plugins/:id/grants` and `/enable` as for any install. The signing policy applies (a script plugin is 409 under `PLUGINS_REQUIRE_SIGNED=scripts`). Audited `plugin.draft.installed` (and `plugin.installed`) |

The wizard (`wizardSchema`, strict): `basics {name, key, description, version, publisher}`, `capabilities[]`,
`optional[]` (a subset), `surfaces[]` (the manifest's `ui` entries), `events[]`, `handler` (`{type: none}`,
`{type: actions, actions: [{type, on?, with?}]}`, `{type: webhook, url}` or `{type: script, language?, entry?,
source?}`; a script without a source gets a skeleton that logs each event and names the calls its capabilities allow),
`config?` (a JSON Schema).

### Overview cards (B-148, `ops/overview-cards.ts`)

`tenant:manage` or `platform:manage`, as the Overview. Each card also needs its own: `instances` and `capacity`
platform administration, `audit` `audit:read`, `workflows-running` `workflows:manage`, `sla-breaching` the review
permission of at least one queue type, `revisions-waiting` `knowledge:read`; `alerts`, `counters`, `schedules`,
`plugins` and `approvals-pending` (only approvals the caller may decide) need nothing more.

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/admin/overview-cards` | The caller's layout over the cards they may see: `{cards: [{id, title, description, optional, pinned, hidden}], density, saved, updatedAt, visible}`; pinned first, optional cards start hidden |
| PUT | `/api/admin/overview-cards` | `{order, pinned?, hidden?, density?: comfortable\|compact}`; an unknown id is 400, a card the caller may not see 403 (`cards`). Audited `overview.cards.updated` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/overview-cards` | Back to the default layout. Audited `overview.cards.reset` |
| GET | `/api/admin/overview-cards/data?cards=a,b` | Figures of the optional cards named that the caller may see (others are not computed): `workflows-running {running, waiting, items}`, `sla-breaching {warning, breached, byType}`, `approvals-pending {count, items}`, `revisions-waiting {count, decidable, items}` |

### Knowledge feedback and the page tree (B-149, `knowledge/feedback.ts`, `knowledge/tree.ts`)

Every route needs `knowledge:read`; the services apply the base's own access on top.

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/knowledge/feedback` | `{target, helpful, comment?, shareQuestion?}` → 201. `target` is `{kind: document, id}`, `{kind: reference, id}` or `{kind: citation, conversationId, messageId, n}` (a knowledge citation of an answer in the caller's own conversation; the cited document must still be readable). The comment passes the `user-input` guardrail (422 `step: guardrails` on a block or hold; a redaction is kept) and is sealed; `shareQuestion` keeps the question asked, sealed, for the eval seed. One answer per person and target (a reference's document counts as the reference): answering again replaces it. Audited `knowledge.feedback.given` or `.changed` |
| GET | `/api/knowledge/feedback/mine?document=\|reference=\|conversation=&message=&n=` | The caller's own answer about a target, or `mine: null` |
| DELETE | `/api/knowledge/feedback/:id` | Withdraws one of the caller's answers. Audited `knowledge.feedback.withdrawn` |
| GET | `/api/knowledge/bases/:id/feedback` | Editors and curators of the base (403 otherwise): totals, per page `{up, down, helpfulness, comments, recentNegative, lastNegativeAt}` and the curation list (at least 3 answers and under 50% helpful, or a negative comment in the last 30 days), over the pages the caller can read now |
| GET | `/api/knowledge/bases/:id/feedback/comments?document=\|reference=` | Editors and curators: the answers about one page with their comments, newest first |
| GET | `/api/knowledge/bases/:id/feedback/eval-seed` | Editors and curators: `{seed, cases, use}`; `seed` has the shape of `POST /api/admin/profiles/:id/eval-sets` (`evalSetBody`): one judge-rubric case per negative answer with a comment or a shared question, `gate: false`, `judgeProfile: null` to be set. Audited `knowledge.feedback.exported` |
| GET | `/api/knowledge/bases/:id/tree` | The references the caller can read as nodes `{id, slug, title, state, version, label, parentId, position, children}`; a parent the caller cannot read shows as `parentId: null` |
| GET | `/api/knowledge/references/:id/tree` | `{breadcrumbs, children, links, backlinks}` of a reference, readable ones only. Links (`[[slug]]`, `[[slug\|text]]`, `[text](slug)`) are written when a revision publishes |
| PUT | `/api/knowledge/references/:id/tree` | `{parentId: id\|null, position?}`: editors of the base. 409 for a move under itself or one of its descendants; the base's moves are serialised. Audited `knowledge.reference.moved` with before and after |

## Sprint 48 (1.8.0, Unreleased): app-local roles and use-limited credentials (B-143, B-146)

Migrations `105_app_roles` (`app_roles`, `app_role_members`) and `106_credential_use_limits` (`max_uses` and
`uses_left` on `api_keys`, `vault_leases` and `app_embed_sessions`). `apps/roles.ts` (`s.apps.roles`) behind
`routes/apps-roles.ts` (inside the apps router); console `web/js/screens/apps-roles.js` (the Roles tab).

### App-local roles (B-143)

Each app keeps its own role catalogue: a name (1 to 63 letters, digits, spaces, `_ . -`) unique per app without regard
to case, and an optional description; at most 100 roles. A role is held by a person (`user`), a social group
(`group`: its members while `s.groups.subjects` counts them, so not banned, suspended or gone, and within their
clearance) or every member of a workspace (`workspace`, the default role; for a workspace app only its own workspace).
Row and field policies name a role with the subject `{kind: app_role, value: <name>}`; `grantFor` reads the reader's
roles only when a policy of the entity names one. A role is only a policy subject: it does not make the app visible,
gives nothing on an entity without policies, and never passes `records:read`/`records:write` or the reader's
clearance. Every route needs `apps:design` and the app's label within the caller's clearance; no tenant permission is
asked, because what a role can do is bounded by the policies the same designers write.

Packages (`exprsn-app/2`) carry `roles: [{name, description}]` (absent when the app has none, so older packages still
verify) and lay them out as `roles/NNN-<name>.json` for git; never the assignments, which belong to each environment.
Import and deployment create the package's roles before its policies; a deployment removes the roles the package no
longer has (with their assignments) after the policies are replaced, and reports `roles: {created, updated, removed}`.
A package whose policy names a role it does not carry is refused. The platform importer reads the app's AppRoles from
`/lowcode/api/security/roles` when the platform serves them and creates the missing ones by name (their permissions
and holders are reported as dropped).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/apps/:app/roles` | `apps:design`. `{roles: [{id, name, description, members: [{id, kind: user \| group \| workspace, subjectId, name, createdBy, createdAt}], policies: [{id, name, enabled, entity, rows, fields, otherFields}], createdBy, updatedBy, createdAt, updatedAt}]}`: the catalogue, who holds each role and what the policies naming it allow |
| `GET /api/apps/:app/roles/candidates?q&limit` | `apps:design`. `{people: [{id, username, displayName}]}`: active users of the app's workspace (the tenant's, for a tenant-wide app) matching `q`, for the person picker |
| `POST /api/apps/:app/roles` `{name, description?}` | `apps:design`. `201` the role; `409` for a name the app has. Audited `app.role.created` |
| `PATCH /api/apps/:app/roles/:id` `{name?, description?}` | `apps:design`. A rename also renames the role in the policies that name it, in one transaction. Audited `app.role.updated` (with `from` and `policies` on a rename) |
| `DELETE /api/apps/:app/roles/:id` | `apps:design`. `204`; the role and its assignments go. `409 Role in use` with `policies` while a policy names it. Audited `app.role.deleted` |
| `POST /api/apps/:app/roles/:id/members` `{kind, id?, username?}` | `apps:design`. `kind` is `user` (by `id` or `username`), `group` or `workspace` (by `id`). `201 {id, roleId, kind, subjectId, createdAt}`. `422` for an unknown user, a group the designer cannot see, or an unknown workspace; `403 step: workspace` for a group or workspace outside a workspace app's own; `409` when already held. Audited `app.role.assigned` |
| `DELETE /api/apps/:app/roles/:id/members/:member` | `apps:design`. `204`. Audited `app.role.unassigned` |

`POST /api/apps/:app/policies` and `PUT .../policies/:id` answer `422 Unknown app role` for an `app_role` subject the
catalogue lacks. `POST /api/apps/:app/entities/:entity/policies/explain` adds `user.appRoles: [{key, name, via:
[{kind, id}]}]`, `policies[].appRole` (the role, and how it is held, when the matching subject is one),
`record.byRole` and `field.byRole` (the app role through which the deciding policy names the user).

### Use-limited credentials (B-146)

`POST /api/me/api-keys` and `POST /api/admin/agent-identities/:name/keys` take `maxUses` (1 to 1000000, or null for no
limit); `1` is a one-shot key for an embed or an agent task. The answers, `GET /api/me/api-keys` and the agent
identity's key list show `maxUses` and `usesLeft`. Each accepted use is spent by one conditional update (`uses_left >
0`): on the key's row for `exai_k1_`, on its lease for `exai_k2_` (`GenericLeases.spend`), so parallel requests on any
number of instances never pass the limit. A use is spent when the key authenticates, before scope, app and signature
checks, so a refused request counts too. The last use is answered; the key is then revoked through `ApiKeyService`
(its record, then its lease), audited `apikey.exhausted` (`actor: identity.api-keys`, `detail: {maxUses, store}`) and
its owner sent the security notice "An API key used its last allowed use and was revoked". After that the key is
`401 invalid_token`. A key without a limit makes no extra query or write.

A host token exchanged at `POST /api/public/embeds/session` may carry `max_uses` (a whole number from 1 to 100000,
else `401 invalid_token`): the embedded session answers that many requests, then is revoked and audited
`app.embed.session.exhausted`.

## Sprint 47 (1.8.0, Unreleased): workflow templates, schedules with a time zone, workflow analytics (B-136, B-138, B-139)

Migrations `094_workflow_templates`, `095_workflow_analytics_indexes` and `096_workflow_schedule_timezone`. Routes in
`routes/workflow-builders.ts`. They use the workflow permissions: `agents:run` (members; what reading a workflow and
its run history needs) to browse templates, list presets, preview schedules and read analytics; `workflows:manage`
(workflow admins, who create workflows) to bind, use, save, change and delete templates. Tenant and workspace come
from the session; every change is audited; errors are problem+json.

### Templates (B-136)

A template is a workflow graph (what an `exprsn-workflow/1` bundle carries) with `name`, `title`, `summary`,
`category`, `tags`, `icon`, `version` (semver), `label` and `needs` (`{tools, profiles, apps, decisions, roles,
connections, knowledge, vault}`: the names the graph references). Six built-in starters ship as data
(`workflows/template-catalog.ts`, seeded by migration 094): `lead-follow-up`, `invoice-approval`, `weekly-report`,
`new-starter-onboarding`, `webhook-to-record`, `document-intake`. A tenant template is saved from a workflow, in that
workflow's workspace (or tenant-wide), at its label. A caller sees the built-ins and their tenant's templates of their
workspace or tenant-wide, at or below their clearance (others are `404`).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workflow-templates?q&category&tag&scope=builtin\|tenant` | `{items: [{id, name, title, summary, category, tags, icon, version, label, builtIn, workspaceId, steps, trigger, needs, uses, sourceWorkflow, createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt}], categories: [{name, count}], tags: [{name, count}], total}`. `q` matches every word in title, summary, name, category and tags |
| `GET /api/workflow-templates/:id` | One template (by id or name) with its `graph`, for the preview |
| `GET /api/workflow-templates/options` | What each kind of reference can be bound to here: `{tools, profiles, apps, decisions, roles, connections, knowledge, vault}`, each `[{value, label}]` (published tools callable here, published profiles within clearance, apps in reach, published decision tables, built-in roles, published read-only saved queries, knowledge bases the caller manages) |
| `POST /api/workflow-templates/:id/check` | `{bindings?}` (`{tools, profiles, apps, vault, decisions, roles, connections, knowledge}`, each a map of the template's name to yours; knowledge bases bind to an id). `{template, bindings: [{kind, from, to, status: bound \| missing \| on publish, detail}], missing, options}` |
| `POST /api/workflow-templates/:id/use` | `{name, label?, bindings?}`. Creates a draft in the current workspace through the bundle import path (`WorkflowBundles.instantiate`) with every reference re-bound: `201 {workflow, template, bindings, missing}`. A missing reference does not stop the draft; publishing checks every reference again. `label` is at least the template's (`422`); a taken name is `409`. Audited `workflow.template.used` (template, version, built in, missing) |
| `POST /api/workflow-templates` | Save as template: `{workflow, name, title, summary, category, tags?, icon?, version? = 1.0.0}`. The workflow's published version (or the draft), decision steps by table name, at the workflow's label. `201` with the template; `409` for a taken name. Audited `workflow.template.saved` |
| `PATCH /api/workflow-templates/:id` | `{title?, summary?, category?, tags?, icon?, version?, refresh?}`; `refresh: true` takes the source workflow's graph again and raises the minor version unless `version` is given. Built-ins are `403`. Audited `workflow.template.updated` |
| `DELETE /api/workflow-templates/:id` | `204`; built-ins are `403`. Audited `workflow.template.deleted` |

### Schedules with a time zone (B-138)

A `schedule` trigger takes `timezone` (an IANA zone; absent is UTC, so earlier schedules fire exactly as before) beside
`cron` (`workflows/schedules.ts`). The cron also reads month and day names, `L`, `LW` and `15W` in the day of the month
and `1#2` in the day of the week. When clocks go forward a schedule that names the hour runs once at the jump, and when
they go back once at the first occurrence; a schedule whose hour is `*` keeps its pace. The trigger row keeps the zone
(`workflow_triggers.timezone`), `GET /api/workflows/:id/triggers` shows it with a reading in plain words, and the tick
still claims each due time with one conditional update. Publishing refuses an unknown zone or a cron that never runs,
with the reason.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workflow-schedules/presets` | `{presets: [{id, title, group, params: [{name, label, min, max, default}], example}]}`: 21 presets (every N minutes, hourly at a minute, every N hours, business hours, daily, twice a day, weekdays, weekends, weekly, monthly, first and last business day, last day, the first chosen weekday, quarterly, yearly…) |
| `POST /api/workflow-schedules/preview` | `{cron \| preset (+ values), timezone = UTC, count = 10 (1 to 50), from?}`. `{cron, timezone, description, runs: [{at, iso, local, offsetMinutes}], notes}` (notes name daylight-saving changes); `422 Schedule not valid` with the reason in plain words |

### Analytics and the running-now board (B-139)

SQL aggregates over `workflow_runs` and `workflow_steps`, bounded by `created_at` (`from` and `to` in ms, or `days`, 30
by default, at most 366) and served by the indexes of migration 095. Only workflows the caller may open, runs at or
below their clearance, dry runs only with `dry=true`, and only the caller's own runs unless they hold
`workflows:manage` (`scope: all runs | your runs`), as in the run history. Days are UTC.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workflow-analytics/:id?from&to&days&dry` | `{workflowId, name, label, range, scope, runs, counts: {queued, running, waiting, succeeded, failed, rejected, cancelled}, finished, successRate, duration: {measured, avgMs, p50Ms, p95Ms}, slowestSteps: [{nodeId, title, kind, runs, avgMs, maxMs}], failingSteps: [{nodeId, title, failures}], failureReasons: [{reason, state, runs, lastAt}], trend: [{day, date, runs, succeeded, failed, other, successRate, avgMs}]}` |
| `GET /api/workflow-analytics?from&to&days&dry` | The tenant summary: the same totals and trend over every workflow the caller may open, and `workflows: [{workflowId, name, label, publishedVersion, runs, succeeded, failed, active, successRate, avgMs}]` |
| `GET /api/workflow-activity?limit&workflow` | Running now: `{at, scope, counts: {queued, running, waiting}, total, items: [{runId, workflowId, workflow, version, mode, state, label, trigger, waitingOn: approval \| wait \| retry \| child \| step \| resume \| null, step: {id, title, kind, state, since}, approval: {role, dueAt, expiresAt}, resumeAt, ageMs, createdAt, startedAt, owner: {id, name}}]}`, oldest first. The console refreshes it on `workflow.run` and `workflow.step` socket events and every 15 seconds |

## Sprint 47 (1.8.0, Unreleased): formula functions; file version compare, alt text, served copies without metadata (B-141, B-142)

Migration `099_file_meta` (alt text and description, one row per file). Tenant and workspace come from the session;
every change is audited; errors are problem+json.

### Formula functions (B-141)

The formula language (`apps/formula.ts`, library in `apps/formula-functions.ts`) has about 70 functions in five
categories, matched case-insensitively. New since 1.8.0: text `Proper`, `Substitute` (with an instance), `Split` (a
list), `Join`, `Find`, `Search`, `Rept`, `Value`, `Char`, `Code`, and `text(value, format, zone)` with a number format
(`0`, `0.00`, `#,##0.00`, `0%`, `$#,##0`) or a date format (`YYYY YY MMMM MMM MM M DDDD DDD DD D HH H hh h mm ss A`);
logic `Switch`, `IfError`, `IsNumeric`, `IsText`; math `Power`, `Sqrt`, `Exp`, `Ln`, `Log`, `RoundUp`, `RoundDown`,
`Mod`, `Sign`, `Clamp`, `Average`, and `min`, `max`, `sum` over lists; dates `DateAdd` and `DateDiff` in seconds,
minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (month ends: 31 January plus a month is the last day of
February), `Hour`, `Minute`, `Second`, `Weekday` (1 is Sunday), `WeekNum` (ISO 8601), `EOMonth`, `NetWorkDays`,
`WorkDay` (holidays as a list), every one in UTC unless an IANA zone is given; lists `List`, `Count`, `CountIf(list,
condition on item)`, `First`, `Last`, `Index`, `Sort`, `Unique`. `Trim` already trims only the ends, so there is no
`TrimEnds`. Each new function's arguments are checked when the formula is saved (count, and the kind of a literal or
of a nested function's result: "Power's first argument is a number; it is given 'x'"); the functions from before
1.8.0 take any argument as they did. Limits: text at 10,000 characters (`Rept` past it is blank, not cut), lists at
10,000 items, and work in proportion to the input counts toward the 20,000-step budget. A formula whose value is a
list gives it as text joined by `, `. A field holding a JSON array of scalars reads as a list (an array holding
objects reads as null, as before).

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/apps/formula-functions` | `apps:design` or `records:read`. The catalogue the formula editor lists: `{functions: [{name, call, category, signature, description, example, minArgs, maxArgs}], maxLength}` |
| `POST /api/apps/formula-check` `{expression, fields}` | `apps:design` or `records:read`. Parses the expression against the field names given, as an entity save does: `{ok: true, refs}` or `{ok: false, message}` (always `200`; `400` for a body that is not valid) |

### Version compare (B-142)

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/files/:id/compare?from=&to=` | Members of the file's workspace cleared for both versions (as for downloading a version). Text, Markdown, CSV, JSON (one-line JSON spread out), HTML, PDF and Word (text extracted as `files.read` does): `{kind: text, file, from, to, added, removed, same, truncated, extracted, hunks: [{fromStart, fromCount, toStart, toCount, lines: [{op: ' ' \| '-' \| '+', text}]}]}` through `textDiff`. Images: `{kind: image, file, from, to, same}`, each side with its `preview` state. `413 Too large to compare` past 4 MB a version, 1,000,000 characters or 20,000 lines of text (`extensions.limits`); `415` for other types or an image beside a text; `409` for a version that has not passed its scan; `400` for the same version twice. Audited `file.versions.compared` |
| `GET /api/files/:id/versions/:n/preview` | Version `n`'s preview (members of the workspace, as for its content); `/api/files/:id/preview` stays the current version's for every reader |

### Alt text and description (B-142)

Per file, not per version: the picture's text is kept when a new version replaces it, with `altVersion` the version
it was written for. Only images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF). `GET /api/files/:id` gives `altText`, `description`,
`altVersion`, `altUpdatedAt` and `owner` (whether the caller owns the file); `GET /api/files/search?q=` matches the
name, the alt text or the description.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `PUT /api/files/:id/meta` `{altText?, description?}` | `files:write`, a member of the workspace cleared for the file. Up to 1,000 and 4,000 characters, no control characters, `null` or empty clears; screened at `user-input` (`422` with `step: guardrails`). `409` for a file that is not an image. Audited `file.alt.updated` and `file.description.updated` (before and after), each only when it changed |
| `POST /api/files/:id/alt-suggestion` `{profile}` | `files:write` and `inference:invoke`. A suggestion from the vision profile named, through `apps/ai.ts` `generate` (an approved model with `vision`, the caller's ceiling, the image's label under the profile's, quota and metering, `model-output`); the model sees the picture without its metadata. `{suggestion, profile, model, version, accepted: false}`: nothing is saved. `409` for a profile without a vision model. Audited `file.alt.suggested` |

### Served copies without metadata (B-142)

Every image the file store serves goes out without EXIF (with its GPS IFD and thumbnail), XMP, IPTC, comments, text
chunks, C2PA manifests and data after the end of the image; the ICC profile and EXIF Orientation stay; the stored
original is never changed (`files/exif.ts`, `docs/security.md`). That covers `GET /api/files/:id/content`,
`/versions/:n/content`, previews, `POST /api/file-links/download`, `POST /api/public/file-links/download`, DAV `GET`
for anyone but the owner, avatars and group pictures, and feed crossposts. JPEG and PNG are cleaned as they stream and
sent without `Content-Length`; WebP and GIF are cleaned in memory up to 32 MB (`413` above). `?original=1` on the two
content routes gives the owner the file as uploaded (`403` for anyone else); audited `file.downloaded` with
`original: true`, cleaned downloads with `metadata: stripped`.

## Sprint 47 (1.8.0, Unreleased): designer editing; presence and soft locks in the designers (B-137, B-140)

Migrations `097_designer_editing` (`workflow_tags`, `workflow_favourites`) and `098_design_locks` (`design_viewers`,
`design_locks`). Console: `web/js/screens/workflows-editing.js` (`App.wfEdit`) and `web/js/screens/design-presence.js`
(`App.designPresence`, used by the workflow designer, the app-flow canvas, the form editor and the entity designer).

### Step comments, tags and favourites (B-137)

Step comments are part of the draft graph: `nodes[].comments: [{id, text (1 to 2000), by?, byName?, at?, resolved?}]`,
at most 50 per step. On `PUT /api/workflows/:id/draft` the server sets `by`, `byName` and `at` of a comment the stored
draft did not have to the saver, and keeps the stored author and time of the others whatever the client sent; a new
workflow (also from a bundle or a template) keeps what its comments carry. Comments are never validated against or read
by a run; versions and bundles carry them.

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workflows?tag&favourites=true` | As before; each row also has `tags: string[]` and `favourite` (the caller's star). `tag` keeps rows with that tag, `favourites=true` the caller's starred ones. `GET /api/workflows/:id` carries both too |
| `GET /api/workflow-tags` | `agents:run`. `{tags: [{tag, count}]}`: the tags of the workflows the caller may see (workspace, clearance) |
| `PUT /api/workflows/:id/tags` | `workflows:manage`. `{tags}` replaces them: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, up to 40 each, at most 10 (`400` otherwise). Audited `workflow.tags.updated` with `added` and `removed` (nothing when unchanged) |
| `PUT /api/workflows/:id/favourite` | `agents:run`. Stars it for the caller: `{favourite: true}`. Audited `workflow.favourite.added` |
| `DELETE /api/workflows/:id/favourite` | `agents:run`. `204`. Audited `workflow.favourite.removed` |

Deleting a workflow removes its tags and everyone's stars.

### Presence and the edit lock (B-140)

Kinds: `workflow`, `app-flow`, `app-form`, `app-entity`. Presence needs the kind's read right (`agents:run`;
`apps:design` for flows; `records:read` for forms and entities, as reading them does), the lock its manage right
(`workflows:manage`; `apps:design` and `workflows:manage` for flows, which save their workflow; `apps:design`). An
object outside the caller's workspaces (or group), or above their clearance, is `404` whether it exists or not. The
REST routes are declared `authenticated` in the route registry because the right depends on the kind; the handler
checks it (`403` naming it).

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/design-locks/:kind/:id?app` | `{kind, id, title, label, canManage, viewers: [{userId, name, since, you}], lock: {userId, name, since, expiresAt, via: socket \| api, you} \| null}` |
| `POST /api/design-locks/:kind/:id` | `{app?, takeover?}`. Takes or renews the lock (TTL 60 s): `{lock, tookOver}`; `409 Being edited` with `lock` when someone else holds it and `takeover` is not set. Audited `design.lock.taken`, or `design.lock.taken_over` with `from` |
| `DELETE /api/design-locks/:kind/:id?app` | Releases the caller's own lock. `204`. Audited `design.lock.released` (`reason: release`) |
| `GET /api/admin/design-locks` | `tenant:manage`. `{locks: [{kind, id, title, label, userId, name, since, expiresAt, via}]}`, live locks within the caller's clearance |
| `POST /api/admin/design-locks/:kind/:id/break` | `tenant:manage`. `:id` is the object's id. Removes the lock without taking it: `{broken}`; `404` when none is live. The holder is told. Audited `design.lock.broken` |

Saves: `PUT /api/workflows/:id/draft`, `PUT /api/apps/:app/flows/:flow` (its own lock and its workflow's),
`PATCH /api/apps/:app/entities/:entity` and `PATCH /api/apps/:app/forms/:form` answer `409 Being edited` with
`lock` (and `design`) while someone else holds a live lock; the existing revision checks stay as the last guard. A
successful save releases the saver's lock (`design.lock.released`, `reason: save`). Locks also go on close, on
disconnect (`reason: close`, `disconnect`) and when they expire (`reason: expired`, by the sweep, kind `system`).

Socket events (rooms decided by the server from the socket's principal; clients never name them):

| From the console | |
| --- | --- |
| `design.open {kind, id, app?}` | Ack `{ok, id, title, label, canManage, canBreak, viewers, lock}` (`lock.mine`: held by this socket; `lock.you`: by this person) or `{ok: false, error: 'Not available to you.'}` |
| `design.heartbeat {kind, id}` | Every 15 s: refreshes the viewer row (lease 45 s), renews this socket's lock, and checks access again (a socket that lost it gets `design.closed`) |
| `design.lock {kind, id, takeover?}` | Takes the lock from this socket; ack as for open, `ok: false` with the holder |
| `design.unlock {kind, id}`, `design.close {kind, id}` | Releases this socket's lock; closes the object |

| To the console | |
| --- | --- |
| `design.state {kind, id, viewers, lock}` | After every change, relayed by every instance to the sockets it holds in the room (`design_viewers` and `design_locks` are shared rows; the state travels on the bus) |
| `design.lock.lost {kind, id, by, reason: taken_over \| broken \| moved}` | To the sockets that held it; the console keeps unsaved changes on the device (localStorage) and offers them back |
| `design.closed {kind, id}` | Access ended |

## Sprint 46 (1.8.0, Unreleased): the webhook trigger of every workflow and run retention (B-130, B-135)

Migrations `085_workflow_hooks` and `086_workflow_retention`. Every route but the public hook needs
`workflows:manage`, acts in the caller's tenant and workspace, on workflows within their clearance, and answers
problem+json.

### Webhook trigger (B-130)

A trigger step may have `source: webhook`. The hook's secret, owner and on/off state live in `workflow_hooks`, never in
the graph, so versions and bundles carry none of them (an imported workflow's webhook arrives switched off with no
secret; the import's `bindings` list it as `trigger webhook, on publish`).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workflows/:id/hook` | `{workflowId, trigger: {draft, published}, enabled, live, secretSet, secretSetAt, owner, ownerName, received, refused, lastReceivedAt, lastRefusedAt, lastRunId, path, url, signature, timestamp, maxBytes, ratePerMinute, windowSeconds, example, deliveries: [{id, at, outcome: accepted \| refused, status, reason, runId, size}]}` (the last 20 of the 50 kept). `live` is on, with a secret, and the published version's trigger is `webhook`. `example` is a `curl` command that signs with `openssl` from `$EXPRSN_HOOK_SECRET`. Never the secret |
| `PUT /api/workflows/:id/hook` | `{enabled}`. On: needs a secret (`409` otherwise), a draft or published trigger with source `webhook` (`409 Not a webhook workflow`) and `agents:run` (`403`); the caller becomes the owner. Audited `workflow.hook.updated` |
| `POST /api/workflows/:id/hook/secret` | `{}`. Makes or rotates the secret: `201 {secret, secretSetAt, enabled, path, url}`, the secret in this answer only, sealed at rest (`workflowhook:<id>`). The old secret stops at once (no grace period) and the signatures seen are forgotten. `409` for a workflow whose trigger is not `webhook`. Audited `workflow.hook.rotated` (`first`, `enabled`) |
| `POST /hooks/workflows/:tenant/:workflow` | Public (outside `/api`; the signature is the authentication), the app flows' signed hook (`workflows/signed-hooks.ts`). `Content-Type: application/json` (`415`), at most 64 KB (`413`). `X-Exprsn-Timestamp`: Unix seconds within 5 minutes (`401`); `X-Exprsn-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, HMAC-SHA256 of `<timestamp>.<raw body>` under the secret (`401`); each signature once (`409` replay, across instances through the shared nonce table). 60 requests a minute per workflow (`429`). `404` for an unknown workflow and alike for one that is off (hook off, no secret, or the published version's trigger is not `webhook`). The body is a JSON object (`400`); it passes `untrusted-content` and `user-input` at the workflow's label (`422`), must match the trigger's output schema when one is set (`400`), and becomes the run input. The owner is checked again (active, `agents:run`, cleared for the label, in the workflow's workspace; `409` otherwise). `202 {run}`, trigger `webhook`, at the workflow's label. Audited `workflow.hook.received`, refusals `workflow.hook.refused` with the reason |

### Run retention (B-135)

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/workflow-retention` | The tenant's policy: `{policy: {runDays, failedDays, maxRuns}, set, defaults: {runDays: 90, failedDays: 180, maxRuns: 1000}, graceHours, sweepHours, lastRunAt, lastPruned, updatedAt, updatedBy}` |
| `PUT /api/workflow-retention` | `{runDays, failedDays, maxRuns}`, each a whole number (days 1 to 3650, runs 1 to 100000) or `null` for the default. Audited `workflow.retention.updated` (`scope: tenant`, before and after) |
| `GET /api/workflows/:id/retention` | `{workflowId, override, tenant, effective, updatedAt, updatedBy}` |
| `PUT /api/workflows/:id/retention` | `{runDays, failedDays, maxRuns}`; `null` follows the tenant's policy, all `null` removes the override. Audited `workflow.retention.updated` (`scope: workflow`) |
| `POST /api/workflow-retention/prune` | `{dryRun = true, workflow?}`. Prunes now (or counts) the runs of the workflows the caller may open, or of one: `{dryRun, runs, steps, items, approvals, deadLetters, workflows, kept: {active, deadLetter, legalHold, evidence, recent}}`. Audited `workflow.retention.pruned` (dry runs too) |

The job `workflow.retention` runs every 6 hours per active tenant over every workflow. A finished run (succeeded,
rejected or cancelled after `runDays`, failed after `failedDays`, or older than the newest `maxRuns` finished runs of
its workflow) is deleted with its steps (the sealed checkpoints), items, approvals and redriven dead letters. Never
deleted: queued, running and waiting runs; runs finished in the last 24 hours; runs with an open dead letter; runs
whose owner or workspace is under a legal hold (`s.legalHolds.held`) and runs kept by `s.evidence.keptOf(tenant,
'workflow-run')` (a hold of scope `object` on one run: `workflow-run` is a moderated object type). Each held run is
recorded once in `retention_skips` (`path: workflow.retention`) with a `retention.skipped` audit entry. A scheduled
prune that removes something writes one `workflow.retention.pruned` summary.

## Sprint 46 (1.8.0, Unreleased): approval deadlines and quorum; SLA timers and routing (B-133, B-134)

Migrations `088_approval_deadlines` and `089_sla_routing`. Every route acts in the caller's tenant, filters by
clearance and workspace, audits its changes and answers problem+json.

### Approval deadlines, reminders, escalation and quorum (B-133)

An Approval step's `config` may add (validated at publish, `workflows/approval-deadlines.ts`):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `due` | `{afterMs}` (from when the step pauses, at least one minute, not past `timeoutMs`) or `{at}` (a template read from the context when the step pauses: ISO 8601 or epoch ms; capped at the timeout; a value that is not a time leaves the approval with its timeout only and a `dueWarning` on the step) |
| `reminders` | Up to five durations before the due time; each notifies the assignees once (`workflow.approval.reminded`) |
| `onBreach` | `{action: notify \| escalate \| reject \| approve \| timeout, role?, user?}`. `notify` (the default) tells the assignees and the run's owner (`workflow.approval.overdue`); `escalate` adds a role or a person who may then decide too (`workflow.approval.escalated`); `reject` decides as a rejection with no decider (`workflow.approval.auto-rejected`, the run ends `rejected`); `approve` needs `autoApprove: true` on the step and publishes with a warning (`workflow.approval.auto-approved`, `decided_by` null, so a four-eyes check such as `knowledge_publish` still refuses it); `timeout` passes the step with `{…input, timedOut: true}` and the run goes on along the step's `timeout` edges only (`workflow.approval.timed-out`) |
| `autoApprove` | `true` allows `onBreach.action: approve` |
| `quorum` | `{mode: any \| all \| count, count?, rejects: final \| counted}`. `any` is one decision, as before. `all` needs every eligible approver counted when the step paused (active holders of the role, cleared for the run's label); `count` needs N distinct approvers. A `final` reject rejects at once; a `counted` one rejects once the approvals still possible cannot reach the quorum. One person counts once (`workflow_approval_votes`, unique per approval and person); a quorum other than `any` cannot have a form or approve automatically. A dry run's quorum is `any` |

Edges: `branch: timeout` is allowed only from an Approval step whose `onBreach.action` is `timeout`, which must have
one. `timeoutMs` stays the hard expiry: the approval expires and the step fails, as before (`workflow.approval.expired`).

The scheduled job `workflow.approvals` (every `WORKFLOW_SCHEDULE_TICK_SECONDS`, one job per bucket for the platform)
reads `workflow_approvals.next_check_at` and claims each reminder, breach and expiry with one conditional update, so it
happens once across instances and after a restart. No job or timer per approval is queued any more; pending approvals
from before the migration are expired by the tick at their `due_at`.

`GET /api/workflow-approvals` and the run view's `approvals[]` add `due: {at, overdue, breachedAt, reminders,
remindersSent} | null`, `expiresAt` (= `dueAt`, the hard expiry), `escalated: {role, user, userName, at} | null`,
`outcome` (`overdue`, `escalated`, `auto-approved`, `auto-rejected`, `timed-out` or null), `quorum: {mode, required,
rejects, eligible}` and `votes: [{userId, name, decision, at}]`; the escalated role or person sees the approval and has
`canDecide`. `POST /api/workflow-approvals/:id` answers `{state: pending, vote, votes: {approve, reject, required}}`
for a vote that does not decide yet (audited `workflow.approval.voted`), `409` for a second vote by the same person.

### SLA timers and assignment routing (B-134)

Queue types: `channel-session` (escalated sessions; scope: the channel id), `flag` (open flags other than those of held
writes; scope: the moderation queue id), `held-write` (writes held for review; scope: the kind), `appeal` (pending and
reviewing appeals; scope: `action` or `sanction`). `*` is the whole type; the most specific enabled policy or rule wins.
Permissions: each type's manage permission (`channels:manage`; `moderation:manage` for flags, held writes and appeals,
as for the moderation review queues) changes its policies and rules; its review permission (`channels:review`,
`flags:review`, `moderation:review`) reads items and statistics. A route declares every permission a type may need
and the handler asks for the one of the type in the body or query.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sla/policies?type=` | `{items: [{id, name, queueType, scope, firstResponseMinutes, resolutionMinutes, warnPercent, hours, pauseOnCustomer, onWarn, onBreach, enabled, createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt}]}` for the types the caller may read |
| `POST /api/sla/policies` | `{name, queueType, scope = *, firstResponseMinutes?, resolutionMinutes?, warnPercent = 80, hours?: {timeZone, week: {mon…sun: [["09:00","17:00"]]}, holidays: ["YYYY-MM-DD"]}, pauseOnCustomer = true, onWarn = [{kind: notify}], onBreach = [{kind: notify}], enabled}`; actions `{kind: notify, role?}`, `{kind: priority, to: high \| urgent}`, `{kind: escalate, role? \| user?}`. At least one target (`400`); one policy per type and scope (`409`). `201`. Audited `sla.policy.created` |
| `PUT /api/sla/policies/:id` | The same body. Audited `sla.policy.updated` |
| `DELETE /api/sla/policies/:id` | `204`. Audited `sla.policy.deleted` |
| `GET /api/sla/routing?type=` | `{items: [{id, queueType, scope, mode, pool, fallback, skipUnavailable, enabled, …}]}` |
| `PUT /api/sla/routing` | `{queueType, scope = *, mode: manual \| round-robin \| least-loaded \| skills, pool: {role? \| users?}, fallback: {kind: queue} \| {kind: any} \| {kind: user, userId}, skipUnavailable = true, enabled}`; one rule per type and scope. Audited `sla.routing.updated` |
| `DELETE /api/sla/routing/:id` | `204`. Audited `sla.routing.deleted` |
| `GET /api/sla/skills` | `{items: [{userId, name, skills}]}` (`users:manage` or a manage permission above) |
| `PUT /api/sla/skills/:userId` | `{skills: [string]}` (lower-cased, at most 50) replaces the person's skills (`users:manage`). Audited `sla.skills.updated` with what was added and removed |
| `GET /api/sla/items?type=&filter=breaching-soon\|breached&scope=` | The open items the caller may see: `{items: [{type, id, title, scope, label, workspaceId, assignee, tags, startedAt, priority, escalatedAt, routedAt, sla: {policyId, policy, state: ok \| warning \| breached \| paused \| met, firstResponse, resolution, dueAt, leftMs} \| null}], counts: {open, withSla, warning, breached, paused}}`, by priority then time left. A target is `{targetMs, dueAt, at, met, breached, warning, paused, leftMs, fraction}` in business time |
| `GET /api/sla/items/:id?type=` | One item with its `firstResponseAt`, `resolvedAt` and `pauses` |
| `GET /api/sla/stats?type=&days=30` | `{type, days, scopes: [{scope, resolved, resolutionMetPercent, firstResponseMetPercent, averageFirstResponseMs, breached, open, warning, breachedNow}], total: {resolved, open, breached, resolutionMetPercent, averageFirstResponseMs}}` |
| `POST /api/sla/evaluate` | Runs the tenant's tick now: `{tracked, warned, breached, routed, closed}`. Audited `sla.evaluated` |
| `POST /api/channels/:id/sessions/:sessionId/assign` | `{userId \| null}` (`channels:review`): a reviewer of the channel cleared for its label, or nobody. Audited `channel.session.assigned`, event `channel.session.assigned`, the person is told |
| `POST /api/moderation/appeals/:ref/assign` | `{userId \| null}` (`moderation:review`): a reviewer cleared for the appeal who is neither the appellant nor the decider under appeal. A routing hint (anyone independent may still take the review). Audited `moderation.appeal.assigned` |

Timers come from each item's own timestamps: a session's starts when it was escalated, its first response is the
first message by a person, it waits on the customer from a person's answer until the customer writes (paused when
`pauseOnCustomer`), and it is resolved when closed; a flag's first response is the first action a person took on it
and it is resolved when decided; a held write follows its flag; an appeal's first response is the start of its review.
Only business hours count when the policy has `hours` (`sla/hours.ts`: windows per weekday in the zone, holidays
closed, daylight saving followed). The job `sla.tick` (every minute per active tenant) evaluates every open item under
a policy, fires the warn actions when a running target passes `warnPercent` and the breach actions when it is past due,
each once per item and target (a conditional update on `sla_timers`), routes unassigned items by their rule, and keeps
finished items' outcomes in `sla_timers` for the statistics. Routing assigns through the domain's own path
(`FlagService.assignTo` for flags and held writes, `ChannelService.assignSession`, `ModerationService.assignAppeal`):
round-robin takes turns by a cursor claimed with a conditional update; least-loaded counts open items per assignee in
the queue type; skills scores people by `user_skills` tags matching the item's tags (a flag: its severity, checkpoint,
kind and `rule:<name>`; a session: `channel:<name>` and its kind; a held write: its kind and rule; an appeal: its kind)
and breaks ties by load. With `skipUnavailable`, people whose presence is away or offline are skipped; when nobody is
left the fallback leaves the item in the queue, takes the least loaded of the whole pool, or gives it to the named
person. Audited `sla.item.routed`, `sla.item.warned` and `sla.item.breached` with what was done.

## Sprint 46 (1.8.0, Unreleased): decision tables and the switch step (B-131, B-132)

Decision tables are tenant objects with a label (`decision_tables`, `decision_table_versions`, migration
`087_decision_tables`; `server/src/decisions/`). Reading, checking and testing need `agents:run` (as reading and running
workflows do); creating, saving, publishing, deleting, exporting and importing need `workflows:manage`. A table above
the caller's clearance answers `404`. A definition is `{inputs: [{name, label?, type: string | number | boolean |
date}], outputs: [{name, label?, type, values?: [ranked values], default?}], hitPolicy: first | unique | priority | any
| collect, aggregation?: sum | min | max | count (collect only, one output column), rules: [{id?, when: {column: test},
then: {column: value | null}, note?}]}`. A test is structured (`{op: any | empty | eq | ne | lt | lte | gt | gte |
contains | starts_with, value}`, `{op: between, min, max}`, `{op: in | not_in, values}`) or text: `-`, `"gold"` or
`= 5`, `≠ 5`, `< 5`, `≤ 5`, `> 5`, `≥ 5` (`<=`, `>=`, `!=` too), `[1..5]` or `between 1 and 5` (inclusive),
`in ("EU", "UK")`, `not in (…)`, `contains "x"`, `starts with "x"`, `is empty`; text is parsed by the column's type and
stored structured (a cell that does not parse is `400` naming the rule and column). Evaluation is pure: no code runs.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/decision-tables` | The tenant's tables within the caller's clearance: `[{id, name, title, description, label, draftRev, publishedVersion, hitPolicy, inputs, outputs, rules, …}]` |
| `POST /api/decision-tables` `{name, title?, description?, label = internal, definition?}` | `workflows:manage`. A draft (a label above the caller's clearance is `403`, a taken name `409`): `201` the view. Audited `decision.created` |
| `GET /api/decision-tables/:id` | By id or name: `{…summary, draft, dirty, check: {ok, errors, warnings}, versions: [{version, state: published \| deprecated, note, publishedBy, publishedAt, rules}]}` |
| `PUT /api/decision-tables/:id/draft` `{definition?, rev?, title?, description?, label?}` | `workflows:manage`. Saves the draft; `rev` is the revision loaded (`409` when someone saved since). Audited `decision.draft.saved` |
| `POST /api/decision-tables/:id/check` `{definition?}` | What publishing would say about a definition (the draft when none is given), without saving: `{ok, errors, warnings, definition}` (the definition normalised). Issues are `{code: structure \| type \| overlap \| unreachable \| policy, message, rule?, column?, other?}` |
| `POST /api/decision-tables/:id/publish` `{note?}` | `workflows:manage`. Checks the draft: types consistent, values in their lists, no two rules that can match one input under `unique`, overlapping rules agreeing under `any`, a ranked output under `priority`, aggregation rules; a rule an earlier one always takes first under `first` is a warning. Problems: `422 Decision table invalid` with `errors` and `warnings` (audited `decision.publish.refused`); otherwise the next version: `{version, warnings, table}`. Audited `decision.published` |
| `GET /api/decision-tables/:id/versions/:version` | One version with its definition |
| `POST /api/decision-tables/:id/test` `{version = draft \| published \| <n>, inputs}` | Evaluates sample inputs: `{version, hitPolicy, aggregation, matched: [{rule, index}], outputs, rows?, explanation: [{rule, index, matched, tests: [{column, test, value, passed}]}], summary}`. An input of the wrong type is `422 Input refused`, two matches under `unique` or disagreeing matches under `any` `422 Hit policy violated` with `rules`. Audited `decision.tested` |
| `GET /api/decision-tables/:id/used-by` | Published workflows whose decision steps name the table: `{id, name, usedBy: [{workflow, workflowId, version, steps}], deleteBlocked}` |
| `GET /api/decision-tables/:id/export?version=<n> \| draft` | `workflows:manage`. `exprsn-decision/1` JSON (`{format, exportedAt, table: {name, title, description, label}, version, definition}`), the published version by default. Audited `decision.exported` |
| `POST /api/decision-tables/import` `{export, name?}` | `workflows:manage`. A new table whose draft is the export's definition, never published (`400` for anything else, `409` for a taken name). Audited `decision.imported` |
| `DELETE /api/decision-tables/:id` | `workflows:manage`. `204`; `409 Still in use` with `usedBy` while a published workflow uses it. Audited `decision.deleted` |

Hit policies: `first` the first matching rule; `unique` at most one; `priority` the matching rule whose outputs come
first in the output columns' `values` order (columns in order); `any` every match gives the same outputs; `collect`
every match in order (`outputs` per column as lists, `rows` per rule), or with `sum`, `min`, `max` or `count` (how many
rules matched) over the one output column. With no match the single-result policies give the columns' defaults, or
`outputs: null`. An empty input (missing, null or "") matches only `-` and `is empty`.

Workflows: the step kind `decision` (`{table, version?, inputs?: {column: template}, source?: template, outputs?:
{field: column}, noMatch: continue | fail}`) evaluates the pinned or latest published version as the run's owner (a
table above their clearance blocks the step) and outputs the mapped values with `matched`, at the table's label. Without
`inputs` the columns read the fields of the same names of `source` (an object) or of the step's input. Publishing
checks that the table is published, at or below the workflow's label, and has the mapped columns. App flows take an
action `{type: decision, table, version?, inputs?, noMatch}`, compiled onto the same step (without `inputs`, from
`{{input.record.values}}`); `GET /api/apps/:app/flows/palette` lists `decisions`. The built-in tool `decision.evaluate`
(`{table, version?, inputs}`, read-only) evaluates as the caller (`agents:run`), never a table above the label of the
call.

The step kind `switch` (`{value: template, cases: [{label, match: equals, value} | {label, match: in, values} |
{label, match: range, min?, max?}]}`, at most 9 cases): the first case whose test the value passes (a range runs from
`min` up to but not including `max`), else `default`, is the step's `case` (`{…input, case}`); each edge out of it
names its case (`edges[].case`) and only that edge is taken. Publishing needs unique case labels (`default` is
reserved), sound ranges, an edge for every case, one edge per case and a default edge; a case on another step's edge is
refused. Workflow bundles carry case edges, and decision steps by table name with `references.decisions: [{name,
version}]`; `POST /api/workflows/import` takes `bindings.decisions` and reports `{kind: decision, status: bound |
missing}` for each.

## Sprint 45 (1.8.0, Unreleased): saved connection queries and REST connections (B-125, B-126)

Designing needs `connections:manage` (as the connections themselves); running needs the read right
`connections:query` (connection admin, tenant admin, workflow admin and knowledge curator hold it; `connections:manage`
alone does not run through the read API). Everything is filtered by clearance: a query or REST connection above it is
a `404`. Every change is audited (`connection.query.*`, `connection.rest.*`), and so is every run, refused or not.

### Saved queries (`connections/saved-queries.ts`, `connections/params.ts`)

A **saved query** belongs to one data connection: `{name, title?, description?, label, write = false, lookups = false,
definition: {text, object?, params, rowLimit = 500, timeoutS = 10}}`. `text` is SQL with `:name` placeholders
(PostgreSQL and MySQL) or the OpenSearch or MongoDB query JSON with `{"$param": "name"}` where a value goes. `params`:
`[{name, type: string | number | boolean | date | list | identifier, title?, required?, default?, allowed?, min?, max?,
maxLength?, itemType? (list: string | number), maxItems?}]`. Values are always bound: `$1`… (PostgreSQL; a list binds
as one array, use `= ANY(:ids)`) or one `?` per value (MySQL; a list becomes `?, ?, …`); JSON placeholders are replaced
by the value as a JSON value. An `identifier` stands only for one of the names `allowed` lists, quoted. The label is at
least the connection's; `rowLimit` and `timeoutS` are capped by the connection's.

Saving classifies the text (`connections/classify.ts` with the allow-list) once per name each identifier may stand
for: a write is `422 Write refused` unless `write: true` (then it must be a single write, `422 Not a write query`
otherwise); DDL, several statements, objects outside the allow-list and text the parser cannot read are `422`; an
undeclared `:word` or an unused parameter is `400`. A write query is saved, published and reviewed, and every run of it
is `409 Write query` (registered connections are read-only in this release). Publishing classifies the draft again
against the allow-list in force.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/connections/:id/queries` | The connection's saved queries within the caller's clearance, each with `draft`, `draftClassification`, `draftRev`, `publishedVersion`, `dirty`, `versions` |
| `POST /api/admin/connections/:id/queries` | Creates one as a draft (`201`); `409` for a taken name, `403` above the designer's clearance. Audited `connection.query.created` |
| `GET /api/admin/connection-queries/:id` | One query with its versions |
| `PUT /api/admin/connection-queries/:id` `{rev?, title?, description?, label?, write?, lookups?, definition?}` | Saves the draft against `rev` (`409 Changed meanwhile` when stale), classified again. Audited `connection.query.updated` |
| `POST /api/admin/connection-queries/:id/publish` `{note?}` | The draft as the next version (`published`; the one before is `retired`); `409` when nothing changed. Audited `connection.query.published` (or `connection.query.publish.refused`) |
| `POST /api/admin/connection-queries/:id/test` `{version = draft \| published \| <n>, params, limit ≤ 200 = 20}` | The test panel: a run of the draft or a version, as the designer, through every check below; the result plus `version` and `classification` |
| `DELETE /api/admin/connection-queries/:id` | `204`; `409 Still in use` with `usedBy` while a knowledge source reads it. Audited `connection.query.removed` |
| `GET /api/connection-queries` | `connections:query`. Published read queries the caller may run: `{id, name, title, description, label, connection, engine, publishedVersion, params, lookups}` |
| `POST /api/connection-queries/:id/run` `{params, limit?, cursor?}` | `connections:query`. Runs the published version (by id or name) |

A **run** (the read API, the tool, a workflow step, a knowledge source, a lookup, B-129's imports through
`s.savedQueries.run(principal, queryId, params, {limit, cursor})`): the caller's clearance and the label of the call
cover the query's label (`403`, `step: clearance` or `label`), the parameters bind (`400 Invalid parameters` naming
each), the bound text is classified again against the allow-list in force (`422` when it narrowed), the `db-query`
guardrail sees the text and the parameter values (`403 Blocked by a guardrail`; a redaction refuses too), the driver
runs it in its read-only transaction with the row and time caps, and the result is masked as the data browser's. The
answer, which charts and reports will read later:

```json
{ "columns": [{ "name": "id", "type": "number" }], "rows": [{ "id": 1 }], "truncated": true, "nextCursor": "…", "label": "internal", "masked": ["email"], "ms": 12 }
```

`nextCursor` pages SQL queries (offset within the same version; a cursor of another query or version is `409`).
Audited `connection.query.run`, `connection.query.run.refused` or `connection.query.run.failed` with `via`.

### REST connections (`connections/rest.ts`)

A **REST connection**: `{name, title?, baseUrl, zone = data, label, auth, headers = {}, timeoutMs = 10000 (500 to
60000), maxBytes = 1 MB (1 KB to 16 MB)}`. The base URL is http or https with no credentials, query or fragment, and
its host must be on the tenant's list of allowed hosts (Registry, Allowed hosts; an internal host also needs the
operator's `SERVICE_ALLOWED_HOSTS`), else `422 REST connection refused`. `auth`: `{kind: none | basic | bearer |
api-key-header | api-key-query | oauth2-client, username?, headerName?, queryName?, tokenUrl?, clientId?, scope?,
secret?}`; the token URL passes the same host rule. The `secret` is sealed (`rest-connection:<id>`) or kept as a
`vault:` reference the saver can read (resolved as them at each call); it is never shown again and moves to the vault
with the other third-party credentials (`POST /api/vault/credential-moves` kind `rest-connection`). A header that
carries a credential takes a `vault:` reference, never a literal (`422`).

An **endpoint**: `{name, title?, description?, lookups = false, definition: {path, params, query, paging, mapping}}`.
`path` is a template (`/people/{id}`) whose parameters are percent-encoded, never empty, `.` or `..`, and the URL must
stay under the base path; `query` maps names to literals or `{param}` (no credential literals). `paging`: `{kind:
none}`, `{kind: page, param = page, start = 1, sizeParam?, size = 50, maxPages = 20}`, `{kind: offset, offsetParam =
offset, limitParam = limit, size, maxPages}`, `{kind: cursor, param = cursor, next (pointer or dotted path to the next
cursor), sizeParam?, size, maxPages}` or `{kind: link, sizeParam?, size, maxPages}` (RFC 8288 `rel="next"`, followed
only under the base URL). `mapping`: `{items: '' | /json/pointer | dotted.path, fields: [{name, path, type: string |
number | boolean | date | json}]}`; without fields every top-level key is a column.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/rest-connections` | REST connections within the caller's clearance, with their endpoints; secrets never. Since 2.0.x each carries `category`: `rest` (REST and OData) or `non-rest` (GraphQL and SOAP), how the console groups them |
| `POST /api/admin/rest-connections` | Registers one (`201`). Audited `connection.rest.registered` (a refusal `connection.rest.refused`) ; 1.9.0: `protocol: rest\|graphql\|soap` (default `rest`), and for SOAP `wsdlUrl` (fetched through the same host checks, at most 2 MB) or `wsdl` (the text), not both. The view adds `protocol`, and for SOAP `wsdlUrl`, `wsdlAt` and `soap: {targetNamespace, ports[{service, name, binding, soapVersion, address, usable}], operations[{name, port, soapVersion, soapAction, style, input, fields[{name, type, minOccurs, maxOccurs}], output, writeLike}], notes}` (never the WSDL itself). A WSDL with a DOCTYPE, or without a port under the base URL, is refused (`422`) |
| `POST /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/wsdl` `{wsdlUrl?, wsdl?}` | 1.9.0, SOAP: fetches or takes the WSDL again and re-reads it: `{connection, missing}` (operations endpoints use that are gone). Audited `connection.rest.wsdl.refreshed` |
| `GET /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/wsdl` | 1.9.0, SOAP: the stored WSDL document |
| `GET /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/graphql/schema` | 1.9.0, GraphQL: an introspection query; `{queryType, fields[{name, description, type, args[{name, type}]}]}`. Audited `connection.rest.graphql.schema` |
| `POST /api/admin/rest-connections` with `protocol: odata` | 1.9.0, OData v4: the base URL is the service root; `<root>/$metadata` is read at once with the connection's authentication (the egress guard, 2 MB, the strict XML parser: a DOCTYPE is refused) and a connection whose metadata cannot be read is not kept (`422`/`502`, audited `connection.rest.refused`). The view adds `metadataUrl`, `metadataAt` and `odata: {kind, version, namespaces, sets[{name, kind: set\|singleton, entityType, properties[{name, type, nullable, key}], navigation[{name, type, collection}]}], actions, functions, notes}`; actions and functions are listed, never called |
| `POST /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/odata/metadata` | 1.9.0, OData: reads `$metadata` again: `{connection, missing}` (endpoints whose entity set is gone). Audited `connection.rest.metadata.refreshed` |
| `POST /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/openapi` `{url}` or `{document}` | 1.9.0, REST: reads an OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0 document (JSON or YAML; by URL through the egress guard and the tenant's allowed hosts, 4 MB; pasted text within the 256 kB body limit) and keeps it as the connection's service description: `{connection, specVersion, title, version, servers, operations[{operationId, name, method, path, summary, importable, reason?, endpointPath, params[{name, param, in, type, required, enum?, default?}], paging, mapping, notes}], notes}`. Only GET operations under the base URL are importable; credential-like and header or cookie parameters are left out. Audited `connection.rest.openapi.read` |
| `POST /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/openapi/import` `{operations: [{operationId, name?}]}` | 1.9.0, REST: makes the chosen operations endpoints through the ordinary endpoint checks (names kept unique, never replacing one): `{created[{operationId, endpoint}], refused[{operationId, reason}], connection}`. Audited `connection.rest.openapi.imported` and `connection.rest.endpoint.created` |
| `GET /api/admin/rest-connections/:id` | One, with `usedBy` (app entities and knowledge sources) |
| `PATCH /api/admin/rest-connections/:id` | Settings, headers or `auth` (leave `secret` out to keep the sealed one). Audited `connection.rest.updated` or `connection.rest.credential.rotated` |
| `DELETE /api/admin/rest-connections/:id` | `204`; `409 Still in use` with `usedBy`. Audited `connection.rest.removed` |
| `POST /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/test` | Authenticates (an OAuth2 token) and GETs the base URL: `{ok, status, ms, detail, health}`. Audited `connection.rest.tested` |
| `POST /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/endpoints` | Creates (`201`) or replaces by name (`200`, next version). 1.9.0: `definition.graphql: {query, variables}` (one `query` operation only: a mutation or subscription is refused before anything is sent; depth ≤ 12, ≤ 500 fields; parameters bind into variables only) or `definition.soap: {operation, port?, args, confirmRead}` (arguments are escaped text, never XML; an operation named like a write is refused without `confirmRead: true`); cursor paging takes an optional `hasNext` pointer; a GraphQL answer with `errors` and no `data` is `502`, partial data comes with `warnings`; a SOAP Fault is `502`. OData: `definition.odata: {entitySet, select, filter?, orderby?, expand, search?, count}`, checked against `$metadata` (names, a filter of properties, operators, standard functions, literals and `{param}` placeholders only); parameters become OData literals of the type of the property they are compared with (strings quoted with quotes doubled, numbers, dates, GUIDs, booleans; a value of the wrong type is a `400`), a search placeholder a quoted phrase; paging is `offset` (`$skip`/`$top`) or `link` (the body's `@odata.nextLink`, kept under the base URL); items default to `/value`; an OData error answer is `502` with its message. Audited `connection.rest.endpoint.created` or `.updated` |
| `PATCH /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/endpoints/:endpoint` | Changes one endpoint |
| `DELETE /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/endpoints/:endpoint` | `204`; `409` while an entity or knowledge source reads it. Audited `connection.rest.endpoint.removed` |
| `POST /api/admin/rest-connections/:id/endpoints/:endpoint/test` `{params, limit ≤ 200, definition?}` | The editor's test call: the saved endpoint, or (with `definition`, endpoint `_draft`) the one being edited; the mapped rows |
| `GET /api/rest-connections` | `connections:query`. Connections and endpoints the caller may read |
| `POST /api/rest-connections/:id/endpoints/:endpoint/read` `{params, limit ≤ 5000, cursor?}` | `connections:query`. Reads mapped rows (also `s.restConnections.read(principal, connectionId, endpointName, params, {limit, cursor})`) |

A read pages in the endpoint's style until `limit` rows, the last page or `maxPages`; `nextCursor` goes on from the
next item (a cursor of another endpoint or version is `409`). Each request goes through `guardedRequest`: resolved
once, every address checked against the operator's rules and the tenant's list, pinned, no redirects, at most
`timeoutMs` (`502`, "No answer within") and `maxBytes` (`502`, "larger than"). A non-2xx answer is `502`, a host no
longer allowed `422`. The rows pass the `untrusted-content` checkpoint (source `http`): a block is `422 Withheld:
untrusted content`, an annotation comes back as `untrusted: {action: annotate, rule}`. Audited `connection.rest.read`
(host, status, pages, rows, bytes, never a header, query string or body), `.read.refused` or `.read.failed`.

### Where they are used

- The built-in tool **`connections.query`** (migration `090_saved_queries`, read-only, platform entry): `{query,
  params?, limit?, cursor?}` or `{connection, endpoint, params?, limit?, cursor?}`, as the caller (`connections:query`),
  never above the label of the call; workflow tool steps call it the same way. Its result is screened as every tool
  result.
- **Knowledge sources** of kind `saved-query` (`{queryId, params?, idField?, titleField?}`) and `rest` (`{connectionId,
  resource, params?, idField?, titleField?}`) on `POST /api/knowledge/bases/:id/sources`: the curator needs
  `connections:query` and clearance; each sync reads every row (up to 5,000) through the governed path held to the
  source's label floor (at least the query's or connection's label), one document per row, unchanged rows skipped by
  hash, rows gone removed.
- **App lookups**: a field `{type: lookup, source: query, query, valueField, labelField?, params?}` or `{type: lookup,
  source: rest, connection, endpoint, valueField, labelField?, params?}`. Only a query or endpoint marked `lookups`,
  at most at the entity's label and within the reader's clearance; options are kept 30 seconds per process, and a
  written value must be one of them (`400`).
- **App entity sources** (`PUT /api/apps/:app/entities/:entity/source` with `kind: rest`, `object` the endpoint's name,
  `params`): pulled on schedule by `apps.source-pull`, read-only (`writes: true` is `409`, record writes `409`).

## Sprint 44 (1.8.0, Unreleased): charts and dashboards of an app (B-120, B-121)

Migrations `100_app_charts` (`app_charts`, `app_chart_versions`) and `101_app_dashboards` (`app_dashboards`).
`apps/charts.ts` (`s.apps.charts`), `apps/dashboards.ts` (`s.apps.dashboards`), `apps/chart-render.ts` (the static
drawing for snapshots: SVG and PDF operators), routes in `routes/apps-charts.ts` (inside the apps router, so behind
its authentication and app-scoped credential checks). `aggregate` in `apps/query.ts` gained `bucket` (below). Console:
the Dashboards tab of an app (`web/js/screens/apps-dashboards.js`) and the chart renderer and builder
(`web/js/screens/apps-charts.js`).

**Permissions.** Every route needs `records:read`, as saved views do: anyone who reads an app's records may keep
private charts and dashboards. Sharing one with the app's readers, and changing or deleting someone else's shared one,
needs `apps:design` and the app's label within the designer's clearance (`403`, `step: role` or `clearance`). A chart
over a saved query or a REST endpoint needs `connections:query` to save, and each reader needs it, with clearance for
the source's label, to see it computed. A chart or dashboard is private to its owner or shared; one that is not shared
with the caller, or is above their clearance, is a `404`. Names and definitions are sealed with the tenant key.

**Computed as the reader, never stored.** An entity source goes through `records/aggregate` with the reader's grant,
clearance and hidden rules (a row the reader may not read is never counted), after the optional saved view's filters
(the view must be one the reader sees) and the dashboard's filters. A field a policy hides or masks from the reader
(dimension, split, measure, comparison) makes the chart unavailable to them. A saved query is read with
`s.savedQueries.run` and a REST endpoint with `s.restConnections.read`, as the reader, at most 5000 rows, held to the
app's label (`ceiling`), `via: app-chart`, and grouped in memory. Results are cached for 15 seconds keyed by the
reader, their permissions, clearance and grant, the chart's version and the filters (`fresh: true` skips it).

### `records/aggregate` date buckets

`POST /api/apps/:app/entities/:entity/records/aggregate` takes `bucket: day | week | month | quarter | year` with a
`groupBy` that is a date field, `createdAt` or `updatedAt`. Keys are UTC: `2026-10-16`, the Monday of the ISO week
(`2026-10-12`), `2026-10`, `2026-Q4`, `2026`; records without a value are the `null` group, last. `400` for a bucket on
anything else.

### Charts

A chart: `{name, shared = false, label?, definition}`. The label is the source's at least (the entity's, the saved
query's or the REST connection's) and the app's at most. `definition`:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | `bar`, `line`, `area`, `pie`, `donut`, `scatter`, `number` (a tile), `table` |
| `source` | `{kind: entity, entity, view?: <view id>, filter?, q?}`, `{kind: query, query, params = {}}` or `{kind: rest, connection, endpoint, params = {}}` |
| `dimension` | `{field, bucket?}`: an indexed field, `state`, or a date (`createdAt` and `updatedAt` need a bucket); a column for query and REST sources. Null only for `number` and `table` |
| `split` | `{field}`: one measure split into at most 8 series (the most frequent values), for bars, lines, areas and tables |
| `measures` | 1 to 5 of `{op: count}` or `{op: sum \| avg \| min \| max, field}` (an indexed number, date or boolean field, or `<relation>.count`), each with an optional `label`. A pie, donut, tile or split shows one; a scatter one (against a numeric dimension) or two (against each other) |
| `orientation`, `stacking` | `vertical` or `horizontal`; `grouped` or `stacked` (areas with several series always stack) |
| `compare` | A tile's comparison: `{kind: target, value}` or `{kind: previous, field, period}` (this period so far against the previous one, UTC) |
| `sort`, `limit` | `{by: key \| value, dir}`; 1 to 200 categories (empty keys stay last when sorting by key) |
| `colors` | Names of the console theme's colours in order: `accent`, `info`, `ok`, `warn`, `danger`, `fg2`; never literal colours |
| `labels` | `{title?, x?, y?, values = false, legend = true}` |

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/apps/:app/charts` | `{charts: [{id, name, shared, label, ownerId, mine, canEdit, rev, sourceKind, definition, ...}], canShare}`: the caller's own and the shared ones within clearance |
| `POST /api/apps/:app/charts` | `201` with the chart (`rev: 1`). `400 Invalid chart` with `problems` (a field that is not there, not indexed, of the wrong type; a view the author cannot see); `403` for sharing without `apps:design` or a query or REST source without `connections:query`; `409` past 100 per person or 100 shared. Audited `app.chart.created` |
| `POST /api/apps/:app/charts/preview` | `{name?, definition}`: the builder's live preview, computed as the caller and never cached: `{state: ok, data}`; `400` or `403` for what the reader could not compute |
| `GET /api/apps/:app/charts/:id` | The chart |
| `PATCH /api/apps/:app/charts/:id` | `{rev?, name?, shared?, label?, definition?}`; each save is a new version. `409` with the current `rev` when `rev` is stale. Audited `app.chart.updated` (`changed`, `rev`) |
| `DELETE /api/apps/:app/charts/:id` | With its versions. Audited `app.chart.deleted`. `204` |
| `GET /api/apps/:app/charts/:id/versions` | `{versions: [{rev, name, definition, by, at}]}`, newest first, at most 50 |
| `POST /api/apps/:app/charts/:id/data` | `{filters?: [{id, kind: date \| value, field, from?, to?, value?}], fresh = false}`. `{state: ok, data}`, `{state: unavailable, reason}` (shown as "Not available to you") or `{state: error, title, detail}`. `data`: `{type, title, dimension, categories: [{key, label}], series: [{name, values}], points?, axes, value?, compare?, colors, truncated, groups, rowsRead?, filtersApplied, summary, label, computedAt, cached}`; `summary` is the text a screen reader hears |

### Dashboards

A dashboard: `{name, description?, shared = false, label?, cards = [], filters = [], refresh = 0}`. The label defaults
to `internal` (the app's when lower). Cards, at most 24, in order, each with an `id`, a `title?` and a `size`
(`small` a quarter, `medium` a third, `large` a half, `wide` two thirds, `full`): `{kind: chart, chart}` (a chart or
number tile of the app the author can see), `{kind: view, entity, view?, rows = 10}` (a saved view's table, or the
entity's first records) or `{kind: text, markdown}` (at most 5000 characters, rendered escaped: headings, paragraphs,
lists, code, tables and rules; HTML, links and pictures stay text). Filters, at most 6: `{id, kind: date \| value,
field, label, default?: {from?, to?} \| {value?}}`; each applies to every card whose source has that field (an indexed
field, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` or `state` for records; a column for queries and REST) and the others say they are not
filtered. `refresh`: `0`, `30`, `60`, `300`, `900` or `3600` seconds between the console's automatic refreshes.

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/apps/:app/dashboards` | `{dashboards: [{id, name, description, cards, filters, refresh, shared, label, ownerId, mine, canEdit, rev, ...}], canShare}` |
| `POST /api/apps/:app/dashboards` | `201`. `400 Invalid dashboard` with `problems` (a chart the author cannot see, an entity that is not there, a view they cannot see, duplicate ids); `403` for sharing without `apps:design`; `409` past 50 per person or 50 shared. Audited `app.dashboard.created` |
| `GET /api/apps/:app/dashboards/:id` | The dashboard |
| `PATCH /api/apps/:app/dashboards/:id` | `{rev?, name?, description?, shared?, label?, cards?, filters?, refresh?}` (moving and resizing cards is a `cards` update). `409` with `rev` when stale. Audited `app.dashboard.updated` (`changed`) |
| `DELETE /api/apps/:app/dashboards/:id` | Its charts stay. Audited `app.dashboard.deleted`. `204` |
| `POST /api/apps/:app/dashboards/:id/data` | `{filters?: {<filter id>: {from?, to?} \| {value?}}, fresh = false}` (a filter left out takes its default; `{}` clears it). `{id, name, label, rev, refresh, applied, cards: [{id, kind, size, title, state: ok \| unavailable \| error, reason?, detail?, chart?, table?: {entity, columns, rows, total, filtersApplied}, html?}], computedAt}`, every card computed as the caller; a view's column a policy hides from them is left out. `400` for a range whose start is after its end |
