| `GET /api/apps/:app/dashboards/:id/render?format=pdf\|html&filters=<JSON>` | A static snapshot computed as the caller, as a download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`, `no-store`): HTML with each chart as SVG (`role="img"`, its summary, and a "View as table" table), or PDF with each chart as a vector drawing followed by its table. Cards the caller cannot read say "Not available to you". Audited `app.dashboard.rendered` (`format`, `cards`, `unavailable`, `filters`, `bytes`) |

`s.apps.dashboards.render(principal, dashboardId, {format: 'html' | 'pdf', filters?})` returns `{filename, contentType,
bytes}` the same way, for `s.appExports` and scheduled delivery: always as the person it is for, never stored.

## Sprint 44 (1.8.0, Unreleased): scheduled delivery of views, reports and dashboards (B-124)

Migration `104_app_subscriptions` (`app_subscriptions`, `app_subscription_recipients`, `app_subscription_runs`,
`app_subscription_deliveries`). `apps/subscriptions.ts` (`s.apps.subscriptions`), routes in
`routes/apps-subscriptions.ts` (inside the apps router: an app-scoped credential is refused) and
`routes/apps-subscriptions-public.ts` (the unsubscribe link). Console: `web/js/screens/apps-subscriptions.js` (the
Subscribe dialog on saved views, reports and dashboards, and `#/app-subscriptions`).

A subscription names one object (`kind`: `view`, `report`, `dashboard` or `records`; `id`: the view, report or
dashboard id, or the entity for `records`) of one app, a `format` (`xlsx`, `pdf`, `csv`, `html`; a dashboard is `pdf`
or `html`), `params` (a report's, scalars, at most 10) and `filters` (records filters added to the object's own), a
`schedule` (`{preset, values?} | {cron}` with `timezone`, the workflow schedule model of B-138, at least
APPS_DELIVERY_MIN_INTERVAL_MINUTES apart), `destinations` and `options` (`onlyIfRows`, `onlyIfChanged`, `message`).
Destinations:

- `email: {self = true, others = []}`: the subscriber, and other people of the tenant (usernames or ids) whom only a
  holder of `apps:design` cleared for the app may add. Each recipient's copy is rendered as that recipient. A file over
  APPS_DELIVERY_ATTACH_MAX_BYTES is not attached: a copy goes to the recipient's file store (folder "Deliveries" in the
  app's workspace) and the email links to it (a sign-in opens it). Every email carries a signed unsubscribe link and
  `List-Unsubscribe` / `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers;
- `file: {folderId}`: a folder the subscriber may write to (`files:write`, a member of its workspace); the file is named
  after the render with the local date and time;
- `webhook: {url, signing: hmac | ed25519, maxLabel = internal}`: `webhooks:manage`; the host must be on the tenant's
  list of allowed hosts (an empty list allows none) within the operator's rules; the object's label at most `maxLabel`.
  The POST carries `x-exprsn-event: app.delivery`, `x-exprsn-timestamp`, `x-exprsn-delivery-id` (the run) and
  `x-exprsn-signature` (`sha256=` HMAC over `<timestamp>.<body>` with the subscription's own secret, returned once as
  `webhookSecret` and stored sealed) or `x-exprsn-signature-ed25519` with `x-exprsn-key-id` (the tenant's webhook key,
  `/webhooks/keys/<tenant>`). Body: `{type, subscription: {id, name}, run: {id, dueAt}, object: {kind, id, app}, file:
  {filename, contentType, size, sha256, rows, truncated, label}, content}` (`content` base64, or `null` with
  `tooLarge: true` and the file-store copy's `fileId` when over the attachment limit).

Runs: the `apps.subscriptions` tick (every APPS_SCHEDULE_TICK_SECONDS) claims each due time with one conditional update
and queues `apps.subscription.deliver`, tried APPS_DELIVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS times with the queue's backoff (a retry skips
what was delivered). Each recipient is re-checked before their render (active, `records:read`, the app visible, the view
or entity readable at its label) and rendered through `s.appExports.render` as themselves (grants, masks, clearance, the
connection query right); someone refused gets nothing, recorded as `denied` with the reason. A run fails when the owner
is refused, a destination of the owner fails for good, or a retryable error outlasts the attempts; after
APPS_DELIVERY_PAUSE_AFTER failed runs in a row the subscription pauses and the owner gets a notification (and an email).
The history keeps time, destination, recipient, rows, size, outcome and reason, never content. Audited
`app.subscription.created`, `.updated`, `.paused`, `.resumed`, `.deleted`, `.run`, `.unsubscribed` and
`app.delivery.sent`, `.skipped`, `.denied`, `.failed`.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/apps/subscriptions` | `records:read`. `{subscriptions, received}`: the caller's own, and those that email them (without settings): `[{id, name, app: {id, name, title}, kind, objectId, entityId, label, format, schedule: {cron, preset, values, timezone, description}, state, pausedReason, nextRunAt, lastRunAt, lastOutcome, owner, mine, receiving, unsubscribed, createdAt, updatedAt}]`, plus for the owner `failures, lastProblem, params, filters, options, destinations: {email: {self, selfUnsubscribed, others: [{id, name, username, unsubscribed}]}, file: {folderId}, webhook: {host, signing, maxLabel}}` |
| `GET /api/apps/subscriptions/options` | `records:read`. `{presets, formats, kinds, attachMaxBytes, minIntervalMinutes, emailEnabled, renderAvailable}` for the Subscribe dialog |
| `POST /api/apps/subscriptions/preview` | `records:read`. `{schedule: {preset, values?} \| {cron}, timezone}, count = 5}`: `{cron, timezone, description, runs: [{at, iso, local}]}`; `422 Schedule not valid` (unknown zone, never runs, more often than the minimum interval) |
| `GET /api/apps/subscriptions/all?state&app` | `tenant:manage`. Every subscription in the tenant at labels the caller's clearance clears, with its settings (never the webhook secret) |
| `POST /api/apps/subscriptions` | `records:read`. `{name, app, kind, id, format, params?, filters?, schedule, destinations, options?}`. The object is checked as the subscriber (a report or dashboard by a check render; `503 Not available` while this build has no renderer). `201` with the subscription and, for an HMAC webhook, `webhookSecret` (once). `403` without the right a destination needs or for a host not on the list; `400` for no destination or a label above the webhook's; `409` past 50 per person. Audited `app.subscription.created` |
| `GET /api/apps/subscriptions/:id` | `records:read`. The owner, a recipient (without settings) or a tenant admin within clearance; else `404` |
| `PATCH /api/apps/subscriptions/:id` | `records:read`. `{name?, format?, schedule?, options?, state?: active \| paused}`. The owner; a tenant admin only `{state: paused}`. Resuming re-checks the object as the owner and clears the failure count. Destinations do not change (subscribe again). Audited `app.subscription.updated`, `.paused` or `.resumed` |
| `DELETE /api/apps/subscriptions/:id` | `records:read`. The owner or a tenant admin. The history stays. Audited `app.subscription.deleted`. `204` |
| `GET /api/apps/subscriptions/:id/deliveries?limit=100` | `records:read`. `{deliveries: [{id, run, at, destination, recipient: {id, name}, outcome: sent \| linked \| skipped-empty \| skipped-unchanged \| denied \| failed, reason, rows, bytes, truncated, fileId, statusCode}]}`; a recipient sees only their own emails |
| `POST /api/apps/subscriptions/:id/run` | `records:read`. The owner: one run now, re-checked as at its times. `202 {run, jobId}`; `409` while paused; `503` without a renderer. Audited `app.subscription.run` |
| `POST /api/apps/subscriptions/:id/unsubscribe` | `records:read`. The signed-in recipient (the owner too) stops their own email copies. Audited `app.subscription.unsubscribed` (`via: console`) |
| `GET /api/public/app-subscriptions/unsubscribe?t=` | Public, rate-limited, `no-store`, `noindex`. The email's link: a page saying what it stops, with a button; changes nothing. `404` for a link that is not valid |
| `POST /api/public/app-subscriptions/unsubscribe` | Public, rate-limited. `t` in the form or the query (RFC 8058 one-click from the `List-Unsubscribe-Post` header): stops that recipient's email copies only. The token is `v1.<subscription>.<user>.<HMAC>` under the platform key `link`. Audited `app.subscription.unsubscribed` (`via: link`) |

## Sprint 44 (1.8.0, Unreleased): reports and exports of an app (B-122, B-123)

Migrations `102_app_reports` (`app_reports`, `app_report_runs`) and `103_app_exports` (`app_exports`).
`apps/report-engine.ts` (the definition schema and `computeReport`, pure), `apps/reports.ts` (`s.appReports`),
`apps/export-render.ts` (XLSX, PDF, CSV and HTML from a result), `imports/xlsx-writer.ts` (the XLSX writer),
`apps/exports.ts` (`s.appExports`), routes in `routes/apps-reports.ts` (inside the apps router). Console:
`web/js/screens/apps-reports.js` (the Reports tab) and `web/js/screens/apps-export.js` (the export dialog, also on the
Records tab).

**Reports.** A definition, never SQL: `{title, notes, source, parameters, columns, computed, layout, sort, formatting,
page, rowCap, cacheMinutes}`.

- `source`: `{kind: entity, entity, view?, filters?, filterMode?, q?, state?}` (a shared saved view's filters, search,
  sort and columns first; `filters` on indexed fields), `{kind: query, query, params}` (a saved query) or
  `{kind: rest, connection, endpoint, params}`. A filter value or source parameter `{"param": "<name>"}` takes a
  report parameter; a condition whose parameter is empty is left out.
- `parameters`: up to 10 `{name, title?, type: text | number | date | boolean | choice, required, default?, options?}`.
- `computed`: up to 20 `{name, title?, formula}` in the formula language (`apps/formula.ts`) over the source's columns
  and earlier computed columns.
- `layout`: `{kind: table}`, `{kind: grouped, groupBy (1 to 3), aggregates: [{op: count | sum | avg | min | max,
  column?}], subtotals, grandTotal}` or `{kind: crosstab, rows (1 to 3), column, values (1 to 4), rowTotals,
  columnTotals, maxColumns (1 to 50, default 20; further distinct values add up in an "Other" column)}`.
- `formatting`: up to 20 `{column, when: gt | gte | lt | lte | eq | ne | between | contains | empty | notEmpty, value?,
  value2?, style: good | warn | bad | info | muted | strong, icon: none | up | down | warn | check | flag | dot, text?}`;
  the first matching rule styles a cell, shown with its symbol and words as well as colour.
- `page`: `{size: a4 | letter, orientation: portrait | landscape, breakGroups}`; `rowCap` (1 to 50000, default 10000)
  source rows read at most, beyond which the result is `truncated`; `cacheMinutes` (0 to 1440, default 15).

A run is the viewer's: entity rows through the records query with their row policies, field grants, masks, clearance
and the hidden rule; saved-query and REST rows through `s.savedQueries.run` and `s.restConnections.read` as the viewer
(who then needs `connections:query`, 403 otherwise), held to the app's label. Every cell is computed from those rows:
a row the viewer may not read never counts in a total. A masked column shows what the viewer is shown, and anything
built on it (an aggregate, a computed column, a group, a formatting rule) is masked too. The result: `{title, notes,
layout, columns: [{key, title, type, source, masked?, computed?}], lines: [{kind: row | group | subtotal | total,
level, label?, count?, cells: [{v, masked?, fmt?}]}], formats, rowsRead, rowCap, truncated, columnsFolded, params,
page, generatedAt}`.

Runs are kept per person (the last 50 per report) with their parameters sealed; the result is cached sealed for
`cacheMinutes`, readable only by the person who ran it while their clearance clears its label, then cleared by the
`apps.report-cache.sweep` job (410 after that). Audited `app.report.created`, `.updated`, `.deleted`, `.run` and
`.run.failed`.

**Exports.** `s.appExports.render(principal, {kind: view | report | dashboard | records, id, params, filters, format:
xlsx | pdf | csv | html})` returns `{filename, contentType, bytes, rows, truncated, label}`, read as `principal`
(`records:read`). `records` takes the entity id; `filters` is `{filter, q, sort}` for records, `{filter}` for views and
reports (entity sources), one filter or a list of filters that all apply. A dashboard is rendered by
`s.apps.dashboards.render` (HTML or PDF); without it, 501. XLSX: shared strings, numbers, booleans, dates and
date-times as typed cells, the header frozen, column widths, group and total rows bold with outline levels, an "About"
sheet. PDF: the chat exports' writer with the report's page setup, the header repeated on each page, a page per
top-level group when asked. CSV: cells starting with `= + - @` made inert. Masked values are written masked. Files are
sealed (`app-export:<id>`) and kept for 7 days. Audited `app.export.rendered`, `.queued`, `.ready`, `.failed`,
`.downloaded`.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/apps/{app}/reports` | `records:read`. `{reports: [{id, app, name, title, label, sourceKind, definition, version, needs, canEdit, canRun, …}], canDesign}`, at labels the caller clears |
| `POST /api/apps/{app}/reports` `{name, label?, definition}` | `apps:design` (and `connections:query` for a query or REST source). The source is checked as the designer (a view must be shared); the label is the entity's at least, the app's at most. `409` for a name in use. `201` |
| `POST /api/apps/{app}/reports/preview` `{definition, params?}` | `apps:design`. The draft over the first 200 rows as the designer, not recorded. `{result, label, preview: true}` |
| `GET /api/apps/{app}/reports/{report}` | `records:read`. One report (by id or name) |
| `PATCH /api/apps/{app}/reports/{report}` `{label?, definition?, version?}` | `apps:design`. A stale `version` is `409`; cached results of earlier versions are cleared |
| `DELETE /api/apps/{app}/reports/{report}` | `apps:design`. The report and its runs. `204` |
| `POST /api/apps/{app}/reports/{report}/run` `{params?}` | `records:read` (plus `connections:query` for a query or REST source). `{run: {id, params, rows, truncated, ms, label, cached, expiresAt}, result}`; a bad parameter is `400` (recorded as a failed run) |
| `GET /api/apps/{app}/reports/{report}/runs?all=1` | `records:read`. The caller's runs with their parameters; `all=1` for a designer: everyone's |
| `GET /api/apps/{app}/reports/{report}/runs/{run}` | `records:read`. The cached result of the caller's own run; `410` once expired |
| `POST /api/apps/{app}/exports/download` `{kind, id, params?, filters?, format}` | `records:read`. The file at once (at most 5000 rows; more is `409` with `queue: true`). `Content-Disposition: attachment` |
| `POST /api/apps/{app}/exports` `{kind, id, params?, filters?, format}` | `records:read`. Queues the job `apps.export-file` (progress on the job); access is checked again when it runs. `202` with the export |
| `GET /api/apps/{app}/exports` | `records:read`. The caller's exports of the app (the last 50) |
| `GET /api/apps/{app}/exports/{id}` | `records:read`. One of the caller's exports: `{state: queued | running | ready | failed | expired, file, rows, truncated, …}` |
| `GET /api/apps/{app}/exports/{id}/download` | `records:read`. The requester's file while their clearance clears its label; `409` before it is ready, `410` once expired |

## Sprint 56 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): cloud accounts, regions and validation (B-10002, B-10007 to B-10009)

Reads need `cloud:read`, changes `cloud:admin`; a platform account also needs `platform:manage` (checked in
`cloud/accounts.ts`), a tenant account belongs to the caller's tenant (taken from the session). Credentials are
`vault:` references and non-secret parameters only; no answer holds a secret value, and readers without
`cloud:admin` get the reference names only. Without migration `146_cloud_accounts` every route but the catalogue
answers `503` `migration_pending`. See [cloud.md](cloud.md).

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/catalogue` | `{installed, labels, residencyGeos, providers: [{id, name, modes, federation: {available, reason}, credentialFields, regions: [{region, name, zone, geo, ceiling}], features: [{id, name, checklist: [{permission, level?, usedFor}]}]}]}` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts?provider=&scope=&state=` | `{accounts: [account], residency, platformAdmin}`. An account: `{id, name, provider, scope, tenantId, providerIds, credentialMode, defaultRegion, state, description, regions: [{region, zone, ceiling, geo, isDefault}], validation, credential: {mode, params, refs}, federation, pending: [proposal], mayChange}` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts` `{name, provider, scope, providerIds, credential: {mode, params, refs}, regions: [{region, ceiling?}], defaultRegion?, description?, reason?}` | `202 {account, proposal}`: the account as `pending` (unusable) and its `account.add` proposal. `scope: platform` needs `platform:manage`. `400` for a mode the provider does not offer (`mode_unavailable`, with the reason), a literal secret (`not_a_reference`), a region it does not offer (`unknown_region`) or ids of another provider; `409` for a name taken in the scope. Audited `cloud.account.proposed` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id` | One account, as above |
| `PATCH /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id` `{description?, defaultRegion?, state?: active \| disabled, regions?, credential?, reason?}` | `200 {account, proposals: []}`, or `202` when a raised ceiling (`region.ceiling`) or another credential mode (`account.credential`) became a proposal; the rest applies at once. `409` while the account is pending. Audited `cloud.account.updated` |
| `DELETE /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id` `{reason?}` (or `?reason=`) | `202 {proposal}`: an `account.remove` proposal; nothing in the cloud is deleted |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/validate` | `{account, report: {at, ok, identity: {ok, principal, providerAccount, requestId, error}, features: [{feature, name, status: ok \| missing \| unsupported \| error, required, missing, reason}]}}`; the account moves between `active` and `attention`. `502` (`provider_error`, `provider_request_id`) and `429` (`Retry-After`) keep the last report; `503` `cloud_component_missing` without a credentials module or adapter. Audited `cloud.account.validated` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/proposals?state=&accountId=` | The proposals of the caller's tenant, of the platform (platform tenant) and every restricted override (platform admins), each with `mine` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/proposals/:id/approve` `{note?}` | Recent sign-in. Another cloud admin than the proposer; a platform account's change or a `restricted` ceiling also needs `platform:manage`. Applies it; audited `cloud.proposal.approved` and the change's own event |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/proposals/:id/reject` `{note?}` | Another cloud admin; a rejected add removes the waiting account |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/proposals/:id/withdraw` | The proposer only |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/residency` | `{geos, options}`: where the tenant's confidential data may be placed |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/residency` `{geos, reason?}` | Narrowing: `200`; widening: `202 {geos, proposal}` (`residency`). Audited `cloud.residency.updated` |

## Sprint 56 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): cloud federation issuer and credentials (B-10003 to B-10006)

Every route needs `cloud:admin`. The issuer is the platform's, so its changes (`target`, `publish`, `check`,
`rotate`) also need `platform:manage`; an account's credential routes follow the account's own rule (a platform
account also needs `platform:manage`, a tenant account belongs to the caller's tenant). Routes marked "recent" need a
recent sign-in (a session, not an API key). No answer ever holds a key, a secret or a token. Without migration
`147_cloud_federation` the issuer answers `installed: false` and federated credentials `503`.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/issuer` | `{installed, issuer, consoleIssuer, algs, azureAlg, custody, keys: [{kid, alg, state: next \| signing \| retired, custody: signer \| openbao \| sealed, createdAt, activatesAt, retiresAt, removesAt, published}], target, publication: {at, hash, kids, error}, check: {at, state: ok \| mismatch \| error \| unpublished, detail, alertedAt}, documents: {discovery, jwks}}` |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/issuer/target` `{target, secrets?}` | Recent. Where the discovery document and JWKS are published: `{kind: none}`, `{kind: console}` (served on `/cloud-issuer/...`), `{kind: s3, bucket, region, prefix?, endpoint?, accountId? \| accessKeyRef?+secretKeyRef?}`, `{kind: azure-blob, storageAccount, container? ($web), prefix?, endpoint?, accountId}`, `{kind: spaces, bucket, region, prefix?, endpoint?}`, `{kind: r2, bucket, cloudflareAccountId, prefix?, endpoint?}`. `secrets: {accessKeyId, secretAccessKey}` (S3, Spaces, R2) are vaulted at `cloud/issuer/<kind>` and the target keeps the references. Publishes at once; answers the status plus `publish` (`{published, kids, hash}` or `{published: false, error}`). Audited `cloud.issuer.target-set` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/issuer/publish` | Writes both documents now (the JWKS first). `502` when the target refuses (recorded as `publication.error`, audited `cloud.issuer.publish-failed`); audited `cloud.issuer.published` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/issuer/check` | Reads the published copy over the issuer URL and compares it with the issuer's keys: `{state, detail, missing, extra}`. A mismatch or an unreadable copy notifies the platform's cloud admins (kind `security`) and is audited `cloud.issuer.mismatch`, once per change. The job `cloud.issuer.check` does the same every `CLOUD_ISSUER_CHECK_MINUTES`, republishing first when what should be published changed |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/issuer/rotate` `{alg?: ES256 \| RS256, immediate?}` | Recent. A new key, published at once; it signs once the published JWKS holds it and `CLOUD_ISSUER_PUBLISH_LEAD_MINUTES` have passed. `immediate` (a suspected compromise) signs with it now. The retired key stays published until every session bought with it has ended. `{next: {kid, alg, state, activatesAt}, previous, published, publishError}`; audited `cloud.issuer.rotated` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/secrets` `{scope: platform \| tenant, provider, values, expiresAt?}` | Stores secret values in the vault (platform scope, `cloud/secrets/<scope>/<id>`, sealed, `restricted`) and answers `201 {refs, version}` to name in an account's credential. `values`: AWS `{accessKeyId (AKIA…), secretAccessKey}`, Azure `{clientSecret}`, DigitalOcean and Cloudflare `{token}`. `scope: platform` needs `platform:manage`. Audited `cloud.credential.stored` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/credential` | `{mode, kind: federated \| aws-keys \| azure-secret \| azure-certificate \| token, secrets (names), roles (AWS federated: read, deploy, billing), lastUsedAt, lastUsedPurpose, rotation: {automatic, by, state: idle \| overlap \| failed, rotatedAt, overlapUntil, lastError}, expiresAt, notice}` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/setup` | The setup helper: `{provider, issuer, subject, audience, available, reason, steps: [{title, commands?, file?: {name, json}, note?}]}`. AWS: the IAM OIDC provider, the trust policy (conditions on `aud` and `sub`), the read, deploy (conditioned on the `exprsn:*` tags) and billing policies, the roles. Azure: the federated identity credential (app registration or user-assigned managed identity) and the role assignments (Reader, Cost Management Reader, Contributor on the managed resource groups). DigitalOcean and Cloudflare: `available: false` with the reason |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/secret` `{values, expiresAt?}` | Recent. A guided replace: the values are written as a new version where the account's references point (moved to `cloud/accounts/<id>` when they point elsewhere, `refsChanged: true`); every instance drops its cached credential. Audited `cloud.credential.replaced` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/rotate` | Recent. AWS keys: create, verify, switch, and delete the old key after `CLOUD_AWS_KEY_OVERLAP_MINUTES`. Azure secret: Graph `addPassword`, verify, switch, `removePassword` after the overlap. `409` for tokens (a person replaces them), certificates and federated accounts. `{rotated, overlapUntil, detail, credential}`; audited `cloud.credential.rotated` (or `.rotation-failed`) |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/azure-certificate` `{days?}` | Recent. A client certificate from the tenant's issuing CA (the platform tenant's for a platform account) through an active client profile accepting RSA-2048, its key made and kept by the signer or OpenBao transit: `201 {ref, certificatePem, thumbprint, notAfter}`. Upload the certificate to the app registration and name `ref` as the credential's `certificate`. `409` without custody, an issuing CA or a profile |

Public, outside `/api`, only while the publication target is `console` (else `404`):

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /cloud-issuer/.well-known/openid-configuration` | `{issuer, jwks_uri, response_types_supported, subject_types_supported, id_token_signing_alg_values_supported, claims_supported}` |
| `GET /cloud-issuer/jwks.json` | The issuer's next, signing and retired keys (public members only) |

`s.cloud.credentials.for(account, purpose)` (`purpose`: `validate`, `read`, `deploy`, `billing`) answers
`{kind: 'aws', accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken?, expiresAt}` (federated: a session for the purpose's role,
`readRoleArn`/`deployRoleArn`/`billingRoleArn` else `roleArn`; vaulted: the key pair, `expiresAt: null`),
`{kind: 'azure', tenantId, getToken(scope)}` (scopes per purpose: validate ARM; read ARM and Cognitive Services;
deploy ARM, Cognitive Services and Storage; billing ARM) or `{kind: 'token', token, accountId?}`. A pending account
is used to validate only; a disabled one not at all (`409`).

## Sprint 57 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): deployments, plans, the operation journal and verify (B-10102 to B-10105, B-10701)

Reads need `cloud:read`; plans, applies and verifies `cloud:deploy`, and a platform deployment (one on a platform
account) also `platform:manage` (checked in `cloud/deployments.ts`). Platform deployments are seen like platform
accounts; tenant deployments by their tenant only. Applying needs a recent sign-in in a browser session. Without
migration `148_cloud_journal` every route answers `503` `migration_pending`. Creating a deployment from a spec is
B-10201's `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments` (over `s.cloud.deployments.create`). See [cloud.md](cloud.md).

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments?accountId=&state=` | `{deployments: [deployment], installed}`. A deployment: `{id, tenantId, scope, accountId, provider, name, region, label, description, state: draft \| planned \| applying \| applied \| ready \| degraded \| failed \| destroying \| destroyed, health: unknown \| healthy \| degraded, spec, endpoints: {publicUrl?, tlsName?, app?, redis?}, observedVersion, currentPlanId, verify, lease: {holder, until} \| null, createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt}` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id` | One deployment, with `currentPlan: {id, hash, state, summary, expiresAt}` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/graph` | `{deployment, resources, edges: [{from, to}]}`. A resource: `{key, type, region, providerId, locator, desired, observed, observedHash, observedAt, dependsOn, protect, tags, state: planned \| creating \| ready \| updating \| deleting \| deleted \| failed \| missing, createdByOperation, createdByAudit, lastVerified: {desired, observed, at} \| null}` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/plans?limit=` | The deployment's plans, newest first; an open plan past its 60 minutes reads `expired`, one made before the observed state changed `stale` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/plans` `{desired: [{key, type, spec, dependsOn?, protect?, region?, name?, network?, tags?: {workspace?, pool?}}]}` | `201` the plan: `{id, hash, purpose, desired, steps: [{key, action: create \| update \| replace \| delete \| noop, changes: [{path, before, after, forcesReplace}], reason?, type, region, protect, dependsOn, providerId, adopts?, unavailable?: {support, reason}, blocked?}], summary, estimate: {monthly, delta, currency?, prices} \| null, observedVersion, observedDigest, state: open, applicable, blockers, expiresAt}`. Every region is checked against the account's allow-list, ceilings and residency first (`403` step `zone`), then the provider is read. `400` for a cycle, an unknown dependency or a duplicate key. Audited `cloud.plan.created` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/plans/:planId` | One plan |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/plans/:planId/apply` `{hash}` | Recent sign-in. `202 {plan, job: {id, type: cloud.apply}}`. `409` with `reason`: `plan_hash_mismatch`, `plan_expired`, `plan_not_open`, `plan_unavailable` (`blockers`: unavailable types, protected deletes), `apply_in_progress` (another apply holds the lease), `plan_stale` (a resource changed out of band; `freshPlan: {id, hash, summary, expiresAt}` is offered). Audited `cloud.apply.started` (or `cloud.plan.refused`) |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/operations?planId=&key=&after=&limit=` | The journal, oldest first: `{operations: [{id, planId, resourceKey, step: create \| update \| delete \| replace.delete \| replace.create \| poll \| refresh \| verify, idempotencyKey, clientToken, providerRequestId, attempt, state: started \| pending \| succeeded \| adopted \| failed \| cancelled, error, handle, providerId, auditId, jobId, worker, at}]}` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/verify` | `202 {job: {id, type: cloud.verify, state}}`; the report lands on the deployment's `verify`: `{at, ok, resources: [{id, key, status: pass \| fail \| unknown \| skipped, detail}], checks: [...], rollback: {offered, reason}}` |

Jobs: `cloud.apply` (`{planId, deploymentId}`; queued by apply, at most five attempts, resumes from the journal),
`cloud.poll` (`{deploymentId}`; settles operations left pending with nobody polling them), `cloud.verify`
(`{deploymentId}`; queued after every successful apply). Audit: `cloud.deployment.created`, `.updated`, `.ready`,
`.degraded`; `cloud.plan.created`, `.refused`; `cloud.apply.started`, `.succeeded`, `.failed`, `.cancelled`;
`cloud.resource.created`, `.adopted`, `.updated`, `.replaced`, `.deleted`, `.failed` (each with the journal step as
`detail.operation` and the provider's `detail.providerRequestId`); `cloud.verify.passed`, `.failed`.

## Sprint 57 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): drift, destroy, rollback and orphans (B-10106, B-10107)

Reads need `cloud:read`; drift checks and decisions, orphan sweeps, adoptions and ignores `cloud:deploy`; destroy and
rollback `cloud:deploy` with a recent sign-in in a browser session; approving or refusing the deletion of a protected
resource and deleting an orphan `cloud:admin` (approving and deleting with a recent sign-in). A platform deployment also
needs `platform:manage` (checked in the services). Without migration `149_cloud_lifecycle` every route answers `503`
`migration_pending` (without 148, the deployments' own `503`). See [cloud.md](cloud.md).

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/drift?state=` | `{findings: [{id, deploymentId, kind: field \| missing \| unmanaged, key, type, providerId, path, desired, observed, detail, state: open \| reverted \| adopted \| ignored \| resolved, decidedBy, decidedAt, note, planId, firstSeen, lastSeen}]}`, newest first |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/drift/check` | Reads every managed resource now: `{checked, findings (open), fresh: [id], resolved}`. Provider failures `502`, throttling `429`. Audited `cloud.drift.detected` when something new was found |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/drift/:findingId/decide` `{decision: revert \| adopt \| ignore, note?, apply?}` | `{finding, plan, job}`. `revert`: a plan back to the desired graph (purpose `revert`; an unmanaged resource is taken into the graph and the plan deletes it), applied at once with `apply: true` (a recent sign-in; `job: {id, type: cloud.apply}`). `adopt`: the observed value becomes the desired one (a missing resource leaves the graph, an unmanaged one joins it). `ignore`: kept out of later runs. `409` for a finding already decided. Audited `cloud.drift.decided` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/destroy` | `{destroys: [{id, deploymentId, state: running \| waiting \| finished \| failed \| cancelled, reason, requestedBy, actingUser, protected: [{key, type, providerId, snapshot: {state: none \| pending \| taken \| failed \| unsupported, reason, name, id, at}, approval: {state: pending \| approved \| rejected, by, at, note}, deleted}], rounds: [{planId, jobId, at}], jobId, note, createdAt, updatedAt, finishedAt}]}` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/destroy` `{reason?}` | Recent sign-in. `202 {destroy, job: {id, type: cloud.destroy}}`: deletes everything in reverse dependency order, through destroy plans applied as `cloud.apply`; protected resources (and what they depend on) wait for a second admin. `409` with `reason` `destroy_in_progress` or `apply_in_progress`. Audited `cloud.destroy.requested` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/destroy/:destroyId/protected/:key/approve` `{note?}` | `cloud:admin`, recent sign-in, not the person who asked (`403` step `dual_control`). `{destroy, job}`: the final snapshot is taken, then the resource is deleted. `409` `snapshot_unsupported` with the reason where the adapter has no snapshot for the type. Audited `cloud.destroy.approved`, then `cloud.destroy.snapshot` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/destroy/:destroyId/protected/:key/reject` `{note?}` | `cloud:admin`. Ends the destroy (`cancelled`); the resource and what it depends on are kept. Audited `cloud.destroy.rejected`, `cloud.destroy.finished` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/destroy/:destroyId/cancel` | Ends a destroy that waits for approvals (`409` while a round runs) |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/rollback` | Recent sign-in. `202 {plan, job}`: every resource that is not protected back to its desired spec at the last passing verify, resources added since deleted (`job` null when nothing changes or the plan cannot be applied). `409` `never_verified`. Audited `cloud.rollback.started` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/orphans?state=` | `{orphans: [{id, accountId, provider, type, providerId, name, region, deploymentName, tags, observed, state: open \| adopted \| deleted \| ignored \| gone, deploymentId, decidedBy, decidedAt, firstSeen, lastSeen}]}`: the account's orphans tagged for this deployment or for none that exists |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/orphans/sweep` | Lists the account's tagged resources in every allowed region now: `{fresh, gone, orphans}`. Audited `cloud.orphan.found` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/orphans/:orphanId/adopt` | `{orphan, resource}`: into this deployment's graph, its observed state as the desired one. Audited `cloud.orphan.adopted` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/orphans/:orphanId/ignore` | `{orphan}`. Audited `cloud.orphan.ignored` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/orphans/:orphanId/delete` | `cloud:admin`, recent sign-in. `{orphan, done}`: deleted at the provider, journalled under the deployment. `409` `protected_type` for a database. Audited `cloud.orphan.deleted` |

Jobs: `cloud.drift` (`{deploymentId}`, every `CLOUD_DRIFT_MINUTES`), `cloud.destroy` (`{destroyId}`, queued again
when a round's apply ends), `cloud.rollback` (`{deploymentId, failedPlan}`, after a failed apply of a verified
deployment, `CLOUD_AUTO_ROLLBACK`), `cloud.orphans` (`{accountId}`, every `CLOUD_ORPHAN_SWEEP_HOURS`). Provider
calls of every cloud route and job now go through per-API-class buckets and a circuit breaker per provider and account:
a call refused while the breaker is open fails with `503` `circuit_open` and `retryAfterSeconds`.

## Sprint 57 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): deployment specs, network foundation and estimates (B-10201, B-10202, B-10601)

Deploying Exprsn-AI is platform-only: both routes need `cloud:deploy` and `platform:manage`; creating also needs a
recent sign-in in a browser session. A spec is validated against its accounts before any provider call: the account's
state, scope and region allow-list, the label ceilings and residency (`assertRegionAllows`'s decision), the zones'
ceilings, the last validation's permission report, the GPU kinds the provider offers and the spec's limits. See
[cloud.md](cloud.md).

A spec: `{name, description?, target: {provider: aws | azure | digitalocean, accountId, region}, label? (internal),
compute: {shape: kubernetes | vm | container, size: small | medium | large}, data?: {mode: provision, engine?:
postgres, cache?: true} | {mode: existing, databaseUrlRef, redisUrlRef?} | {mode: onprem, cidrs, ports?}, frontDoor:
{kind: cloudflare, accountId, hostname, zone, plan?: free | pro | business} | {kind: acme, hostname, zone} | {kind:
byo, hostname}, gpuPools?: [{name, gpu: l4 | a10 | h100, min?, max?, busyHours?}] (at most 4), zones?: {edge, app,
data, inference}, network?: {cidr (10.64.0.0/16)}, estimate?: {hours?, storageGb?, egressGb?}}`. References
(`databaseUrlRef`, `redisUrlRef`) are `vault:` references, never values.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/validate-spec` | The wizard's dry run; calls no provider and changes nothing: `{valid, problems: [{path, check, message}], unavailable: [{key, type, support, reason}], resources (the rendered graph), firewalls: [{zone, key, ingress, egress, egressDenied}], notes, frontDoor: {accountId, resources, planned: false, note} \| null, estimate}` (the estimate from cached and sheet prices only). `check` is `state`, `use`, `region`, `ceiling`, `residency`, `provider`, `scope`, `zone`, `permission`, `offer`, `limit`, `front_door`, `network` or `name` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments` | `201 {deployment, plan, firewalls, unavailable, notes, frontDoor}`: creates the deployment with its spec (`s.cloud.deployments.create`), renders its graph and plans it (`s.cloud.plans.create`, which reads the provider through the adapters; the plan carries the estimate). Refused before any provider call: `403` step `zone` (`check`: `state`, `use`, `region`, `ceiling`, `residency`; `reason: placement_refused`, every problem in `problems`) when a placement check fails, else `422` `invalid_spec` with `problems`; `422` `public_data` if a data resource would have a public address; `503` `migration_pending` without migration 148. Audited `cloud.deployment.created`, `cloud.deployment.spec` (shape, size, data mode, front door, GPU pools, resource count, zones) and `cloud.plan.created` |

A plan's `estimate` (B-10601): `{monthly, delta, before, currency, assumptions: {hours, storageGb, egressGb, notes},
prices: [{sku, unit: hour | month | gb-month | gb, price, currency, source: aws-price-list | azure-retail-prices |
digitalocean-sizes | price-sheet, ref, date, region, stale?}], lines: [{key, type, sku, unit, quantity, monthly,
note?}], cache, at}`. The currency is the account's billing currency (USD by default); a price in another currency is
listed but not converted or totalled. Job: `cloud.prices.refresh` (daily, as the platform tenant; the preset SKUs of
every active platform account that has a deployment; skipped without migration `150_cloud_prices`).

## Sprint 58 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): cloud budgets, alerts, the hard stop and overrides (B-10602)

A monthly budget per cloud account (`cloud/budgets.ts`, `s.cloud.budgets`; migration `152_cloud_budgets`, not
registered yet: every route answers `503` `migration_pending` until it is applied, and no plan is refused for budget).
Reads need `finops:read` or `cloud:read` (the accounts one may see); setting and removing `finops:manage`; proposing,
rejecting and revoking an override `finops:manage` or `cloud:admin`; approving one the same from a second admin with a
recent sign-in in a browser session. A platform account's changes also need `platform:manage`. See [cloud.md](cloud.md).

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/budgets` | `{budgets: [{account: {id, name, provider, scope}, status, pending: [override]}]}`: every budget on the accounts one may see |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/budget` | `{installed, account: {id, name, currency}, budget \| null, status \| null, overrides, mayChange}`. `status`: `{budget: {accountId, amount, currency, hardStop: actual \| forecast \| off}, actual, forecast, pctActual, pctForecast, stopped, override, alerts: [{month, basis, threshold, spend, amount, currency, firedAt}], source}`; `actual` and `forecast` are `{amount, currency, source: estimate \| billing, deployments, excluded: [{deploymentId, reason}], month, at}` |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/budget` `{amount, currency?, hardStop? (actual)}` | Sets or changes the budget (the currency defaults to the account's billing currency, USD, open decision 17); answers the status and sends the alerts already due. A changed amount or currency starts the month's alerts afresh. Audited `cloud.budget.set` or `cloud.budget.updated` |
| `DELETE /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/budget` | `204`; no more alerts or hard stop. Audited `cloud.budget.removed` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/budget/overrides` | `{overrides: [{id, state: pending \| approved \| rejected \| withdrawn \| expired \| revoked, active, reason, hours, proposedBy, proposedAt, decidedBy, decidedAt, note, startsAt, expiresAt, mine}]}` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/budget/overrides` `{reason (10 to 500 characters), hours? (1 to 168, default 168)}` | `202` a pending override; `409` `override_pending` or `override_active` when one is waiting or running; `409` without a budget. Audited `cloud.budget.override.proposed`; the other admins get a `cloud.budget` notice |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/budget/overrides/:oid/approve` `{note?}` | A second admin (never the proposer: `403` step `dual-control`): the hard stop is lifted from now for the override's hours (at most 7 days). Audited `cloud.budget.override.approved` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/budget/overrides/:oid/reject` `{note?}` | Audited `cloud.budget.override.rejected`; the proposer withdraws instead |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/budget/overrides/:oid/withdraw` | The proposer only. Audited `cloud.budget.override.withdrawn` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/budget/overrides/:oid/revoke` `{note?}` | Ends an active override at once. Audited `cloud.budget.override.revoked` |

The hard stop: at or past 100 % (of actual spend, or of the forecast with `hardStop: forecast`), a plan that adds
monthly cost gets the blocker `budget_exceeded: …` (`applicable: false`), and `POST
/api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/plans/:planId/apply` answers `409` with `reason: budget_exceeded`, `budget: {amount,
currency, actual, forecast, pctActual, pctForecast, stopped, hardStop, override}` and `costReasons` (audited
`cloud.plan.refused`). Apply asks again, so the same plan is accepted once an override is approved. Adding cost: a
positive estimated delta in the budget's currency; without an estimate, a create or replace of anything priced; and a
GPU node group scaled above its minimum whatever the estimate (open decision 10). Destroy plans, scale-down and plans
with a zero or negative delta always pass.

Alerts: at 50, 80 and 100 % of actual and of forecast spend, each once per account and month (UTC), as the audit event
`cloud.budget.alert` (`{account, name, month, basis, threshold, percent, spend, amount, currency, source, hardStop,
stopped}`; webhooks subscribed to `cloud.*`, `cloud.budget.*` or `*` receive it) and a notice of kind `cloud.budget`
(Administration) to the tenant's FinOps readers and cloud admins, by email too at 100 %. Job: `cloud.budgets.check`
(every `CLOUD_BUDGET_CHECK_MINUTES`, 60, and after every successful apply), which also marks ended overrides
`expired` (audited `cloud.budget.override.expired`). Since Sprint 59 (B-10603) spend comes from the ingested billing
rows for an account with a successful billing fetch in the last three days, and from the applied plans' estimates,
prorated over the month, otherwise; `actual.source` and `status.source` say which (`actual.basis` why; a billing figure
also has `billedThrough`, and its forecast `runRate`).

## Sprint 59 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): managed databases, extensions, snapshots and restores (B-10301, B-10303, B-10307)

A deployment's managed databases (`database` resources: RDS and Aurora, Azure Flexible Server, DigitalOcean Managed
PostgreSQL and MySQL; `cloud/databases.ts`). Reads need `cloud:read`; a snapshot, a schedule and a restore
`cloud:deploy` (the snapshot and the restore with a recent sign-in). A platform deployment also needs
`platform:manage`. Only the schedule needs migration `153_cloud_databases` (not registered yet: `503`
`migration_pending` until it is applied). `:key` is the database's graph key. See [cloud.md](cloud.md), "Managed
databases".

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/databases` | `{databases: [{key, providerId, state, engine, service, version, size, ha, storageGb, backups: {days, window}, maintenanceWindow, deletionProtection, publicAccess, privateEndpoint, extensions, parameters, endpoint, schedule}]}` (what the provider reports, else the desired spec) |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/databases/:key/extensions?names=vector,postgis` | The extension check (default: the database's `extensions`): `{key, engine, allAvailable, extensions: [{name, state: available \| not_allowed \| not_offered, source: allow_list \| supported_list, detail?}]}` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/databases/:key/snapshots` | The provider's backups and Exprsn-AI's snapshots, newest first: `{key, currency, monthly, snapshots: [{id, name, kind: manual \| automated \| restore_point \| copy, state, createdAt, sizeGb, expiresAt, final, billing, cost: {monthly, currency, sku, unit, price, source, date, unverified, note?}, retention}]}`; `monthly` totals confirmed prices only |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/databases/:key/snapshots` `{note?}` | Recent sign-in. Takes a snapshot now: `202 {job}` (`cloud.db.snapshot`). Audited `cloud.database.snapshot.requested`, then `.taken` or `.failed` |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/databases/:key/schedule` `{everyHours: 1..720, keep: 1..100, enabled?}` | Sets the snapshot schedule: `{schedule: {everyHours, keep, enabled, nextAt, lastAt, lastSnapshot, lastError}}`. A run deletes the schedule's own snapshots beyond `keep`. On DigitalOcean the run fails with `provider_schedule` (its daily backups are the schedule). Audited `cloud.database.schedule.set` (and `cloud.database.snapshot.pruned`) |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/databases/:key/snapshots/:snapshotId/restore` `{key?, size?}` | Recent sign-in. Restores a snapshot (URL-encoded id) to a new instance beside the source: `202 {job, key}` (`cloud.db.restore`); the new database joins the graph as `key` (default `<key>-restored`), protected. Audited `cloud.database.restore.requested`, then `cloud.database.restored` or `.restore.failed` |

Plans: a `database` step that would delete or replace a database with deletion protection, or turn it off, is
`blocked` (the plan is not applicable; apply answers `409` `plan_unavailable`), and a database asking for an extension
the provider does not offer is a blocker naming it. An adapter's own delete of a protected database without a fresh
final snapshot fails with `final_snapshot_required`.

## Sprint 59 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): cloud billing ingestion and estimate against actual (B-10603)

Daily cost rows per cloud account (`cloud/costs.ts`, `s.cloud.costs`; migration `155_cloud_costs`, not registered yet:
every route answers `503` `migration_pending` until it is applied, nothing is fetched and budgets stay on estimates).
Reads need `finops:read` or `cloud:read` and show only the accounts and deployments one may see; "fetch now" needs
`finops:manage` (a platform account also `platform:manage`). Periods are UTC days, `from` inclusive and `to`
exclusive (`YYYY-MM-DD`, at most 400 days; default this month); amounts are in the currency the provider billed in,
never converted. See [cloud.md](cloud.md#billing-ingestion-b-10603).

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/costs` | `{installed, accounts: [{account: {id, name, provider, scope}, month, currency, monthToDate: {<currency>: amount}, budgetSource: billing \| estimate, reason, eligible: null \| why not fetched, lastFetch: {at, state, error, manual} \| null, estimate, actual}]}` (estimate and actual: this month so far, account currency) |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/costs?from&to&by&deployment` | `by=row` (default): `{account, from, to, rows: [{accountId, provider, deploymentId \| null, allocation, service, day, amount, currency, source: aws-cost-explorer \| azure-cost-management \| digitalocean-invoice \| digitalocean-preview, estimated, fetchedAt}]}`; `by=day \| deployment \| service`: `{..., by, groups: [{key, deploymentId, currency, amount, estimated}]}` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/costs/estimate-vs-actual?from&to` | `{account, from, to, currency, deployments: [{deploymentId, name, state, estimate, actual, difference, ratio, excluded}], unattributed, otherCurrencies: {<currency>: amount}, total: {estimate, actual}}`: the applied plans' estimates prorated over the period up to now against the ingested rows |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/costs/fetches` | `{eligible, billing: {billing, lastFetchedAt, reason}, fetches: [{id, key, manual, state: running \| ok \| failed, attempts, window: {from, to}, requests, rows, totals, note, error, requestedBy, startedAt, finishedAt}]}` (the last 20) |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/costs/fetch` | `202 {jobId, key}`: queues `cloud.costs.ingest` for the account now. `409` `billing_not_available` when the account is not active, its last validation lacks billing read access, or (a Cloudflare account, since Sprint 61) it has no Cloudflare account id; `409` `costs_recent` (with `retryAt`) when it was already fetched by hand this hour (each fetch is a paid request on AWS). Audited `cloud.costs.fetch.requested` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/costs?from&to` | One deployment: `{deployment: {id, name, state}, ...estimate-vs-actual for it, rows}` |

Job `cloud.costs.ingest` (daily, as the platform tenant; `{accountId, manual?}` for one account): AWS Cost Explorer
`GetCostAndUsage` (one request per account per UTC day, grouped by the `exprsn:deployment` tag and service), Azure Cost
Management `query` by the same tag key, DigitalOcean balance and invoice items attributed by resource id; it replaces the
rows of the days it covers (the last 14 days and the current month). Audited `cloud.costs.ingested` and
`cloud.costs.failed`.


## Sprint 59 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): document and key-value connections, cloud databases as data connections (B-10304, B-10306)

Five more data connection engines (`GET /api/admin/connections/engines` lists them; Register, the data browser and
the saved queries take them as every other engine): `documentdb`, `cosmos-mongodb`, `do-mongodb` (the MongoDB query
model: `{"find": ...}` or `{"aggregate": ...}`), `dynamodb` (PartiQL `SELECT ... WHERE <partition key> = ...`, or
`{"Query": {...}}`, or `{"ExecuteStatement": {...}}`) and `cosmos-nosql` (one SQL `SELECT`, or `{"container", "query",
"parameters"}`). Writes, table changes, scans and anything else are refused by classification (`422` `Write refused`,
`DDL refused` or `Object outside the allow-list` for a denied operation), audited `connection.query.refused`, with
nothing sent. Options: DocumentDB `{tlsCaFile?, readPreference: secondaryPreferred|primaryPreferred|primary}`, vCore
and DigitalOcean MongoDB `{tlsCaFile?}`, DynamoDB `{region?, consistentRead: off|on, maxPages}`, Cosmos DB for NoSQL
`{auth: key|entra-service-principal, entraTenantId?}`. DynamoDB's credential is an access key id and secret access key
(sealed or `vault:`); Cosmos DB's an account key, or a service principal's client id and secret.

Cloud data connections (`cloud/discovery.ts`; `cloud:read` and `connections:manage` together; migration
`156_cloud_connections`):

| Route | What |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/discover?region&kind&refresh=1` | `{instances: [{providerId, provider, kind: rds\|aurora\|documentdb\|dynamodb\|azure-postgres\|azure-mysql\|cosmos-nosql\|cosmos-mongodb\|do-database, name, region, providerEngine, engine \| null, state, endpoints: {private: {host, port} \| null, public}, database, adminUser, tls, auth: [password\|lease\|rds-iam\|entra\|account\|key], managed, deployment: {id, key} \| null, connections: [{id, name}]}], cached, at}`: the account's managed databases and stores, through the adapters (RDS, DocumentDB and DynamoDB; ARM flexible servers, Cosmos DB accounts and vCore clusters; DigitalOcean database clusters). Kept ten minutes (`refresh=1` asks again). `409` for a pending or disabled account or a Cloudflare one; `403 step: zone` for a region off the account's list. Audited `cloud.discovery.run` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/connect` `{providerId \| deploymentId + resourceKey, name, auth, database?, endpoint: private\|public, dbUser?, adminPassword?, adminPasswordRef?, schemas?, leaseTtlSeconds?, caPem?, zone, label, rowLimit, timeoutS}` | `201 {connection, link: {connectionId, accountId, providerId, kind, region, endpoint, host, auth, dbUser, leaseEngine, leaseRole, caBundle, deployment, createdAt}, notes}`: a data connection to the instance; the endpoint's host is added to the tenant's allowed hosts with it (and taken out if the connection is not made). `auth`: `password` (the admin password to the vault at `connections/cloud/<name>/admin`; DigitalOcean's from its API), `lease` (a B-1704 lease engine `cloud-<name>` with role `conn`: queries run as leased users, dropped when their lease ends), `rds-iam` and `entra` (short-lived tokens from the account's credential for `dbUser`), `account` (DynamoDB, Cosmos DB: the account's own credential), `key` (Cosmos DB's read-only key to the vault). `409` when the instance does not offer the option, has no such endpoint, or its engine is not installed; `403` for the clearance, zone, region ceiling or residency, or a vault policy that refuses the write; `503 migration_pending` without migration 156. Audited `cloud.connection.connected`, `connection.registered` (`via: cloud-connect`), `tenant.hosts.updated` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/connections` | `{links: [...]}`: the tenant's connections made from the account |

## Sprint 59 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): moving this install's database, caches as REDIS_URL (B-10302, B-10305)

Moving this install's own database onto a managed PostgreSQL (`cloud/db-move.ts`, `s.cloud.dbMoves`; no migration:
moves are kept in `platform_state`). Every route needs `cloud:admin` and `platform:manage`; a dry run, asking,
approving, rolling back and finishing need a recent sign-in, and a move is approved by a second admin, never the one
who asked (`403` step `dual-control`). One move is open at a time (`409`). The target's URL comes from a `vault:`
reference the asker can read (`target: {kind: vault, ref}`) or a deployment's wired database (`target: {kind:
deployment, deploymentId, key?}`); `caRef` names the provider's CA bundle in the vault (written to a file beside
`DATABASE_URL_FILE` and used as `sslrootcert`). No answer carries a URL, a password or a CA. These routes answer during
the read-only window; every other change answers `503` `read_only_window` with `Retry-After` until the move switches
or is rolled back. See [cloud.md](cloud.md#own-database-and-caches-b-10302-b-10305) and
[runbooks/db-move.md](runbooks/db-move.md).

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/db-moves` | `{moves: [...], window: {moveId, openedAt, leaseUntil, phase: cutover \| switched} \| null}`, newest first |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/db-moves/:id` | `{move: {id, state: planned \| awaiting_approval \| approved \| running \| failed \| switched \| finished \| rolled_back \| rejected, dryRun, source, view: {client, host, port, database, provider?, size?}, caFile, switchFile, instances, windowBoundMs, keepOldMs, checks: [{id, ok, detail}], budget: {maxConnections, reserved, poolMax, instances, headroom, required, available, ok, source: live \| size}, estimate: {windowMs, rows, basis}, steps: {preflight, schema, read_only, backup, restore, verify, migrate_check, switch: {state, startedAt, finishedAt, detail, attempts}}, backupId, window: {openedAt, closedAt}, switchedAt, keepOldUntil, oldReadOnly: database \| flag, requestedBy, approvedBy, heldAuditEntries, running, error}}` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/db-moves/dry-run` `{target, caRef?, instances?, windowMinutes?}` | The preflight and the window's estimate; changes nothing. `201 {move}` (`dryRun: true`). Audited `cloud.db_move.dry_run` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/db-moves` `{target, caRef?, instances?, windowMinutes?, keepOldDays?, note?}` | Asks for a move: the dry run first, `409` `preflight_failed` with `checks` when a check fails (audited `cloud.db_move.refused`); else `201 {move}` (`awaiting_approval`). Audited `cloud.db_move.planned`, `cloud.db_move.requested` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/db-moves/:id/approve` `{note?}` | A second admin. `202 {move, job}` (`cloud.db.move`). Audited `cloud.db_move.approved`; the run `cloud.db_move.started`, `.switched` or `.failed` (entries made while the window is open are written when it closes, to the new database after the switch) |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/db-moves/:id/reject` `{note?}` | Audited `cloud.db_move.rejected` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/db-moves/:id/rollback` `{discardNewWrites?, note?}` | Before the switch: the window closes. After it, within the keep window: the URL file goes back to `<file>.previous`, the old database is writable again, the new one is put in a window; `409` `writes_since_switch` (with `changed`) when the new database took writes, unless `discardNewWrites`. Audited `cloud.db_move.rolled_back` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/db-moves/:id/finish` | Ends the keep window: the old database may be dropped. Audited `cloud.db_move.finished` |

Job `cloud.db.move` (`{moveId}`, three attempts, resumable: each step is recorded as it finishes). The CLI
`exprsn-ai db:move` runs the same steps on the host without the dual control (`--dry-run`, `--status`, `--resume`,
`--rollback [--discard-new-writes]`, `--finish`).

Caches (B-10305): the `cache` resource type is built on AWS (ElastiCache, MemoryDB described only), Azure (Azure Cache
for Redis, Azure Managed Redis) and DigitalOcean (Managed Valkey); there are no cache routes of their own. A plan whose
desired cache is in cluster mode, has a `maxmemory-policy` other than `noeviction` or has TLS off is not applicable
(the blocker `cache: refused as REDIS_URL (<code>): <reason>`), and `/readyz` reports a configured Redis that breaks a
rule as `checks.redis: "incompatible: <what>"` without answering 503. Audited `cloud.cache.wired`, `cloud.cache.refused`,
`cloud.data.wired`.

## Sprint 58 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): Kubernetes releases, upgrades by digest and database snapshots (B-10203, B-10207)

A Kubernetes deployment's Helm releases, its upgrades and the database snapshots taken before them
(`cloud/releases.ts`, `cloud/upgrades.ts`; migration `151_cloud_releases`, not registered yet: every route answers
`503` `migration_pending` until it is applied). Reads need `cloud:read`; installing, planning and applying upgrades and
asking for a restore `cloud:deploy`; approving or refusing a restore `cloud:admin`. A platform deployment also needs
`platform:manage`. See [cloud.md](cloud.md), "Kubernetes target and upgrades".

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/releases` | The release's revisions, newest first: `{releases: [{release, namespace, revision, chartVersion, repository, digest, valuesHash, state, reason, upgradeId, address, error}]}` (`state` deployed, failed, superseded, rolled_back; `reason` install, upgrade, rollback) |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/releases/install` | Recent sign-in. Installs the release again (after a failure). `202 {job}` (`cloud.release`). `409` `not_kubernetes` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/upgrades` | The deployment's upgrades with their steps |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/upgrades` `{image \| imageDigest, externalBackup?: {ref, note?}}` | Plans an upgrade to a new image by digest: `201 {upgrade, plan}` (the plan's purpose `upgrade`; apply it by its hash). `409` with `reason`: `upgrade_unsupported` (not Kubernetes), `no_release`, `same_release`, `upgrade_in_progress`, `snapshot_unsupported` (the adapter takes no database snapshot, with its reason), `snapshot_unavailable` (a database the deployment does not manage and no `externalBackup`), `infrastructure_differs`. Audited `cloud.upgrade.planned` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/upgrades/:upgradeId` | One upgrade: `state` planned, running, succeeded, rolled_back, blocked, failed; `steps` snapshot, migrate_check, rollout, verify (and rollback) with their state and detail; `snapshotId`, `note` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/upgrades/:upgradeId/apply` `{hash}` | Recent sign-in. Applies the upgrade's plan by its hash (the planner's refusals apply: `plan_hash_mismatch`, `plan_stale`, `apply_in_progress`, the budget's hard stop); `cloud.upgrade` follows. `202 {upgrade, job}`. Audited `cloud.upgrade.started`, `.snapshot`, `.succeeded`, `.rolled_back`, `.blocked`, `.failed` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/snapshots` | The database snapshots taken before upgrades (`kind` provider or external), with `restorable` and the restore's state |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/snapshots/:snapshotId/restore` `{note?}` | Recent sign-in. Asks for a restore (the other cloud admins are told). `409` `restore_external` (the operator's own backup), `not_restorable`. Audited `cloud.snapshot.restore.requested` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/snapshots/:snapshotId/restore/approve` `{note?}` | `cloud:admin`, recent sign-in, never the person who asked (`403` step `dual_control`). `202 {snapshot, job}` (`cloud.snapshot.restore`). Audited `cloud.snapshot.restore.approved`, then `cloud.snapshot.restored` or `cloud.snapshot.restore.failed` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/snapshots/:snapshotId/restore/reject` `{note?}` | `cloud:admin`. Audited `cloud.snapshot.restore.rejected` |

## Sprint 60 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): Bedrock model servers and the cloud catalogue import (B-10501, B-10504)

Amazon Bedrock as a gateway model server (`kind: bedrock`, `gateway/bedrock-server.ts` over `cloud/bedrock.ts`) and
the cloud catalogue import (`cloud/model-import.ts`, `s.cloud.modelImport`; migration `159_cloud_models`, not
registered yet: until it is applied the import answers `503` `migration_pending`, and approvals and labels are checked
as before). See [cloud.md](cloud.md#cloud-model-backends-b-105).

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/admin/pools/:id/instances` `{kind: "bedrock", name, deploy, cloud: {accountId, region}, settings?}` | `pools:manage`. A Bedrock instance: the AWS account (one the caller may see) and the region whose endpoints it calls; no URL, socket, mutual TLS or token (`400`). `403` step `zone` when the region is off the account's allow-list or the pool's label ceiling is above the region's. The stored `url` is the regional runtime endpoint, for display; `settings.cloud` is `{provider: "aws", accountId, region}` and survives `PATCH /api/admin/instances/:id` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/model-import?region` | `cloud:read` and `models:manage`. What the account offers, nothing written: `{account: {id, name, provider}, models: [{id, name, kind: chat \| embedding \| agent \| other, flavour: bedrock \| azure \| digitalocean \| workers-ai, region, routesTo, available, reason, accessState: granted \| pending \| not_granted \| unknown \| available \| unavailable, ceiling: label \| null, catalogued: {modelId} \| null}]}` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/model-import` `{region?, ids?, instanceId?, label?}` | `cloud:read` and `models:manage`. Registers catalogue drafts (`format: server`, licence and terms recorded, a cloud entry) for the chosen listings (every chat and embedding model when `ids` is left out), held by `instanceId` or the instance serving the account (and region, for Bedrock). `201` when one was registered, else `200`: `{account, results: [{id, region, kind, outcome: registered \| updated \| unchanged \| skipped, reason, modelId, ceiling, label, accessState, instance}]}`. Skipped: not a chat or embedding model (an agent is a registry tool), no model access, a routing region off the allow-list or a global profile, already catalogued from elsewhere, a label above the pool's ceiling. `409` for an id the account does not offer, `400` for a region off the allow-list. Never approves. Audited `model.import.requested` (with `cloud`) per draft and `cloud.models.imported` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/model-entries?account` | `cloud:read` and `models:manage`. `{installed, entries: [{modelId, provider, accountId, region, externalId, flavour, offer: foundation \| inference_profile \| deployment \| model, routesTo, ceiling, terms: {name, url, notes}, accessState, importedAt, updatedAt}]}` for the accounts one may see |

`PATCH /api/admin/models/:id` with a higher `label` and `POST /api/admin/models/:id/lifecycle` `{to: "approved"}`
answer `403` step `zone` (with `ceiling`) for a cloud model above its entry's ceiling, or when a region it may route to
no longer admits its label. A Bedrock model call answers `403` the same way (as a failed turn) before anything is sent.

## Sprint 60 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): Azure OpenAI, DigitalOcean GenAI and Workers AI model servers (B-10502, B-10503, B-10509)

Cloud Chat Completions endpoints are `kind: openai` instances with a flavour (see
[cloud.md](cloud.md#azure-openai-digitalocean-genai-and-workers-ai-b-10502-b-10503-b-10509)). Migration
`160_cloud_model_servers` (not registered yet) adds `usage_records.neurons`, `cost_micros`, `currency` and `price_id`.

| Route | What |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/admin/pools/:id/instances` `{kind: openai, name, url?, deploy, token?, tokenRef?, cloud: {flavour: azure\|digitalocean\|workers-ai, accountId, region, apiVersion?, resourceId?, auth?: account\|key}}` | As before, plus `cloud`: the account must be the flavour's provider (`azure`, `digitalocean`, `cloudflare`; `400` otherwise) and the region must admit the pool's label ceiling (`403 step: zone`). `auth` defaults to `account` (Azure: an Entra token for the Cognitive Services scope; Workers AI: the account's token), or `key` when a token is given (Azure's API key, sent as `api-key`); DigitalOcean always takes a model access key (`400` without one). `url` is required for Azure (the resource endpoint) and defaults to `https://inference.do-ai.run` and `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<id>/ai`. `settings.cloud` of the instance records `{provider, accountId, region, flavour, auth, apiVersion?, resourceId?}`; an Azure instance's models are its deployments through ARM |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/agent-tools` `{agent, name, description?, keyRef, label?, ratePerHour?}` | `cloud:read` and `tools:manage`. `201 {id, kind: tool, name, version, impl: cloud-agent, status: draft, label, sideEffect: read, inputSchema: {prompt}, definition: {provider, accountId, agentUuid, agentName, endpoint, keyRef}, checks}`: a DigitalOcean GenAI agent (by uuid or name, from `/v2/gen-ai/agents`) as a draft registry tool, published like any other. `keyRef` is a `vault:` reference to the agent's access key the caller can read (`400` for a value, `403` when unreadable); `400` for an account that is not DigitalOcean's, `404` for an unknown agent, `409` for one not deployed or a pending or disabled account, `409` for a name and version already in the registry. Audited `registry.created` (`impl: cloud-agent`, the agent and its endpoint) |

Guardrail decisions gain provider blocks: an Azure content filter refusal is a `guard_decisions` row at `user-input`
(prompt) or `model-output` (completion) with action `block`, findings `provider:azure:<category>` and `meta.provider`,
`providerStage`, `categories`; the decision lists and statistics show it as any other.

## Sprint 60 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): GPU pools, node enrolment, warm-up and GPU quotas (B-10401, B-10404, B-10405)

Cloud GPU node groups and GPU VMs linked to gateway pools (`cloud/gpu-pools.ts`, `cloud/gpu-enrol.ts`; see
[cloud.md](cloud.md#gpu-pools-b-10401-b-10404-b-10405)). Migration `157_cloud_gpu_pools` is not registered yet: until
it is applied these routes answer `503` `migration_pending` and deployments with GPU pools apply as before. A plan
that creates or grows a GPU node group or VM past the account's GPU quota is not applicable; its `blockers` name the
quota, the requested and available numbers, the limit, what is in use and the increase link.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/gpu-pools` | `cloud:read`. `{pools: [link + {nodes: {enrolled, healthy}, bootToHealthy: {last, median, samples}}]}`: the GPU pool links of deployments the caller can see (`id, deploymentId, provider, poolName, resourceKey, kind: node_group\|vm, providerId, gatewayPoolId, gpu, instanceType, instanceTypes, zones, min, max, desired, priceHourly, currency, warmup, state: active\|pki_missing\|pending, stateDetail`) |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/gpu-pools/:id` | `cloud:read`. `{link, nodes, bootToHealthy, instances: [{id, name, url, state, health, node}], timings: [{node, instanceId, source, bootedAt, enrolledAt, healthyAt, seconds}], warmup: {source, mirror, models: [{name, ref, digest}], problem?}}`. Never a key |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/gpu-pools/:id/enrolments` `{node?, address?}` | `cloud:deploy`, a recent sign-in (and `platform:manage` for a platform deployment). `201 {token, url, mirror, expiresAt}`: a single-use enrolment token for a node set up by hand, bound to `node` and `address` when given, shown once (only its SHA-256 is kept). `409` `pool_not_active`. Audit `cloud.gpu.enrolment.minted` (never the token) |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/gpu-pools/:id/reconcile` | `cloud:deploy`. `202 {job}`: `cloud.gpu.reconcile` for the deployment (node groups: the DaemonSet and a token per node not yet enrolled; every link: boot timings) |
| `POST /cloud/gpu/v1/enrol` `{token, csr, address, node?, port?, bootedAt?}` | Outside `/api`: no session or CSRF; the single-use token is the credential. `201 {instance: {id, name, url}, certificate, chain, gateway: {caChain, clientSha1, clientSha256}, warmup}`: the node's server certificate (an IP name, exactly `address`, inside the deployment's network) and its instance in the pool (`deploy: cloud`). `401` `enrolment_refused` with `why`: `unknown`, `expired`, `replayed`, `node_mismatch`, `address_mismatch`, `address_outside`; `400` `bad_csr` or a malformed body; `409` `link_unavailable` (no active intermediate, the deployment gone). Audit `cloud.gpu.node.enrolled`, `cloud.gpu.node.refused` |

Audit, also: `cloud.gpu.pool.linked` (the follow-up of an applied deployment with GPU pools), `cloud.gpu.capacity.fallback`
(a create refused for capacity, tried with the next allowed type or zone).

## Sprint 60 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): scale-to-zero, autoscale, spot interruptions and idle GPU savings (B-10402, B-10403, B-10406, B-10605)

Cloud GPU pools scaled by the gateway (`cloud/autoscale.ts`, `s.cloud.autoscale`; see
[cloud.md](cloud.md#autoscale-spot-and-savings-b-10402-b-10403-b-10406-b-10605)). Migration `158_cloud_autoscale` is
not registered yet: until it is applied the admin routes below answer `503` `migration_pending` (the cards route
`{installed: false, cards: {}}`) and cloud pools are served exactly as before.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/pools/cloud` | `pools:manage`. `{installed, cards: {<poolId>: card}}`: one card per pool with a scale policy or a GPU pools link: `{poolId, policy, link, provider, region, size, deploymentId, resourceKey, desired, healthy, inflight, queued, priceHourly, currency, costPerHour, idle: {busy, lastLeaseAt, endsAt}, spot: {capacity, now, fallback, offered}, coldStart: {ms, samples, source}, savings, events, interruptions}` |
| `PUT /api/admin/pools/:id/autoscale` `{min, max, idleMinutes?, queueDepth?, maxColdWaitMinutes?, capacity?: on_demand\|spot, onDemandFallback?, deploymentId?, resourceKey?}` | `pools:manage` and `cloud:deploy` or `cloud:admin`. Sets the pool's scale policy (the node group comes from the GPU pools link, else `deploymentId` and `resourceKey`); answers the card. `422` `not_cloud` (no node group), `out_of_range` (above the spec's maximum), `spot_unavailable` (DigitalOcean). Audit `cloud.pool.autoscale.set` or `.updated` |
| `POST /api/admin/pools/:id/scale` `{desired, reason?}` | Same permissions. Sets the node group's desired size: `{outcome: applied\|unchanged, from, to, capacity, message, card}`. `422` `out_of_range` (outside min and max), `409` `budget_exceeded` (a scale-up past the account's hard stop; a scale-down always passes), `502` `provider_failed`. Audit `cloud.pool.scaled` (with the provider's request id), `cloud.pool.scale.refused`, `cloud.pool.scale.failed`, `cloud.pool.capacity.fallback` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/gpu-savings?month=YYYY-MM` | `finops:read` or `cloud:read`. `{month, pools: [{poolId, pool, month, provider, sku, hours, priceHourly, currency, priceSource, saving, intervals}]}`: node-hours avoided by idle scale-downs in the month (UTC, up to now) and `saving = hours × priceHourly` (the on-demand price) |
| `POST /cloud/v1/nodes/interruptions` `{kind: ec2_interruption\|ec2_rebalance\|azure_preempt, eventId?, reclaimAt?, detail?}` | Outside `/api`: no session or CSRF. The caller is the GPU node whose Exprsn-AI CA certificate (valid, not revoked, issued at enrolment) it presents, on this server's TLS socket or as the verified certificate a trusted proxy forwards (`PKI_CLIENT_CERT_HEADER`). `202 {id, duplicate, state: draining, deadlineAt}`; the drain goes on in the background. `401` `node_certificate`, `409` `not_cloud`, `422` `wrong_provider` (a DigitalOcean node, or an EC2 notice from Azure), `429` past 60 notices a minute per address (the enrolment, `POST /cloud/gpu/v1/enrol`, past 30 attempts in ten minutes). Audit `cloud.pool.interruption`, then `cloud.pool.drained` |

The gateway side has no route: a request on a pool with no healthy instance waits for the cold start (`chat.status`
`queued`, position 1) or takes the profile's fallback; with neither possible it fails with `503` and
`reason: cold_start_refused`.

## Sprint 61 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): model pricing, provider guardrails and residency (B-10505 to B-10508)

Per-model prices versioned by effective day (`cloud/model-prices.ts`), the Bedrock Guardrail as an extra layer, the
residency and egress check of every cloud model call and data-terms attestations under dual control
(`cloud/model-residency.ts`), and the Models screen's cloud card. Migration `163_cloud_model_prices` is not registered
yet: until it is applied the price and attestation writes answer `503` `migration_pending` and the reads answer the
price sheet. See [cloud.md](cloud.md#model-pricing-provider-guardrails-and-residency-b-10505-to-b-10508).

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/model-cards` | `cloud:read` and `models:manage`. Every cloud model (`format: server` on a cloud instance, or with a cloud entry) of an account the caller may see: `{cards: [{modelId, name, label, state, provider, flavour, account: {id, name}, region, routesTo, entry, instance: {id, name, kind, health} \| null, price: {current, metered, versions, pricedAs}, residency: {scope: regional \| cross-region \| global, cap, ceiling, regions: [{region, allowed, ceiling, reason}], attestation, pending}, guardrail: {layer, exprsnCheckpoints}, aiGateway: {gatewayId, accountId, cache, logs, confidential} \| null}]}` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/model-prices?provider&model` | `cloud:read`. `{installed, prices: [{id, provider, region, model, currency, basis: tokens \| neurons, inputPerMillion, outputPerMillion, cachedPerMillion, neuronsInput, neuronsOutput, neuronPrice, effectiveFrom, source: aws-price-list \| azure-retail-prices \| price-sheet \| manual, ref, unverified, priceId}]}`: the table's versions and the sheet's (unverified sheet entries flagged; they never price a record) |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/model-prices` `{provider, region?, model, currency?, basis?, inputPerMillion?, outputPerMillion?, cachedPerMillion?, neuronsInput?, neuronsOutput?, neuronPrice?, effectiveFrom, source?, note?}` | `finops:manage`. A price version by hand (`basis: tokens` needs `inputPerMillion`; `neurons` needs `neuronsInput` and `neuronPrice`); it prices records from `effectiveFrom` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) on, earlier records keep theirs; the same provider, region, model, currency and day replaces the version. Audited `cloud.model-price.set` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/model-prices/refresh` | `cloud:read` and `finops:manage`. Prices the account's cloud entries from the AWS Price List API (`AmazonBedrock`) or the Azure Retail Prices API (Azure OpenAI meters of the deployment's type): `{account, fetched, known, missing, failed: [{model, error}], skipped?}`; DigitalOcean and Cloudflare answer `skipped` (no price API). Audited `cloud.model-prices.refreshed` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/attestations?model&account` | `cloud:read`. `{installed, attestations: [{id, modelId, accountId, terms: {noTraining, retentionDays, abuseMonitoring, reference, note}, state: proposed \| active \| rejected \| revoked \| superseded, proposedBy, proposedAt, decidedBy, decidedAt, note}]}` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/model-entries/:modelId/attestations` `{noTraining: true, retentionDays, abuseMonitoring: off \| standard, reference, note?}` | `cloud:admin`. Proposes the account's data terms for a regional entry; nothing changes until a second cloud admin approves. `409` for a cross-region or global entry (it stays at `internal`) or while one is waiting. `201`. Audited `cloud.model.attestation.proposed` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/attestations/:id/approve` | `cloud:admin`, never the proposer (`403` reason `dual_control`). The entry's ceiling rises to `confidential` (bounded by its regions' ceilings, never `restricted`): `{attestation, ceiling}`. Audited `cloud.model.attestation.approved` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/attestations/:id/reject` `{note?}` | `cloud:admin`. Rejects (or, by the proposer, withdraws) a proposal. Audited `cloud.model.attestation.rejected` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/attestations/:id/revoke` | `cloud:admin`. The ceiling drops back to `internal` and the model's label with it: `{attestation, ceiling}`. Audited `cloud.model.attestation.revoked` |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/model-servers/:id/guardrail` `{guardrail: {id, version, mode: converse \| apply, enabled} \| null}` | `cloud:admin` and `models:manage`.
