A Bedrock instance's Bedrock Guardrail (an id or ARN; a version number or `DRAFT`), confirmed with GetGuardrail in the instance's region first (`409` `guardrail_unconfirmed` when Bedrock does not know it); `null` removes it. Exprsn-AI's checkpoints are not changed. `{instance, guardrail}`. Audited `cloud.model-server.guardrail.set` |

`GET /api/admin/usage/daily` gains `cloudCostMicros` per day (`{<currency>: micros}`, the sum of the day's records'
`cost_micros`) and `GET /api/admin/usage/summary` `costMicros` per row, once migration 160 added the cost columns;
`GET /api/admin/analytics/summary` rows gain `cloudCost` (`{<currency>: amount}`). A call on a cloud model server is
refused (`403` step `zone`, check `residency`, `ceiling`, `region` or `egress`) before anything is sent when the
request's label is above `internal` for a cross-region or global model, above the entry's ceiling, outside a routing
region's ceiling or residency, or when its pool's zone has no egress; a turn blocked by a Bedrock Guardrail fails and
is recorded as a guardrail decision (`provider:bedrock:<category>`).

## Sprint 61 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): Cloudflare billing and showback (B-10608, B-10604)

See [cloud.md](cloud.md#cloudflare-billing-and-showback-b-10608-b-10604). **Cloudflare billing** adds no route of its
own to fetch: `cloud.costs.ingest` now fetches active Cloudflare accounts whose last validation shows billing access
(one GraphQL Analytics request and the billing history, once a UTC day; "fetch now" as for the others), with row
`source` `cloudflare-analytics` (usage priced at the published rates, `estimated: true`) or `cloudflare-billing` (each
finished month reconciled with what was charged). Job `cloud.costs.neurons.check` (queued after each Cloudflare fetch)
compares Workers AI neurons per day and audits `cloud.costs.neurons.mismatch` when they differ by more than 1 %.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/costs/neurons?from&to` | `finops:read` or `cloud:read`; a Cloudflare account (else `400`). `{account, tolerance: 0.01, accountId, from, to, days: [{day, analytics, metered, difference, ok}], mismatches}`: the analytics' Workers AI neurons per day against the neurons metered on `usage_records` for the pools holding the account's Workers AI instances |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/showback?month=YYYY-MM&tenant=` | `finops:read`. The month's showback (default this month): `{month, computedAt, stored, rules: [{costType, name, basis, default}], currencies: [{currency, ingested, allocated, unallocated}], tenants: [{tenantId, name, currency, amount, workspaces: [{workspaceId \| null, name, amount, byType}]}], unallocated: [{currency, amount, byType}], lines: [{tenantId, workspaceId, currency, costType, method: tag \| pool \| tenant \| shared \| unallocated, amount}]}`. A platform admin (`platform:manage`) sees every tenant and the unallocated line (`tenant` narrows it); anyone else their own tenant only (`403` for another). Per currency, never converted. `503` `migration_pending` without migration 155 |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/showback/export?month&tenant&format=csv\|json` | `finops:read`. The same as a download (`showback-<month>.csv`: `month, tenant_id, tenant, workspace_id, workspace, currency, cost_type, method, amount`, then a `total` line per currency). Audited `cloud.showback.exported` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/showback/:month/compute` | `finops:manage` and `platform:manage`. Recomputes and stores the month: `{month, lines, stored}` (`stored: false` without migration 164). Audited `cloud.showback.computed` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/showback/rules` | `finops:read`. `{installed, rules: [{costType, name, basis, default}], bases}` |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/showback/rules` `{rules: {<costType>: <basis>}}` | `finops:manage` and `platform:manage`. Sets the platform's rules (cost types `gpu`, `model`, `compute`, `database`, `storage`, `network`, `other`; bases `gpu_time`, `tokens`, `model_cost`, `requests`, `storage`, `even`, `unallocated`) (a type set to its default keeps no row). `503` `migration_pending` without migration 164. Audited `cloud.showback.rules.updated` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/showback/settings?tenant=` | `finops:read`. `{tenantId, installed, statementLines}` for the caller's tenant (another one: `platform:manage`) |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/showback/settings?tenant=` `{statementLines}` | `finops:manage` or `tenant:manage`, in the caller's tenant (another one: `platform:manage`). Turns the showback lines on the tenant's B-13 statements on or off (default off). `503` without migration 164. Audited `cloud.showback.settings.updated` |

Statements (B-13): with a tenant's `statementLines` on, `GET /admin/billing/statements/:month`, `.../preview` and the
JSON export carry `showback: {note, month, lines: [{workspaceId, workspace, costType, description, amount, currency}],
totals: {<currency>: amount}}`, and the CSV export ends with a `showback` section. These lines are informational: not in
`totalMicros`, not pushed to Stripe. With the setting off (the default) or migration 164 missing, statements answer
exactly as before.

Job `cloud.showback.compute` (daily once ingested costs exist, as the platform tenant; `{month}` for one month)
recomputes and stores this month and the last.


## Sprint 61 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): the Cloudflare front door (B-10901 to B-10904)

See [cloud.md](cloud.md#cloudflare-front-door-b-10901-to-b-10904). Migration `161_cloud_edge` (not registered yet):
without it every route below except `ranges` answers `503` `migration_pending`. No route answers a tunnel token (only
its `vault:` reference) or an identity provider's secret. A front door's account must be a platform Cloudflare
account; creating, applying and setting up Access also need `platform:manage`.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/edge` | `cloud:read`. `{edges: [{id, name, accountId, deploymentId, hostname, zone, plan, origin, waf, access, state: draft \| applied \| failed, switchedFrom: acme \| null, tunnelId, tokenRef, accessAud, steps, lastError, labelCap: confidential, ...}], ranges: {asOf, source}, accessExclusions: [{path, why, required}]}` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/edge` `{name, accountId, deploymentId?, hostname, zone, plan?: free \| pro \| business \| enterprise, origin: {kind: tunnel, service} \| {kind: public, address, port?}, waf?: {enabled, adminCidrs}}` | `cloud:admin`, a recent sign-in. → `201 {edge}`. `409` for a name outside the zone, a duplicate name or hostname, a non-Cloudflare or tenant account, or a `restricted` deployment (open decision 5). Audited `cloud.edge.created` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/edge/ranges?accountId=` | `cloud:read`. `{asOf, source, shipped}`; with an account also `{live, added, removed}` from Cloudflare's `GET /client/v4/ips` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/edge/:id` | `cloud:read`. `{edge, waf: {plan, phases, mirrored, notes} \| null, accessExclusions, ranges}` |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/edge/:id/apply` | `cloud:deploy`, a recent sign-in. Edge certificate, SSL Full (strict), the origin's certificate (public origin), the tunnel (created or found by name, its token into the vault, its ingress), DNS switched with no gap, the WAF. → `{edge}` with `steps`. `409` `edge_certificate_pending` or `origin_certificate` (nothing changed), `409`/`502` `edge_apply_failed` with `step` and `steps`. Audited `cloud.edge.applied` or `cloud.edge.apply.failed` |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/edge/:id/access` `{scope: admin \| host, teamDomain, idp: {kind: exprsn, clientId, clientSecret} \| {kind: cloudflare, identityProviderId}, allowedEmails?, allowedDomains?, sessionDuration?}` | `cloud:admin`, a recent sign-in. Makes the Access identity provider (Exprsn-AI's OIDC client, checked: active, confidential, the team's callback, `openid` and `email`, the given secret) and applications (scope `admin`: `/api/admin` and `/admin`; `host`: the name plus a bypass application for the exclusions). → `{edge, aud, settings}`. `409` for `exprsn` with `host`, or for a cloud deployment. Audited `cloud.edge.access` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/edge/:id/install/:target` | `cloud:read`; `target` `helm`, `systemd` or `compose` (else `400`). What runs `cloudflared` beside the app: `{image, ingress, values \| unit \| file, env, steps, inboundPorts: []}`. `409` for a public origin |

With `CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS_AUD` set, a path `CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS_SCOPE` protects answers `403` `access_required` without a
valid `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion`; the session is still required. CLI: `exprsn-ai cloud:tunnel-token --edge <name>
--out <file>` (a new 0600 file; audited `cloud.edge.token.written`).

## Sprint 61 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): Cloudflare app tier, R2, D1 and AI Gateway (B-10905 to B-10908)

See [cloud.md](cloud.md#cloudflare-app-tier-r2-d1-and-ai-gateway-b-10905-to-b-10908). No migration.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/validate-spec`, `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments` | As before; `compute.shape` may be `cloudflare` (the hybrid app tier, with `compute.cloudflare: {redisUrlRef?, r2Jurisdiction?: auto \| default \| eu \| fedramp, databaseVia?: tunnel \| direct}`). A Cloudflare spec without Redis on another provider (`compute.cloudflare.redisUrlRef` or `data.redisUrlRef`), without a Cloudflare front door, with GPU pools, without an image by digest or with cloud KMS keys has problems with check `app_tier` (`422 invalid_spec`). The answers carry `appTier: {accountId, resources, notes}` (the Worker, the container, Hyperdrive and the R2 bucket on the front door's account); creating also makes the app tier's own deployment on the Cloudflare account (`<name>-edge`) and returns `appTier: {deployment, plan}`. The planner refuses an app tier graph without Redis on another provider or without Hyperdrive, with that reason, and any secret among the Worker's plain settings |
| `PUT /api/admin/instances/:id/ai-gateway` `{accountId, gatewayId, cache?, cacheTtl?, logs?, confidential?: {cache?, logs?}, customProvider?}` | `pools:manage` and `cloud:read`. Puts Cloudflare AI Gateway in front of a cloud model instance (Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, DigitalOcean GenAI or Workers AI): `accountId` is a Cloudflare cloud account the caller can see. → `{instance, aiGateway, policy: {public, internal, confidential, restricted}}`, each `{cache, logs}`: up to `internal` as set (both on by default), `confidential` off unless set, `restricted` never. `409` for an instance that is not a cloud one or an unusable account. Audited `instance.ai_gateway.set` |
| `DELETE /api/admin/instances/:id/ai-gateway` | `pools:manage`. → `204`; calls go straight to the provider again. Audited `instance.ai_gateway.removed` |
| `PUT /api/admin/cloud/accounts/:id/ai-gateways/:gateway` `{rateLimit?: {limit, intervalSeconds, technique?: fixed \| sliding} \| null, cacheTtl?, logs?, authentication?}` | `cloud:admin`. Creates (`201`) or updates (`200`) the gateway on the Cloudflare account: rate limits, the default cache TTL (0), logs (off by default; requests turn them on for what may be logged) and authentication (on). `409` for a non-Cloudflare account; `409`/`502` when Cloudflare refuses. Audited `cloud.ai_gateway.created` or `cloud.ai_gateway.updated` |

Connections: the engine `cloudflare-d1` (`GET /api/admin/connections/engines`) registers like any SQL engine: the
endpoint `https://api.cloudflare.com`, the account is the Cloudflare account id, the database the D1 database id, the
secret an API token. A write, `PRAGMA`, `ATTACH` or schema change answers `422` (`Write refused` or `DDL refused`) and
nothing is sent to Cloudflare.

## Sprint 62 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): spend anomalies and the Cloud spend screen (B-10606, B-10607)

See [cloud.md](cloud.md#anomalies-and-the-cloud-spend-screen-b-10606-b-10607). Migration `166_cloud_anomalies` (not
registered yet): without it the anomaly routes answer `503` `migration_pending`, and nothing is detected. Without
migration 155 every route below answers `503` `migration_pending`. Reads see only the accounts the caller may see.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/spend?month=YYYY-MM` | `finops:read` or `cloud:read`. The Cloud spend screen's overview of a month (default this month): `{month, accounts: [{id, name, provider, scope}], daily: [{day, provider, currency, amount}], totals: [{provider, currency, amount, estimated}], tokens: [{model, provider, profileId, profile, currency, inputTokens, outputTokens, neurons, cost, calls}], savings: [{provider, currency, hours, saving}], anomaliesOpen}`. Amounts per currency, never converted. `tokens` are the cloud model calls priced at metering (B-10505) of the caller's tenant (every tenant for `platform:manage`); `savings` the idle GPU hours avoided by scale-to-zero (B-10605); `anomaliesOpen` is null without migration 166 |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/anomalies?state=open\|acknowledged&account&from&to&limit` | `finops:read` or `cloud:read`. `{anomalies: [{id, account: {id, name, provider}, accountId, tenantId, provider, day, service, currency, actual, baseline, mad, score, ratio, increasePct, historyDays, contributors: [{dimension: service \| deployment \| region \| tag, key, name, actual, baseline, extra}], top: {deployment, region, tag}, state, suppressedBy, acknowledgedBy, acknowledgedAt, note, auditId, detectedAt}]}`, newest day first (at most `limit`, default 200, up to 500) |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/anomalies/:id` | `finops:read` or `cloud:read`. One anomaly as above; `404` for one on an account the caller cannot see |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/anomalies/:id/acknowledge` `{note?}` | `finops:manage` (a platform account also `platform:manage`). Marks an open anomaly acknowledged with the note (at most 500 characters): an anomaly of the same account and service in the next 3 days is stored acknowledged without a notice (`suppressedBy`). `409` `anomaly_acknowledged` when it is already. Audited `cloud.anomaly.acknowledged` |

Job `cloud.anomalies.detect` (`{accountId}`, queued after every successful `cloud.costs.ingest`; daily for every account
with ingested costs, as the platform tenant) checks the last 3 ingested days of the account per service and currency
against the 14 days before each (median and median absolute deviation; the rule is in cloud.md). A new anomaly is the
audit event `cloud.anomaly.detected` (every webhook subscribed to `cloud.*`, `cloud.anomaly.*` or `*` receives it; its
target names the top deployment) and a notice of kind `cloud.anomaly` (Administration) to the tenant's FinOps readers
and cloud admins; a repeat inside an acknowledgement's quiet days is audited `cloud.anomaly.suppressed` instead. Metrics
`exprsn_cloud_anomalies_total{provider}` and `exprsn_cloud_anomalies_open{provider}`; alert `ExprsnCloudSpendAnomaly`.

## Sprint 62 (1.9.99-final, Unreleased): on-prem front doors and the change trail (B-10209, B-10703)

See [cloud.md](cloud.md#on-prem-front-doors-b-10209) and [cloud.md](cloud.md#change-trail-b-10703). Migration
`165_cloud_change_trail` (not registered yet): without it drift runs as before, nothing is looked up, and each finding
answers `changedBy: null` with `trail.state: unavailable`. The on-prem registration needs no migration of its own.

| Method and path | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/validate-spec` `{kind: onprem, name, description?, label?, install: {kind: compose \| baremetal \| helm, service?, version?}, compute?: {shape: none}, frontDoor: {kind: cloudflare, accountId, hostname, zone, plan?, waf?: {enabled?, adminCidrs?}}}` | The on-prem dry run; calls no provider: `{valid, kind: onprem, problems, unavailable: [], resources: [] (no compute), firewalls: [], notes, frontDoor: {accountId, resources: [tunnel, dns_record], planned: false, note}, appTier: null, estimate: null, origin, attach: {id, name, state} \| null}`. `origin` is `install.service`, else `http://app:8080` (compose), `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (baremetal) or `http://exprsn-ai.exprsn-ai.svc:80` (helm); `attach` names a front door for the name made earlier without a deployment, which registration attaches |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments` (the same body) | `cloud:deploy`, `platform:manage` and, for an on-prem install, `cloud:admin` (it creates the front door); recent sign-in. `201 {kind: onprem, deployment, plan, firewalls: [], unavailable: [], notes, frontDoor, edge, install}`: the deployment on the Cloudflare account (`region: global`, `kind: onprem`, its spec with `compute: {shape: none}`), a plan with no step, the front door (`edge`, a tunnel origin at `origin`) and what runs `cloudflared` beside the install (`install`, as `GET /api/admin/cloud/edge/:id/install/:target`). Nothing is called on any cloud. Refused before anything exists: `403` step `zone` for the label above `confidential` or a placement check of the Cloudflare account, else `422` `invalid_spec` with `problems` (`front_door` for a name outside its zone or a front door already there, `permission` for an account not validated for the front door, `name`). Audited `cloud.deployment.created`, `cloud.deployment.spec` (`kind: onprem`, `shape: none`, the install kind), `cloud.plan.created`, `cloud.edge.created` (or `cloud.edge.attached`) |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/edge/:id/apply` | As before; for an on-prem deployment's front door, the tunnel and the proxied record then join its graph (`tunnel`, `dns-app`, with their provider ids), and the deployment is `applied` with `endpoints.publicUrl`. Audited `cloud.deployment.updated` (`actor.service: cloud.edge`) |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments?accountId=&state=&kind=cloud\|onprem` | As before; every deployment carries `kind: cloud \| onprem` |
| `GET /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/drift?state=` | As before; each finding also carries `changedBy: {principal, principalType, at, action, source, eventId, sourceIp, byExprsn} \| null` and `trail: {state: pending \| found \| not_found \| unsupported \| error \| unavailable, provider, attempts, window: {from, to} \| null, events: [{at, principal, principalType, action, source, eventId, sourceIp, byExprsn}] (up to five), checkedAt, error}`, from the cache the drift run fills; this read calls nothing |
| `POST /api/admin/cloud/deployments/:id/drift/check` | As before; after recording, the open findings without a trail yet are looked up (CloudTrail `LookupEvents`, the Azure Activity Log, Cloudflare audit logs; at most ten per run, the 24 hours before each finding's first sighting, at most four times each over six hours). A failed lookup is the finding's `trail.state: error`, never the run's failure |

Permissions the accounts' credentials need (the setup helper renders them): AWS `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` in the
`deploy` feature, Azure `Microsoft.Insights/eventtypes/values/read` in `deploy` (and the custom role), Cloudflare
"Account Settings Read" in `frontdoor`.

## 2.0.x: Docs portal

Documentation sites over knowledge bases (`server/src/docs/`, console `#/docs`). A site lists knowledge bases in order;
its pages are their published references (Markdown with slugs, versions and a page tree), and with `library` the
bases' other documents grouped by category. Reading needs `knowledge:read`, and every read asks the knowledge services
whether the reader may see the base, the reference (label, publication) or the document (label, row access): a base
the reader cannot see is left out of the site, and a site with none of its bases readable is a `404`. Curating sites
needs `docs:manage` (Knowledge curator) and read access to each base named. Audited `docs.site.created`, `.updated`,
`.removed`.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/docs/sites` | The sites with a base the caller can read: `[{id, slug, title, description, bases: [{id, name, label}], home: {kbId, slug} \| null, library, version, updatedAt, canManage}]` (only readable bases are listed) |
| `POST /api/docs/sites` `{slug, title, description?, kbIds, home?, library?}` | `docs:manage`. Creates a site (`201`); `409` for a taken slug, a base listed twice, or a home page that is not a reference of one of the bases; `404` for a base the curator cannot read |
| `PATCH /api/docs/sites/:id` | `docs:manage`. Any of the same fields; a home page outside the bases is dropped |
| `DELETE /api/docs/sites/:id` | `docs:manage`. `204` |
| `GET /api/docs/sites/:site/nav` | `{site, sections: [{kb, duties, pages: [{id, slug, title, parentId, position, children, state, version, updatedAt}], library: {documents, categories: [{path, depth, documents}]} \| null}]}`; pages as `knowledge/tree.ts` gives them (drafts only for editors and approvers) |
| `GET /api/docs/sites/:site/page?kb&slug&version?` | One reference rendered: `{page: {id, kbId, kb, slug, title, version, current, label, state, updatedAt, approvedAt, approvedBy}, html, toc: [{level, id, text}], breadcrumbs, children, links, backlinks, versions, canEdit}`. `html` is rendered on the server from the parsed Markdown with every piece of text escaped (HTML in a page stays text; links only http, https and mailto), headings carry the `toc` ids, front matter is left out, and `[[slug]]`, `[[slug\|text]]`, `[[slug#part]]` and bare-slug links become `#/docs?site=…&kb=…&page=…` links marked `data-docs-missing` when the target is not a page the reader can open. `version` reads an earlier published version |
| `GET /api/docs/sites/:site/library?kb&category?&q?&limit?` | The base's documents that are not references, newest first, in a category or matching a name: `{documents: [{id, name, title, categories, label, updatedAt, source}]}`; `404` when the site has no Library |
| `GET /api/docs/sites/:site/document/:doc?from?` | A library document's extracted text as a page: `{doc, html, toc, next}` (sections passed through the `context` guardrail as every read is; `next` continues) |
| `GET /api/docs/sites/:site/search?q` | Knowledge search over the site's readable bases: `{hits: [{kind: page \| document, kbId, slug?, docId?, title, heading, snippet}]}`; a hit on a reference's document points at the page |
